book.foreword: This book was made by the Takodachis of the Tentacult Temple Fan Server as a thank-you and congratulatory gift to Ina and everyone involved in the release of the Abyssal Hymn MV. It is also a way to share our ideas, theories, and explanations of the Ina lore with all Takos and anyone else interested in the amazing work Ninomae Ina'nis put into this story. The book is divided into three sections. The first describes and explains the elements, motifs, themes, and more of the MV, along with other important details of the Ina lore. The second describes the meanings of the Re:Vision album and other related songs to showcase the story behind it all. The third showcases standalone theories about the Ina lore by fellow Takodachi theorycrafters. As explained below, this book is entirely a fan-made work. Some of what is stated here is theory, fun thoughts, and other bits of information that may or may not align with what Ina explains or confirms in the future, or has already confirmed. She said we got all the clues, so this is our best shot at putting together all the puzzle pieces! Hope you all enjoy! Happy Birthday, Takodachis!
book.disclaimer: WORD OF CAUTION: Everything within these pages is merely theory and analysis from a fellow takodachi, not confirmed lore unless Ina says so herself. A deep dive into imagery, themes, and pieces that *may* play a role in her puzzle. What you choose to use and how you connect it, is up to you.

body.text: For we brought nothing into this world, and can take nothing out of it.

Ninomae Ina’nis, commonly known as Ina, is the priestess of the Ancient Ones, eldritch beings and gods beyond human comprehension, who greatly resemble and take inspiration from lovecraftian mythos. Wearing a cute smile and singing with a soothing voice, it can be hard to imagine her as the herald of the deep.

But look closer, and you will see it behind her like a shadow, following her wherever she goes. Tentacles that are dolled up in paint, a halo she calls an onion ring, and ink on all her paperwork that leaves you wondering “wait, how old?”
Indeed, the background of Ninomae Ina’nis is a mystery.
But,

beginning in 2021 with the release of her first single, Violet, that all began to change. Slowly, year after year, Ina would delight and live in the minds of her Takodachis (Octopus friends that follow her) with various hints and glimpses into an evolving and expanding story, finally culminating in RE:Vision, Ina’s first EP, within it containing the story behind the one known as Ninomae Ina’nis.

As of the time I am (was) typing this, the full story still remains debated, with many different takes and ideas, caught between timeloops and multiple points of view, as we all await for the release of Abyssal Hymn’s Music Video, a fully animated music video for the climax of her universe that she has dubbed, “The Inaverse”, which will no doubt answer many questions. Indeed, within only 10 seconds of its nearly 4 minute runtime, we already got many new and exciting views, and now all that’s left is to wait, ponder, and seek to understand a person beyond mortal comprehension.

Thus, for all fans, new and old, join us here as we embark on a journey that follows Ina’s storytelling and creative vision over the years! Whether this is your first time discovering her, a regular theorist, or someone simply wanting to see her work again, all are welcome to explore the tale she has woven before us.
**Let us dive into the world of the Inaverse, TOGETHER!**
Primary and secondary sources

Not all hints are as apparent as others, and for that reason, I am leading with the preface that throughout some of this, I will be getting into some theoretical analysis. However, I only do this if I can build a connection with other repeated themes, either as an influence on Ina's story, or, if there are direct connections.
For this reason, original songs, artwork, and content produced by Ina will be the primary sources to rely on.

However, a great deal of her ideas began life elsewhere and were developed over time, and may have been explored before in other forms. For that reason, we will also be taking looks into some covers, 3D lives, and ESPECIALLY her solo-concert. Even though many of the performances are covers of songs not directly connected to her story, their themes and staging may help direct us, and have several major hints about the nature of the Inaverse as a whole.
Take them all with a grain of caution, as they all have their own already existing meanings and stories, but, they are more than worthy of a closer look.
General Themes

Before we can truly expand into each entry, let’s take a moment to dive into some of the general themes that appear across Ina’s various works. These are all thematically present within Ina from the very start, and are continuously explored in new ways as her story expands, each new release giving more hints into her lore, while weaving these throughout new elements.
THE ANCIENT ONES

Right from the beginning, no connection is as immediately striking as Ina’s connection to the Ancient Ones, and with it, heavy inspiration from Lovecraftian Mythos. An expansive universe in its own right, the lore from Ina’s identity is inspired from revolves around cults to gods and powers beyond human comprehension, deriving much of their intrigue from the unknown in the universe and the anxieties of the mind.

In a similar fashion, Ina’s own backstory from the very beginning is shrouded in mystique. She claims to be a normal girl, regardless of tentacles and extra appendages. She isn’t a goddess of a cult, yet those who flock to her are called the tentacult. Her age is uncertain, constantly covered in black ink. Deriving these connections, we can make a few connections…

Much of Ina’s background lore and direction is derived from Cthulhu, Azathoth, and other gods of Lovecraftian mythos, and we can get a glimpse of her future work with some familiarity of the subject, as the Ancient Ones, whether directly implied to be, or merely inspired, take great inspiration from these fictional beings.
AO-Chan

The nickname given to Ina’s book/tome, which appears to be a direct reference to (and is said verbatim in [Temari]) the Necronomicon. In Lovecraft mythos, the Necronomicon, also known as the Book of the Dead, is a book of forbidden knowledge, and within the Inaverse, contains the ability to perform magic and spells, and appear to act as a way for Ina to directly communicate with The Ancient Ones.
Takodachis

Literally meaning “Octopus friends”, takodachis are the adorable little blobs that follow Ina around. Heavily resembling dumbo octopuses, they act as both a mascot and a representation of her fans, who are collectively known as the Tentacult. However, Ina assures everyone, that just as she is a normal girl, we are also not a cult.
In spite of that though, the cthulhu inspiration only becomes more intense here, the chimera-like girl surrounded by octopi followers who worship the very ground she stands upon.

In spite of their cute appearance, the origins of the takos themselves, are, unspecified. Ina states that they come from, or are made of void, but what that actually means at first, is left for the audience to decide.
But as time went on, just as Ina evolved, so did the takodachis, and this will be far from our last time discussing these cute little blobs…
Time, and the Ina’s of Past, Present, and Future, and one other.

Since the early days of Hololive EN, Ina has long made jokes about past and future Ina. Future Ina, always taking the brunt of work left today, Past Ina always hurting the present with her decisions. Though mostly comedic, they also reflect her enjoyment of playing with time, warping it, treating the Ina that was and the Ina to be like separate individuals rather than just herself. This would later expand with each new Ina outfit and model introduced, treating many of them like separate people.
With each new entry however, time has become an increasingly major element, suggesting a story of several different timelines or points in time coming together at the end.
The Deep Blue Sea

Already by being a stand in for the eldritch, it should come as no surprise she’s connected with the deep sea, the oceanic depths, the [ABYSS]. The ocean itself, with unpredictable currents and still able to overthrow the strongest of mankind today, is an awe inspiring entity, one that drives equal parts fear and intrigue. It’s blue surface stretching to the very horizon, reflects the sky and heavens above, and it is not uncommon for the ocean to represent the strength and breadth of thoughts and feelings. However, below the surface, within the abyss, lies a world more alien to us today than the stars themselves. Thus, the depths of the ocean can also represent the mystery of an individual, the uncertainty and curiosity upon its beholder. Likewise, the abyss can also represent the depths of one’s true heart and nature, and all the secrets they hide within.
Space, the Moon, and Stars

It wouldn’t be eldritch horror and fantasy without the deep and entrancing void of the heavens themselves. From the very start, Ina’s identity is covered with multiple references to stars and celestial bodies, and will only become deeper and richer with each new entry. The fantastic cosmos have long since dominated mankind's curiosity, and are a popular source for both inspiration and wonder. Though frightening in the scale that dwarfs us, they also inspire us to seek greater heights, and represent a realm elevated beyond the human experience. Fantasies, grandeur, and magic, everything and anything in a world beyond our grasp, living in our wildest dreams.
Colors

Starting with her first song, Violet, many of her following songs would be associated with different colors, culminating in “A rainbow of colors, an array for Abyssal Hymn.”
These include:
Violet - Violet
Meconopsis - Blue
Temari - Red
TakoTakover - Purple
Takodachi no Uta - Black and White
Abyssal Hymn - Rainbow
With each color introduced in Ina’s story, we can look to build connections between different characters and attempt to interpret their role in the story.
Reflections, Duality, Perspective

Throughout the Inaverse, there are numerous connections to reflections. Eyes, mirrors, the surfaces of water, reflections can both reveal things previously unseen, but also bring wisdom and awareness to the one within it. With each new entry, this becomes more complex and deep, as hints at multiple perspectives and an increasingly dualistic nature, lead us to question both who is speaking, and who is being spoken to…
Love

The last, but most important element to Ina’s lore, is one that will purvey every subsequent entry to come, and deserves to be mentioned ahead of time. Across Ina’s story, the one theme which connects everything together, is love. An emotion deeper than the darkest oceans, more vast than the universe, and with the ability to drive people beyond the realms of sanity. Yes, as Ina’s story expands, you will find love everywhere. Lurking in the dark. Watching from above.
Following through time…
A power so monstrous, that even the Ancient One’s could never control it.
Love is what completes Ina and her story.
And love is where it all begins.
Hatred Stirs up dissension, but love covers all wrongs

The first of Ina’s original songs and her first solo release altogether, debuting months before her first cover, is the charming and contemplative Violet. Born at a time when Ina was just beginning to develop her story and lore, Violet would go on to shape much of her later direction. Centered around Ina as she wanders through a shallow sea, she sings about how desperately she misses someone, yet questions if she can to these past memories and dreams she holds precious. All the while, we see glimpses of [Past Ina], living in a grey world, holding a Temari Ball, a far cry from her current form as Violet Ina. We also get our first ever glimpse of [The Friend], given only a blank face, Ina only able to remember her words.

Over the course of the song, Ina’s memories of the past begin to fade as she wavers on her decision, until all that is left is a void where her past was, and stars emanating from within.
With a smile on her face, Ina finds her inner strength, and dives back into the depths, reaching her hand to one that likely belongs to [The Friend].

A song about growth and patience, Violet gives Ina the time and space to process her emotions. All the while, Love drives her forward, giving her the strength to face the fears lurking in her past, and the drive to save the friend she desperately misses.

Though Violet was years away from RE:Vision and Temari, where she began to finalize the story of Ninomae Ina’nis, it would go on to influence many future works. From the mysterious Friend appearing in future projects again [See: The void and beyond] and the first reveals of the Ninomae Family, and more insight into Past Ina, Violet marks the foundation of everything to follow.
The Friend

"Who's the boy in the MV?" "It's not a boy! It's a friend of mine... I think. There was a friend I had when I was little, she disappeared without saying anything. The island that Ina, me, lives on, is isolated, so we don't get many people coming in and out. So Ina was takobocchi. That's all I'm giving you for now."

The friend plays an interesting role within Ina’s narrative. Though at first sharing many similarities and connections with the Apostate of the Ancient Ones, Tsukumo Sana, including appearing in a special teaser before their first collab, their identity would ultimately shift over time, with heavy hints to [The Wahtcher], a strange being in another realm who watches over Ina.

The two appear to have a close history together, Ina having met them while she was a young girl on the island [Past Ina], and following Violet’s lyrics, appear to have opened Ina’s eyes to a larger world.

Further clues within the MV and future song, [Temari], heavily suggest that the friend and Ina would eventually fight, and that The friend became [The second priestess] in her place, leaving Ina alone. Lyrics throughout the MV also give some insight into Ina and her friend’s predicament.

“Even with all the handholding and tight embraces, The sky will still turn red and the leaves will still fall” indicates an oncoming change that cannot be prevented, and reveals Ina has made peace with the future to come. Past Ina mirrors a similar sentiment, stating “Even if I let you hold my hand and lead me forever, the sky would still well and the rain would still fall”, suggesting that no matter how much anyone else tries to protect her, the coming storm is inevitable. Regardless of what the friend does, they cannot protect Ina from her destiny, even if it means taking on Ina’s priestess duties and vanishing. As unfortunately for Ina’s friend, she has become important to Ina’s happiness, and one day, Ina will no doubt return for them.
"Past Ina"

One of the more difficult to decipher figures in Violet is a mysterious short-haired girl, one that in her stream after Violet released, Ina called Past Ina. Within her hands she holds the glowing tome of AO-chan, and overall, her expression is more serious, her eyes void of any light, the only remaining detail a pair of dark rings. The colors also appear muted, drab and gray, a reflection of her dreamless, colorless future, living only to fulfill her priestess duties. Another detail that will strike most viewers nowadays is her resemblance to the [Temari “Ina”], a figure that is implied to be her long lost friend she has been searching for, one that Ina at numerous points teases is not Ina.
If both statements are true, then this image of Ina is our first ever look at [The first priestess]. Contrasting Violet Ina to Past Ina, the difference could not be any more stark, and gives the impression that her friend allowed her a glimpse into a bigger, more colorful world, and with her gone, now Ina lies at a crossroads. Does she run away? Does she return to her duties? Or, does she try and find the friend again, risking her own safety to bring back the person that brought color to her life.
Violet (Flower)

“If you see the design of the Violet Ina, it’s closer to the flower. I really like the flower as well… hehehehehe.”
“Does the flower have any meaning? Is it spoilers I don’t know-”

Violet's can represent modesty, faithfulness, and spirituality,
along with inner growth. Violet's also have a history with romantic
connections, both for love between women, and also for enduring
love. All parts seem to match Violet's Ina as both modest, and also
seeking a sort of spiritual wisdom, with her meditating on a difficult decision. But no matter how difficult and murky the depths of the future look, Love, enduring and faithful, compels Ina to reach her hand back one more time, and plunge into the deep to reunite with the other…
Colors and the lack thereof

Throughout Violet's MV, we see multiple pointswhere we switch between colors and no colors, a monochrome world. Given how in later performances, such as **Neverland Paradox** and **Drawn two Dawn**, how Ina described her past as being colorless, we can recognize these scenes to be a glimpse into the life of Past Ina. Living in a world devoid of all colors, it suggests Past Ina only lived to fulfill her role as priestess of the ancient Ones.
However, it's a far cry from who she is by Violet. Swathed in violet, an elusive color for much of history, imbues Ina with mysterious qualities, caught within the tides of something greater...
Design

Violet loosely wears a yellow raincoat with a blue interior filled with white dots. Beneath this layer she wears a white strap dress, and she overall tends to wear it loosely. Finally, rather than letting her hair down, she has it tied up in a ponytail, and is adorned with several of the violet flowers. The loose yellow raincoat suggests Violet Ina is going through a metamorphosis, learning to set aside the protective layers that slow her down, and embrace her vulnerability. The color choices merge the sun and the rain, showing them not as opposites, but as two sides of the same coin. Overall, while Violet emphasizes her innocence and youth a great deal, it also highlights her own self-actualization and self acceptance, both the joy and the tears.
The Broken Pencil

The image of a Broken pencil, split in half with a little chunk in between, works as a striking symbol within Violet, and later, [Temari]. Given that Ina is an artist, yet Past Ina lives in a gray reality, it suggests that the person who left Ina was able to introduce them to new joys, and brought color into Past Ina’s life. However, the broken pencil with the colorless backdrop shows that with her friend gone, the color she was gifted has vanished, her world now even emptier because she cannot replace the joy she was given.
Moon
The moon makes her grand appearance at multiple points in Violet, both visually and in the lyrics.
“The waxing moon incites my wanderlust” associates the growing light side of the moon with excitement and fantasy, the desire to dream and create in the world.
“The waning moon vanishes into the dark” precedes the final chorus, and hints that the source and drive of that joy is threatening to vanish, before Ina proceeds to dive into the depths.

The moon also appears with all [8] different phases during the part after chorus 1, shifting between them as Ina sings in the original language made by Lumina-san. As these moons appear, so do two overlapping circles, along with a second pair within, together forming the number 8. Finally, a third white circle lays over top between the two, forming in between.
Original Language

After chorus 1, Ina begins to sing several words as she prays on the ground, and with each word, another phase of the moon appears over her head, nestled within the figure 8. Ina would state in the following stream that this is actually an original language made by Lumina, and translates to:
**“Scars, fireflies, empty, music, sound, childhood.“**

Together, these lyrics offer a glimpse into past Ina’s childhood, displaying a mixture of fantasy and painful memories, suggesting both Ina and her friend struggled with living, and in past Ina’s case, as the priestess with her duties.
The Ocean, Mist, and Train Tracks
Throughout Violet, Ina walks through a shallow sea within a vast ocean, striding across the raised tracks just below the surface, leading her into the distance.

In the first shot, mist surrounds Ina, an element that appears in later songs, and is intertwined with dreams, showcasing Violet is not so much just following Ina, but showing her state of mind. Confused and wandering, her memories clouded to her, Ina sticks to the train tracks as the only surface she can see, limiting her choices. This can also be a reflection of Ina’s inner turmoil, believing that no matter what is done, her fate will ultimately lead her to the same place.

However, before the second chorus, the mist clears, and reveals the ocean to in fact be a sea reflecting the stars above, and shows how vast and deep the ocean is that surrounds her. Enchanting, dangerous, and impossible to grasp, reflecting the well of unspoken thoughts and feelings below the surface, made even more imposing and wondrous as it reflects the impossibly large heavens above. As the song concludes, Ina finds her bravery to face those depths, and leaps into the water.
Perspective

“Has Ina always had flaps?”
“Maybe, maybe not, it depends on perspective!”
Rather than a single point of view, Ina more or less directly teases that Violet, and therefore the rest of the Inaverse, features more than one perspective.

This has many, many ramifications, especially in the future, but for now, states that Violet is more than just one story, and involves other people. This in particular, draws back attention to her missing friend, the girl who was with her on the island, who one day vanished...
A birthday, a wanderer, a watcher, and a ghost.
The early evolution of the Inaverse.

In between Ina’s original releases, nearly 3 years would pass, but that didn’t mean Ina’s storytelling stopped. Cryptic messages during the interim, strange visitors to stream, and appearances in covers would give more insight to the thoughts and ideas within her head. Though years before she finalized her story, this period would introduce many of its elements, and leave numerous ties to her future work…

And none were as ominous as her October 31st tweet, a drawn image of a girl in a white sleeveless high-neck dress and dark long hair (See: Temari[The first Priestess]) with the image torn to hide her face, shadow and ink blotting her image. Standing before a room without color, she cradles a tako made of the void-
The First Takodachi

-and wishes it a happy birthday. All the while a single white crease, or thread crosses right over her heart (See: Temari[Threads]). All the while, poor thing clings to her back, light only appearing from its eyes, almost appearing as if it is crying.
A journey like a dream

Ina's first cover, Tabi no tochuu, is seemingly innocent on the surface. The opening song of Spice and Wolf, Tabi no Tochuu is a love song at its heart, sung by two people, and their dream of running to a place beyond the world. Ina took great care in not only making the visuals, but also editing and animating it, wanting it to "be like an anime opening!"

Ina would even go as far as to sing the backing vocals, giving the song an ethereal, ghostly quality, and within the context of the song, carries the desire of two who hold one another dearly, wishing to explore a world together of their own, without prying eyes. A song laced with both yearning and nostalgia, with love woven into it, Ina sings the part of both lovers…
Though far ahead of her later established story, the roots of it may already be present to those who take the time to dig deeper…
A World Just for Us

But amidst the the bright colors of flashbacks through the eyes of a possible observer, were also numerous moments of darkness, flickering briefly within the MV. The first, appearing for a single brief moment, might be the most concerning. Ina, water upon her face, her eyes shrouded in shadows, lies within a dark background, void of any objects. Her expression has no smile, her hair is unkempt, and everything is covered in gray, the color being washed away. Perhaps this Ina merely fell into the water. Perhaps she fell *somewhere else...*
Visual Glitches and loss of self

Lying within a white sheet, Ina goes to sleep at night, all the while memories play before her like a series of photos, each one lighting her own body in their colors. 
UNTIL SUDDENLY, between lines, the images vanish, and film glitch effects warp her appearance, leaving the sensation that something is wrong.
Another break in between lines later, and it happens again, and along with her face being distorted, her eyes are drawn over, obscuring the very windows to her soul.
Premonition of the Cracked Moon
“Is it lore? Is it not? It’s up for you to decide?”

body.text:
Given the significance of the moon within her lore, a vision of its coming destruction is a rather ominous prophecy, for both the priestess, and anyone associated with it.
Combined with the imagery of Ina’s face being distorted within a white shroud, Tabi no Tochuu warns that not all is as it seems, and danger may lurk within the future…
The Light and her Shadow. The Shadow and her Light.
Within Ina’s stream, she would explain her process of using After Effects and how she animated the MV. Along the way, she brought up this shot, Ina both holding up the cape before running forward.

However, with added context and time, it almost looks like two separate individuals. One enjoying the moment, the other racing to reach somewhere. One in the light, one in the dark… Perhaps she hadn’t planned it at the time, but it isn’t hard to imagine the two as both singers, one in the dark trying to reach the other in the light, the memory turning fuzzy and fading, in conjunction with the imagery of Ina’s face being blurred under the cloak, adds to the idea that this world or dream may be fading.
Fading Images in time...

The last element comes from the second clip section, images now swapping behind Ina one after the other, as if she is now on the opposite side of the film, her entire body remaining shrouded in darkness as image after image, memory after memory, slides behind her, opposite of where it played over her when she was cloaked earlier.
*Take note of this.*

Whether she had intended to, or became inspired after the fact, many elements within Tabi no Tochuu can be seen more literally within Temari, and like other great things, drops of ideas here may have swelled into deep oceans of story down the line.
Two singers wanting to explore a world of their own, a world that is fading, fate and time running out.

Creative use of light and dark to create mood, with multiple scenes that are almost unsettling with how they shroud Ina in darkness, her expressions at times even looking concerned.
Images, memories, and dreams, all floating before and behind them, signifying different places.
And a moon that is broken, and a priestess whose face is fading…

body.text: The story of the three takos
During the New Years Kimono relay at the start of 2022, Ina had prepared a small story to accompany the outfit, featuring Three tako siblings, two on her head as hairbuns, and one as a bag to hold.

The story is simple, the priestess asks each what they would like. The eldest and smartest, asks to be on her head, to be one of her braincells. The youngest and most playful, wished to join on her head to touch her hair. The last tako, the middle, could not decide, and asked “I am not the smartest or funnest, can I be like them too some day?” to which Ina responded “Of course, and I will hold you until you are ready.”

Though there is some similarity with Violet Ina and the middle tako, both being patient and waiting to choose, the other two are less clear. However, it does add the seemingly silly detail of takos being her braincells [See Tako Takover], and also reaffirms that Takos can be made into any shape. More important however, is that this was the first stream outfit to be included in any music videos, appearing as [Umbrella Ina] in [Temari].
Also, amusingly, Kimono Ina would reveal a set of horns, looking a bit less like an octopus, and almost like a dragon priestess... but that sounds ridiculous... right?
Don't forget, always somewhere, someone is fighting for you. As long as you remember her, you are not alone.
A call from the beyond

Arguably one of the most important bits of lore early on came from none other than an innocuous April Fool’s stream, taking place in 2022. After Ina left her stream to grab a package, AO-chan, now in tablet form, rose up to the screen front and center, with a new message prompt upon it. Moments after accepting, the world melted into black and white, and the bgm shifted into something more mysterious…
Falling asleep, the viewers would wake up moments later, to find themselves in a mysterious realm, and moments later, were greeted by a shadowy silhouette.
The stranger spoke, their voice distorted and out of order. However, if one reversed the audio, they got
“Can you hear me- [Fae]? Hello-yes-hello can you hear me Fae?”

Realizing the error in their audio, the stranger fixed their connection, allowing takos to meet face to face with its only inhabitant.
Well, face to mask.
The Wahtcher
The stranger would then ask chat a number of questions, and takos got some very, very interesting answers and hints…

Shortly after the Wahtcher first appeared, Ina would release her second cover, Nai Nai, a song by Reona used in the ED of Shadows House. Contextually, in the story of Shadows house, there exists a family of nobles who live far from other humans, named the Shadows for their appearance as living shadows. Attending to them are a number of humans, or more accurately: living dolls, humans that don’t just attend to the shadows, but act as the shadows second half, a face for the faceless.

It is within this context that Nai Nai’s EP begins, centered around two individuals, one human, and one seemingly, a living shadow/void. After all, the void can take on the shape of many things. In this instance, it looks like Ina… but, pure white with hints of pink, looking remarkably similar to the Wahtcher. All the while, the human Ina doesn’t appear to have flaps or squishies, her standard octopus traits.
The Shadow

The first and most striking visual of Nai Nai is that of **The Shadow**, a creature that resembles Ina, but has their colors inverted, and more shocking, a featureless body, as if composed of shadow itself.
Now, this could merely be a reference to the titular "Shadows" that reside in Shadows House, were it not for one thing...

The Shadow and the Wahtcher are colored the same. White hair bleeding into pink, while looking very, very similar to the Ina beside her. However, the shadow has flaps and squishies, unlike the goth Ina that resides over the MV who lacks the usual priestess features. And of course, her body is pitch-black, and while in Shadows house they are made of soot, the versatility of the void within the Inaverse could very much work like this.

The very fact that the shadow uses inverted colors only spices up that possibility further, playing off of Ina's enjoyment of color theory in her work, while establishing a new possibility: There exists a shadowy realm that is an inversion of our very own...
Forbidden Fruit

An intriguing metaphor repeated throughout the MV, and one I could not quickly find in the original song it was based off of, is that of an apple, repeatedly seen throughout Ina's cover of Nai Nai. Bright, red and juicy, it stands out strongly amidst the many blacks and whites that make up the MV, offering a temptation as enticing as it is foreboding.
Though apples can have a number of positive symbolic meanings, randing from love and healing, to preference and even immortality, they also, have a far more common association in western cultures.

Within literature and art, it is often the apple that is portrayed to be the "forbidden fruit", a fruit containing forbidden knowledge, growing from the tree of the knowledge of Good and Evil, which God forbade the first humans from eating. However, tempted by the devil, who promised a greater understanding of the universe, tempted the humans into taking a bite, and instantly, they became aware of both themselves and the universe around them, damning themselves with a single bite.

In western media, this fruit commonly takes the shape of an apple, and across various books and films, it is associated with both greater awareness, consciousness, and the curse of understanding. It also may simply parallel the religious narrative to describe a temptation, a choice that offers release for curiousity or an apparent pain, but comes with great consequences.

Within the context of the Inaverse, there are many, maaaany implications that can come into play. In particular, given the lyrics of Nai Nai and Ina's morose state of mind, the fruit might be less beneficial to her, and more to the one lurking behind her. The Shadow, without a soul of their own, looking to live once again... or perhaps even the first time, to gain the awareness and "become human."

Given goth Ina's acceptance of her own pointless existence and desire to give up, it might be that she is willing to give in to temptation, going so far as to state "Might as well start over." In similar fashion to how the "forbidden fruit" damned its consumers, the apple may represent a tempting choice to Ina:

Give yourself up to the being who wants to be you, and lose your awareness of the struggle and the pain of the world and your place in it altogether. An inverse of the classic story, but one that feels strongly connected with the Inaverse's themes, where the danger and temptation comes from Ina giving up her humanity.

HOWEVER, we cannot forget there are two people present here, and the forbidden fruit may not present knowledge for Ina,,, but for **The Shadow** lurking beside her, wishing to be human. Thus, the temptation is not to lose her favor with a deity for higher knowledge, but to give up something... her bodily vessel, her mind, her very soul?
For freedom from all the weight it takes to remain human. To give in, and let someone else live in your stead...
Whether it means  giving life to a shadow, reviving a lost soul, or becoming a puppet for a monster, so long as she can sleep, Ina might just...
TAKE
THE
BITE
And given the crash at the end of the MV, she very well may have taken the bite, giving sentience and a soul to something new...
Mirror

One recurring motif throughout the MV that WAS present in the original, is that of mirrors, paralleling Ina and her shadowy counterpart. The imagery invoked suggests not only that the two live in opposite worlds, but that their very realities might be shaped by one another.

In particular, mirrors do not present worlds of their own, but merely *reflect* their counterpart, and may indicate that rather than a unique entity, the shadow may be some form of Ina hidden from view. A reflection of her inner desires taking form in the shape of a silky silver and pink doll, radiant with light and charm. A doll that she would no longer have to be the face of...
Bird Cage
Within the Shadows House ED itself, we do see a bird cage, so here it may be simply a nod to the original. However, it does also fit the theme of being trapped, which leaves the question… which one?
Ina, or her shadow?

More interesting still, is that we see this scene as one among several on a film reel, calling back to the visuals of film images seen in Tabi no Tochuu, and potentially relating to the passage of time or parallel universes.

The camera than zooms into the cage once more, and we watch the cage explode and the colors invert, suggesting whatever was locked inside has been set free, and may have inverted the roles and positions.
Reincarnation

Combining together the lyrics with the Forbidden fruit, along with lines in various later performances and songs, the end of Nai Nai deepens the idea that Ina and the Wahtcher are reborn at some point in time. In particular, Ina appears to accept her own death, seeing herself trapped with no way out, taking a bite from the forbidden fruit…
The Lost Voice
“I say goodbye, but I am not seen nor heard”

One idea present in Nai Nai that will get continuous evidence in following performances, is that of an unheard voice. In this song, Ina contemplates giving in and accepting her disappearance, fully embracing her identity as a soulless puppet, and along with it, the idea that nobody can hear her voice. This weary, self-defeating acceptance may just be the original song's lyrics, but thematically, it repeats again in future projects and performances. 
This leads us to two likely candidates:
Past Ina, living in a colorless world, accepting her priestess duties and becoming a puppet.
The Wahtcher, locked outside of the world, forced to live a life alone, forgotten by the universe outside.
The song’s lyrics describing them as a ghost who can’t feel joy or cry leads me to believe it is past Ina more than the latter, struggling to understand the humanity she was deprived of.

Synopsis

Meconopsis is Ina’s 2nd original song, first revealed at the end of 2023 in Neverland Paradox, and released as a full MV on Ina’s birthday, May 20th 2024. A stark contrast to Violet, it follows Ina as she wakes out of a dream, and rejects the Ancient Ones.
Unlike her previous song, Meconopsis was HEAVILY inspired by the fan animation, Myth’s Bad Ending, a fan made story where Ina’s friends fight to bring her back from the Ancient One’s possession.

Whereas Violet had many direct visual clues and hints that connect to future work, Meconopsis is more cryptic, focusing on the moment where Ina recalls her memories and chooses her own path. As a result, placing Meconopsis within the larger Inaverse as a whole was difficult at first, feeling like an endpoint, if anything. However, as future songs released, takos would have a broader context on Ina’s vision as a whole, and Meconopsis’ place within it.

Overall, Meconopsis is a very unique song within the Inaverse. It is directly influenced by Myth’s Bad Ending, makes more direct connections to Lovecraft’s mythos, and has few references to the friend/other Ina’s… but if you look closer, you’ll find hints that connect to both Violet, and projects to come.

All together, the background details and direction behind the scenes of Meconopsis come together to create a unique and rare Ina, forged by her conflicts and saved by her bonds.
Meconopsis

The titular flower of the song, Meconopsis are rare Blue flowers that grow in the Himalayas, a harsh, high altitude environment where few other things can grow. Thus, the flower symbolizes Meconopsis Ina, a rare, ethereal beauty rich in spirit, forged by artificial conditions in the form of the priestess duties that tied her to AO. A wisdom and resolve that can only be learned through experience.

Additionally, the flowers themselves have a delicate appearance, and do not last long in most gardens or other environments. Thus, as strong-willed and mystical as Meconopsis Ina may be, it is only a matter of time until even her own petals are blown away. This matches both with Ina’s description of the song, with Meconopsis struggling to remain herself against the strain of AO’s influence, and the visuals, the melting halo and ballerina appearance showcasing her fragile, fading strength teetering moments before collapse.

Finally, the imagery has several poppy’s during the “A-o-i-ke-shi” sequence with the rainbows, showing two that have bloomed, one facing up, the other facing down, while a third has begun to bud. This unbloomed poppy may very well represent Meconopsis Ina herself, and suggests that regardless of whoever it is meant to be, a rebirth is coming.
Tenjo no yosei - The Heavenly Fairy

Another name for Meconopsis, it also befits Ina, as Riku mentioned. However, Meconopsis may not be the only fairy. During the first and second bridge, the line begins with “The fae up above drop their last petal,” suggesting that there are other fairy’s up above, each one giving Ina the last of their strength to free her. In spite of the Ancient One’s mockery as they fall, it is enough, and gives Ina the strength and power to fight back.
Cat's Cradle

Also known as Ayatori in Japan, Cat’s cradle is a game involving string between the fingers, one that can be played individually or with 2 or more players, and involves making new shapes by looping the string on and off between fingers, or by passing the loop of string with another player. In this instance, the position Ina is holding the string and the shape, implies she is playing with another person and waiting for their move. The choice of a children’s string game seems to call back to past Ina and her friend, to a simpler time where games allowed them to connect, and now, Ina is inviting them back to play again.

It can also be read in a more existential manner, Ina holding fate within her very hand, and wishing to create a new shape, one without the dominance of AO. The combination of Gold being used for the strings also has grand implications, as its scarce uses during the line “they see through all your lies-” and its appearance in Takodachi no Uta (See Drawn 2 Dawn), suggests it is connected with truth, trust, honesty. All together, it suggests Ina is attempting to meet another heart to heart, this time, without AO’s interference.
Fear

“The oldest and strongest emotion of mankind is fear.
And the oldest and strongest kind of fear is fear of the unknown.”

A quote by Lovecraft, its usage in the very intro of Meconopsis highlights the very conflict within Ina. Beneath the quoted text, 4 boxes of an unknown word appear, suggesting both of the major words within not just meconopsis, but across the entire Inaverse.

And in this instance, we are given what Ina fears without even having to look too far. Juxtaposed to Love, Ina’s fear highlights her struggle to be free of AO’s influence and live as herself. In spite of the danger and doomed fate remaining as the priestess, it was also what Ina was raised for, and until she made her friend(s, in the case of the Bad End influence…), that was all she knew. But thanks to that person, she discovered a greater world with more colors, full of both excitement and wonder, yet doubt and uncertainty, of dangers that leave her so weary and anxious that she might prefer to remain the priestess forever…
The fear that she might lose the things she holds close. The fear of her own new world of emotions and expression being rejected. The fear of a love she can never give or receive…
And all the awareness of just how DIFFERENT she truly is only makes it worse.
Love

Despite how cliche it may sound, Love really is the power that can do anything. In the same way that the ancient Ones are incomprehensible, Love is ABSURD. It can allow people to transform in the blink of an eye. It can give the strength for people to break past their own walls. It can even make the numb feel the world around them.
**Or keep two souls intertwined across Space and Time.**

Love is what drives Ina and her friend(s) to keep fighting against fate, no matter what stands against them.
An emotion that for those who can’t experience love, would simply become mad at the impossible strength it gives.

At the end of the day, the Unknown and the Heart are one in the same. Both are immeasurable depths that strike nerves and anxiety into all who plunge in. Both spin minds mad with curiosity and possibility.
And thus...
