body.text:
Overall, hints and responses heavily indicate that the Ina in Temari [The Second Priestess], is not Ina. Is she AO? A Shadow? Or is it her [Friend]? Or of course her “nemesis", [Past Ina]?
Perhaps the truth, is some mixture of the above…
The “Family”

At long last, we get our first look at the Ninomae Family. However, given that this is a cult that hides its children from the world to be used in sacrifices, the familial names appear to be less literally related, and more the nature and mannerisms of the faith. Not unlike Nuns calling one another “sister”.

Especially when the “Papa” Ina appears to call out to is a voice calling from the void, almost certainly belonging to THE ANCIENT ONES. In similar fashion, the “sisters” refers to the various girls taken into the cult to be used in ritual to summon AO, and with no other basis for close bonds, became family and more than one another, the only semblance of love and kindness in one another’s life that wasn't driven by ulterior motives.
Though not technically blood related, their shared role as sacrifices does tie them by blood in a way. An oath of blood, not by choice, but forced upon them by the cult. And though it may be for ulterior motives, the girls beside Ina in Tako Takover all being nuns only seems to reinforce this angle.
The Second Inanis/Other "Ina" (Temari Ina)

The second priestess. The Friend. And perhaps even: The Wahtcher. Throughout Temari, we get numerous hints that the Ina we see within is “not Ina”, to the point that *even Ina herself teased it in both the Post-MV stream and her 5th anniversary recap.*
Umbrella/Kimono Ina

A strange girl who shares some features with the Ina seen in her ending stream, Umbrella Ina is seen briefly at the beginning and end of Temari, with her eyes and upper features hidden. However, one immediate thing that can be distinguished, is that this is also Kimono Ina/Tako Bun Ina, the Ina revealed years earlier with the story of the three Tako siblings.

Combined with the Takodachi lore later revealed in Tako Takover, one can gather the idea that Umbrella Ina may not be one single person, but one girl with more than a single soul attached to her body. Even further evidence comes with her visual appearance, the bright red umbrella coloring her hair inside crimson, all the while, we are not allowed to see her eyes. Given that not long after Temari dropped we got chuuni Ina with her Dragon-Eye, one can guess that not only is Umbella Ina the [Dragon] (or at least containing them), but that she is possibly connected with [Abyss Ina].

Further evidence can be seen with the image of a shadow descending into the Earth beneath Umbrella Ina at the start of the song, altogether hinting that [Past Ina] or [Temari Ina] (i.e. the Wahtcher), are connected to Umbrella Ina in some fashion.
But of course, there might be one other…
AO: The Ancient Ones

All throughout Temari, the unmistakable presence of the Ancient Ones are felt. From the worship and actions of the Ninomae Family, to flashbacks of girls swallowed in darkness, there is no escape from the dread of horror beyond understanding.

And yet… AO’s role continues to be complex, and uncertain.  The vast majority of the evil that takes place in Temari isn’t the bidding of AO themselves, but the **family**, seemingly seeking to bring about AO, if not outright use them. A family that worships the very ground the priestess walks upon, leaving the other children to be forgotten, as if they were broken toys.

Given that Ina’s relationship with AO isn’t always hostile, along with a very strong hint that AO-chan was sent to help a priestess by none other than the friend/Wahtcher, it seems as though AO might not be pure evil. Rather, given previous songs and performances, along with imagery involving mirrors and reflections, an interesting conclusion arises:
AO may not be evil, but answers to, empowers, and most importantly, reflects the mind of the person they are bonded with.

After all, even Seibin and Lumina describe Temari with a dark yet hopeful context, implying that Ina is able to change her fate by reaching out to another. Though who responds back and when, may need more context to fully align together…
(Query): Amongst the humans?

Within Lovecraft and eldritch stories, it is not unusual to get tales that involve possession, bodies and minds being taken over by the will of other beings. This has largely fueled various fan projects like Myth’s Bad End, tales of Ina losing her personality and being taken over by a hostile, otherworldly presence.

However, in Neverland Paradox and Nai Nai, we get a more nuanced relationship. We see within them a girl who, doubting her own ability and voice, willingly gives her body up to the Ancient Ones. Rather than actively seeking a host, it may be instead that the sisters seek AO in desperation. This also goes along with Lumina and Seibin’s statements, AO potentially giving the girls the means to change their fates.

So, is AO taking pity on the girls, but maybe struggling to understand humanity? Indifferent and reflecting their desires? Or are they what we Feared all along, eager and excited to bring the world to ruin, and drown all that was worth loving? Or perhaps something else?
*Who, if any, has been possessed?*
*Does AO have ulterior motives, whether good or bad?*
*Would you trust AO to wake you up before your 8 hour flight?*
Perspective

What Ina said in Violet, “it all depends on perspective,” pays dividends in Temari. Throughout the MV, there are changes in graphics and details that suggest different locations. Pay enough attention, and you can see the cracks where reality falls into... *something else*. Take for instance: “her mole is on the wrong side of her face!” That would certainly seem true, no doubt.
But, if you look at it as a mirror world, suddenly, little things that look out of place, suddenly make sense.  Pay attention to when things appear flipped, and you begin to get a clearer image of just what is happening...

This is seen in greater obviousness when you slow down specific sequences. Within chorus 2, we have the mole flipping between when Ina is viewed from afar and up close. Combined with her eyes being closed in the up close, when her mole is on the correct side, it suggests we are an *observer*.

A similar thing occurs during verse 3, as we jump between a shot of Ina in the void from afar, with a ball to her left. Yet when we flip perspectives, her eyes are closed, and the ball is now on the right. Yet again, we are not her, looking at her reflection, but the one observing her. In both instances, we assume the view of both girls, split across a divide, attempting to contact each other.
Mirror Worlds: The Void and Reality

ONE IMMEDIATE thing you must understand, is that Temari takes place, in multiple locations/realms, and likely, multiple timelines/points in time. The easiest and quickest way to showcase this, is by comparing different scenes of the ritual, and taking note of multiple consistent differences. The biggest however? The bars and walls are not the same. For example, during verse 2, if you look behind Ina, the wall is grey, and you can see the pillars spinning around her. But, during verse 3, the bars are all black, and when they go behind her, they vanish into the dark…

We are no longer in reality. Reality has physics, structure, threads you have to tie around pillars to keep them hooked… Not black bars that reflect no light fading into a featureless void, nor does it have mist and floating threads that zip around.
How does that even make sense?
Well, remember how Ina was mirrored in some scenes?
**The void is a shadow of the real universe. A reflection of realspace, it has no form of its own. And as a result, the void is a mirror to reality. A realm without shape.**
Thus, the bars of one world, with its light and features, appear only as a dark mass in the other, the facsimile of the real thing, a genuine SHADOW of what should be there.
Remember the existence of these parallel worlds, and continue to pay attention to differences throughout similar scenes, and soon, you'll begin to unravel the mysteries of Temari...
But now that we are aware of the parallel worlds, we can explore the rest of the elements in greater detail.
Textured borders

Another unique variable, there are multiple scenes, mainly near the beginning and end, in which borders rise up from the bottom and top of the screen, looking rather similar to the void cards that appear at the beginning of verse 3. Each time they appear, they also have different colors, and we can use the combination of color to help decipher both who is in the scene, and who they are communicating with…
But how to communicate between worlds?
TEMARIS

The titular visual of the song, temaris are balls woven of thread featuring various designs, and are generally thought of as children’s toys. Within the context of Temari, the creators describe Ina weaving together memories, and combined with each sister having a different temari, depicts them as objects with an intimate attachment to the holder.
Within the into of Temari we see 6 surrounding a red umbrella, linked with a ripple in the water. All of them feature unique designs of red, black, and white…
EXCEPT FOR ONE.

There is one seen in the intro and during the descent into the abyss that is only black and grey… except for when it is glowing. The lack of red in a song dripping in it, and especially being grey, not even white, HEAVILY correlates with two thoughts. Either the ball belongs to Past Ina, in her monochromatic world. Or, the Ball belongs to something that isn’t human anymore, which given the black fiery drop of paint that lands on the girl’s eye insignia, might be the case.
Temari Balls: Purpose
*So what is the purpose of the temari balls?*
Well, remember how the creators of the song state that it represents "Ina weaving painful memories into new ones?"
Temaris hold memories.
If you recall back in **[Violet]**, we watched Ina's memories of the past fade into the dark, and all throughout, she struggled to remember anything beyond a single detail of that person she missed.

Thus, temari's being able to store memories not only helps her to reconnect with her past, but also suggests that something. Be it a parallel reality, the void, or both, have a tendency to steal memories over time, or make them difficult to reach. And perhaps not just memories, but given the use of takodachis in **[TakoTakover]**, might act as literal containers for souls.

**And given the Ninomae family "daughters" had to make contact with the void, the temari balls may have been the only way to anchor them to reality, as without being remembered, they can't return, lost to the abyss forever.**
Temari Balls: Additional

There are also several interesting circumstances involving temari balls. First, right before the priestess eyes glow red, we see a Temari ball not seen anywhere else (seen in textured borders above) that vanishes shortly after, has strange patterns, and is painted red. This suggests the owner is both at least partially human, and may be the result of Ina using past memories to weave together new ones. Weaving past temari balls into a new one.

The second curiosity is that in verse 3, there are 6 temari balls, and two are duplicates. These balls appear to belong to Ina, the likely first priestess, and heavily hints that more than 1 timelines are involved. This also may allow for the second priestess to pull off some elaborate plays as she tries something different.

Finally, within the intro, the temaris surround the umbrella, suggesting that the umbrella may be just like the temari, a device or object that can hold a soul. Further evidence to this is Ina’s very own ending screen, in which AO’s dark tentacles can be seen lurking within the umbrella. Umbrellas also function as an apparatus for preventing rain, and can symbolize protection from evil. All together, it paints the image that umbrella Ina is not as stable and cool as she first appears, and one bad breeze might have dangerous consequences.
Placing the umbrella in between the other balls, does a lot to indicate it might actually be what is trapping AO. Ironic, a device used to ward rain, containing the Abyssal God within… *How poetic.*
Threads

One strong way to notice whether we are in the real world or in the abyss in any scene, is to look at how threads are used. Now, within our very real and physical world, a thread is mostly, just a thread. An object bound to the realm of physics. You can tie it around a pillar, hang it on something, but it still has to obey gravity and the laws of physics. Unless we aren’t in the real world.

Take for instance: Temari balls, balls woven together with thread, that within Temari, appear to encase thoughts, memories, and souls of individuals. Acting as a sort of body for the soul even in the void. Just like how physics move differently, thought moves differently within the abyss. THUS, Threads don’t just represent the above, but also act as lines of communication, connecting souls to one another.

Hence why throughout various scenes, we get glimpses of threads that float or zip across empty space, seemingly impossible in the real world…
Because we aren’t in the real world.

Thus, Threads can not only help us understand whether we are in the real world or the abyss, but also inform us of whom and when characters are talking to each other…
Combine that with the perspective rules above, and we get a much better understanding of who we are and where.
*Now combine perspective and threads…*

Thus, in the wide shots of Verse 2, we are seeing our own reflection in the real world. When the camera zooms in right at the end of the Verse on Ina(?)’s red eyes, we are looking from the perspective of the girl across the divide. Hence, why we see the red eye Ina with the mole on the correct side, and her eyes close before transitioning. Because we are her OBSERVOR.

On the flip side in verse 3, we are yet again in the perspective of the observer, gazing at our own reflection within the void. When the camera zooms in and the priestess in the void closes her eyes, we are looking from the other side, hence why her mole is on the left again (seen very fuzzily at 2:27).
Thus, throughout the two ritual sequences in verse 2 and 3, we witness two parts of a conversation between the priestesses. One in reality, one in the void.
Threads: The lost voice

The theme of a voice being lost, depicted both in [Neverland Paradox] and [Nai Nai] previously, comes back in full. In one of the MV's most striking scenes, we witness the white silhouette of a young girl trapped in a white void, amidst many white threads, all the while screams around her ask to be saved.

Given both the previous context of the hints of a voice being lost continuing further in **[Takodachi no Uta]**, it appears it may be the voice of the very girl here, trapped in the void, her voice unable to reach anyone anymore...

Whether she willingly gave away her voice in exchange for saving another, or had it stolen, is not certain. In either instance, the **[Wahtcher]** is heavily implied to be that very individual. A voice whose words are fleeting to Ina, and who needed to use a voice similar to Ina's to speak to takos. Combined with the hints in **[Meconopsis]** of their being travelers in the *Inaverse*, there might be a chance the reason the voice can't reach others is because it is coming from another universe altogether.
The truth? We'll learn someday soon, no doubt.
Hanafuda Cards

Rather than focusing on flowers like her previous MV’s, Ina’s primary visual motif for Temari were the balls. However, in order to spice them up, Ina would also base their designs off of Hanafuda playing cards. In particular, the ball of the girl in the center most aggressively resembles the full moon card, the hikari (bright) card of the August suit. In addition to tying her presence to late summer, each set seems to be associated with a different plant, with August being Susuki grass. Said grass is strongly associated with Autumn and Tsukimi, the moon viewing festival. The grass generally seems to have association with the changing of seasons and transient nature of life, swaying under the autumn sun and moon. It is also thought to bring good harvests, and ward evil spirits.
The inspiration is made a bit more clear and obvious with Lumina’s post of the layout and raw design for Temari, depicted here.
Hanafuda also come in a variety of other plants and symbols, perhaps you’ll be able to find something interesting by looking through them!
Temari is a dense song, so I will be continuing the rest of the analysis in a second chapter!

entries.title: Temari: Two Inanis', Time travel, and more...
entries.subject: Temari part 2
entries.author: Astraea

body.text: Towards the beginning and the end

Temari is an exceptionally dense song loaded with many clues for those who take the time to pursue them. As a result, we will be continuing on with our previous knowledge as we get into some even more intriguing revelations.
Time
“I have to say, there is… multiple points of time in one MV…”
body.cite: Ina during the Temari MV release stream.

body.text: One theme that will probably reach most listeners and watchers after a play or two, is that Temari does not take place in a sequential order. Rather, right from the beginning, we get multiple points of time. Umbrella Ina lays over the image of Past Ina, not only implying Past Ina’s connection to Temari, but implying what we see within the MV is a sort of memory, or perhaps even an event taking place elsewhere. Right after, we see the priestesses, heads of the Ninomae Family, who appear at least to be close in age with the other Ina’s. But not long after, we also see a much fuller flashback of Past Ina, and it immediately becomes apparent that Temari takes place at multiple points in time.

However, the story keeps flipping back and forth, showing parts of a story, but forcing us to try and put it together. Try to put it all in the order as its presented, and you’ll be left dizzy.
Because just as Temari involves mirrored realities where left is right, Temari involves time that moves forward… and backwards…
That's right.
Temari has time travel.

The most immediate and effective example, will be the scene of Ina and her friend shoving one another, like in Violet, now being played backwards. We begin with the shot of a girl standing alone, and then it transitions into the shoving scene, the opposite order of Violet’s depiction. All the while, a clock can be heard in the background. But even more important, follow the shadows, moving right to left, suggesting a sun that is moving backwards…

This entire sequence builds up to our sight of Past Ina when she got AO-chan, stuck within a grisly looking cage, body horribly mangled. If this is the family’s beloved priestess, it’s no wonder the other sisters perished. After slathering her blood upon the wall, she is gifted the necronomicon beneath a [white light], suggesting that it was her friend who brought her AO-chan in the first place.

That isn’t where time-travel ends.
If you pay close attention during the ritual sequences, you will see the pillars moving in unison, right to left. Almost resembling the spinning of a clock. If that is true, remember the mirror worlds? They are not spinning in the same direction, because one is mirrored.
*Time in the Abyss moves backwards.*
This also means, intriguingly, the equivalent to rewinding time in the real world, is winding time forward in the Abyss.

Which is why, even though everything about the wall sequence appears to be moving backwards, Ina always spins to this song clockwise. Because it is the Ina of the Abyss who is returning to the present.

This is also why the ritual requires 2 girls, because without one remaining to act as an anchor in reality, the other will be lost in the void forever, always marching to the beginning of the universe.
The time flipping nature of the void also provides an idea to why the memories of those in the void are lost over time.
For we brought nothing into this world, and can take nothing out of it.
People who are lost in the void aren't erased... they are simply going backwards and time. Or, at least that is one possibility.

While these exact mechanics may not be perfectly accurate, what is certain with songs to come, is that time travel is integral to the Inaverse, provides a clue as to how Ina’s from different worlds communicate, and may be one way rebirth plays such a vital role within the story.
A third realm?

Within each chorus, we get a glimpse into a world that is not reality or the void, but seems to behave similar to the void. Here, black threads float freely in chorus 1, perhaps representing a chaotic realm beyond human comprehension, and with additional clues from lyrics and the spinning cipher, likely belongs to AO, or some sort of celestial deity. Further evidence is displayed after chorus 1, where we see a red and white star in the sky over the island and ocean. The presence of a rainbow to signify divine power and transformation, also gives hints at an ascension or possession taking place.

On the flipside, in chorus 2, the threads are now white, and rather than float freely, are all spun in an outward circle, as if under the command and strain of a new entity taking control. Almost like a spider web she has fallen into…

Combined with the (Wahtcher, Second Priestess, Temari?)’s manic expression and her transforming appearance, it would appear that she has overthrown AO or taken their power, looooong hinted ago in [Neverland Paradox]. The return of the rainbow within the scene further fuels that some sort of ascension has taken place.

All together, this location, bathed in radiant red may not be the void at all, but something different, a form of *unreality* or higher plain, weaving together the light and dark. Just who or what it means, we can't tell by Temari, though it may just be where AO came from...
Beyond the Void: A ball of frozen time

Given the tease we get of Wahtcher we get at the end of Temari, we might as well address them too. Between Violet, the Wahtcher stream, and Abyssal Hymn, there are multiple mentions of a world without time, which all points to Beyond the Void, a [third realm] that can observe all realities at once. Even further proof comes with the Wahtcher herself speaking backwards when she first appeared, suggesting she might be used to communicating in the void. However, given that she isn’t there, it would appear that she was somehow able to create or take over a realm that exists beyond time. Alternatively, in spite of her calm demeanor, she might be imprisoned there, still waiting until infinity to be rescued.

Further evidence was later found when takodachis, taking Ina's comments to heart, began to searching for clues in other works. One unexpected connection came from her art gallery of all places, a VRchart world made in previous years to enjoy all of Ina’s artwork. The art gallery lies in an infinite ocean, an oasis between an endless blue sky and sea. Within it, Ina’s art surrounds a central white pedestal, looking exactly like the pillar Beyond the Void.
And for anyone bold enough to touch the pillar, they are transported directly to Beyond the Void itself. Thanks to the takos who explored within, we discovered that the place itself isn’t merely a bubble, but actually a giant temari, likely within the void, and you can see its lines by looking up and increasing the brightness!
All together, it confirms that not only is the priestess at the end of the song the Wahtcher, but that her realm safe from AO’s influence lies within a giant Temari ball.
Ciphers

Vital to understanding Temari, there exist a number of cipher coded texts throughout the MV, many of which describe two different priestesses. Upon the top of the screen, text with Ina’s crown would appear, while on the bottom, another with an unknown symbol (The Eight Bridges?) would respond. Within days, Takodachis were able to decipher most of the language, giving us an insight into two very interesting individuals, and a glimpse of their story within the Ninomae family.

0:01 
Ninomae Inanis From Today Onwards You Shall Become The Head of This Family

0:11 
Can you hear my voice? || Witchcraft

0:26 
This whole world feels || Nothing but cursed

0:40 
the second inanis

0:43 
the second destiny || another destiny

1:03 
the necronomicon || forbidden knowledge

1:53 (floating around the priestess)
I shall descend now into the world of humankind to watch over you

1:57 
the sealed island || and a resurrection

2:08 
divine omen || and they worshiped her with absolute devotion

2:15 
across the divide stood another fated child || she was wracked with guilt and at last she made a new choice

IMMEDIATELY, the cipher gives us many ground-breaking revelations. The biggest one? There is more than one Inanis. And given the visuals used to represent them sometimes being different than "Our" Ina's, it's likely they are entirely separate individuals. Not only that, but the cipher outright states that there is both a second destiny, if not more given "another destiny". And perhaps most intriguing of all, is a voice stating they will now enter humankind to watch over someone… More than likely, this is AO speaking, perhaps even taking pity upon Ina and the Ninomae girls, and gives further evidence that AO possesses someone to walk and live amongst humanity.
The Two Priestesses

We CANNOT go any further, however, without diving into the two decoded speakers from the ciphers. Rather than being the same individual, it is ABUNDANTLY evident that these two are incredibly different from one another, and heavily telegraph that the two? Are the first and second priestesses.

First and foremost, the top cipher speaker is far more direct and factual, devoid of most emotion. This, combined with Temari’s overall nature, and Ina’s crown accompanying the statements, leads me to believe the top cipher is Past Ina [Violet:Past Ina] and the First Priestess. This very heavily fits Past Ina’s character of being married to her priestess duties (metaphorically), and living in a grey world.

On the other hand, the bottom cipher is DEEPLY EMOTIONAL, far more disgusted with both the cult and world at large, and beyond everything, is full of Deep regret and sorrow, guilt driving them to make a new choice. Given that we yet again see Past Ina being shoved away, we can make the strong inference that the one who shoved her is none other than the Second Priestess, choosing to change destiny by taking Ina’s place as priestess.
Camellias

Though Ina herself would state that flowers don’t have as overt of a message as they did in the previous songs, they still do a lot to amplify the atmosphere of Temari. 
Having multiple meanings, they can be seen as resilience and beauty in modesty, calling back to the meanings of violets. However, they also have a darker side, and are likened to a samurai’s head being chopped off, as well as an ill-omen in some contexts. Given that these only appear over the heads of sisters with dark imagery around them, it's safe to say that within the Inaverse, camellias are associated with death and misfortune, diligent girls slain by the very task they were born for.

Another, increasingly intriguing fact, is that there is also a yokai (Furutsubaki-no-rei) said to grow from old Camellia trees. An inspiration that if used, would not mean well for anyone who remains around the cult for a long time…
The Ring/Halo

Displayed in both the crown mentioned below and here, this is the only time aside from Meconopsis we have seen something resembling (or implied to be), Ina’s halo. The first, seen briefly during chorus 1, appears as the imagery is glitched out, and almost seems to resemble a portal, within which, we see Ina’s crown. The last two, however, are red rings that appear, scattering out red balls tied to a twin with thread, each ball mimicking a shared bond. Appearing both during verse 3 and the final chorus, the red ring and balls appear to indicate a connection between different dimensions, and implies that Ina’s halo isn’t just a sign of her divinity, but also grants her the ability to travel between realities.

The red balls spiraling out from the ring further the idea that it acts as some sort of portal. Given the fact that each bacll is connected to another via thread, it also stands to reason that they are representingthe actual temaris, suggesting each one may be connected with another somehow.
Crown

Within chorus 1, we get a brief shot of visuals ran through a filter, showing the priestesses(?) hand reaching through a ring towards 5 diamonds resembling the tiara/crown that Ina wears. Combined with the earlier shot of the 5 sisters holding Temari balls, it suggests Ina may be a combination or vessel for their shared souls, or that they are attached to her in some fashion.

Around the 5 diamonds/stars we see the unmistakable ring that seems to represent Ina's halo. If the halo is truly an indicator of Ina's divinity and ability to cross realms, the diamonds may be a significant clue as to how she achieved that ability. Namely, given the 5 girls seen earlier, along with several hints of the number 6 throughout temari being significant, it may be that 5 other girls are needed to make the 6th ascend.  This is further supported by the ever present role of **pairs** and **duos** across Temari, each potentially being split across the mirrored realities.
Unknown symbol

Within chorus 1, we witness passing banners displaying an unknown set of visuals, the same ones used in the bottom cipher text on the screen. I had previously considered it might be connected with Yatsuhashi, the eight bridges, but I can't find enough corresponding evidence to support that claim.

Thus, my best current guess is that it may be related to the themes of languages in some way, and Lumina designed this to exemplify the idea. If that is the case, then it might be a similar instance to Meconopsis invoking a traveler. Especially with them having memories of a previous life, whether having lived it themselves or just recieving them, they appear to be more than meets the eye.
Sigils of blood and thread

Throughout the ritual portions of Temari’s MV, the priestesses sit upon a sigil. Starting with an outer ring, the inside displays 2 overlapping circles, and within it, a single line, mimicking an octopus eye. Paying close attention to the scenes, you will also notice it only glows on the ground in the void, not in the grey/physical world. Although interestingly, it only glows for one brief scene, suggesting a difference in perspective, or entirely different instances.

Following chorus 1, an image of a sigil appears out of looks like dried blood, the lines all muddled together. The scene then shifts into the void, and the sigil becomes 2 threads trying to tie together, reminiscent of the moon sequence in Violet. With the change in design, the eye design becomes even more apparent, and is now sheltered within a hexagon. The brief scene here in Temari may hint at the nature in the 2 priestess creations being different, one done out of duty, blood, connections forced upon them. The other? A choice, brought to fruition by a bond, heart, and desire.
"An oath of blood, an oath of love."
Blood and Love

Referred to previously in Meconopsis, here we get a full display on the difference between the blood taken in duty, and the love given by the heart. Within the various flashbacks, we not only get solid evidence at the deaths of the other sisters, but also witness past Ina(?) herself straining through her duties, sacrificing her own blood on a wall out of desperation. This blood, forced by the “family” duties placed upon her, displays the violence in connections born out of imposed dreams and wishes, stripped of her own freedom of expression to become a deity she had never sought to be. Rather, her whole life without color offered her little alternative, and it was only after others brought new colors into her life that she began to have a change of heart. But here? It was too late.
And thus, the first priestess was born.

A life given solely for others to impose upon it reveals the deterioration that is left behind. If the other dead girls didn’t stop the family, there’s no doubt they’d care little for the damage done for the one who is left, nothing more than an object to fulfill their wishes, her body matching her future. Broken and empty. A host for a dream she was rehearsed into.

This is contrasted deeply with love in both Temari and its repercussions in Violet and Meconopsis. While the first ritual was marked by a pool of blood, the second shows two threads looped around together. Taking into consideration the meanings of the threads and temaris, the juxtaposition of the two ties back to the discussion of [Love and fear in Temari], revealing Love to be an equivalent to witchcraft, magic that can overwrite reality and fate.
However, Temari isn’t a simple story where love just wins.

Though Past Ina is unaware of her own feelings, and will take time for her world to blossom with colors, the second priestess is burdened with the guilt of the past, and still carrying the scars gifted by the family, her love is shaped into sacrifice.
She shoves Ina away.
She hides the truth, hoping to keep her safe in the dark.
She takes all the burden upon herself.
And all the sin, should she choose revenge…
But most importantly, she bears the weight alone.
Her love isn’t just sunshines and rainbows, it’s toxic and self-harm, putting every sacrifice upon herself, to protect the only person that made her world worth living.
A person raised to be an empty idol, a void without a soul to become a living god, who deep down, had a soul inside… Brilliant and shining in the abyss of her own heart.
And as Ina realizes (Violet) who she is, against her sister/friend’s wishes, she will return to the abyss.
Moon and stars

The moon and stars play a particularly indirect role in Temari, appearing briefly in chorus 1 along scarlet lyric banners, the top depicts an 8 pointed star with 2 teardrops, while the bottom depicts a crescent moon with 3 teardrops. The star immediately plays with the idea of godly beings (Ancient Ones), as 8 is both a sacred number, and represents something beyond counting (Infinite). Though another interesting connection could be made to the Buddhist eight-fold path. Another, even further reach might be to the goddess ishtar, who had the 8 pointed sun as a symbol, and was connected to Venus, the morning star. Digging even further back, can connect it to the goddess Inanna.

On the flipside, the crescent moon and 3 teardrops is more difficult to find answers for, but the best immediate connection is to a pagan/wiccan symbol used in blessing circles, though the examples I found are rather brief. Though another connection could be to the goddess Isis, wife of Osiris (god of the dead and resurrection), who is associated with the flood, which was sometimes associated as the tears she shed for Osiris. Isis is both related with the kingship, magic, and the sky.

Overall, these inspirations may not be exact, but the symbols in general both weeping does seem to connect with an oncoming flood, hinted at multiple times in Violet and with various other performances. The morning star also appears to connect more with Ina’s counterpart/friend, or perhaps even a different Ina, as ours to this point has yet to be connected with an 8 sided star. On the other hand, the moon with 3 tears connects to her already established moon symbols, and intertwines with the connection between the moon and the tides. Tying it all together, it may indicate that their grief and longing will always bring them back together, and the inevitable gravity of the coming future.
Colors and light

Throughout Temari, color plays an important role, even moreso than usual, filling us in on clues, such as who is present in the scene, and who is being talked to. In particular, three/four colors play the biggest role.

Red -  representing both blood, but also love, stylizing the threads that bind the girls together. Red also can be said to represent their humanity Though, of course, red often has rather antoganistic associations with evil and inner darkness. Through this lens, one might believe the red is instead, evidence of something darker creeping into the the girls' lives.
Black - Easily connected with the Abyss and all its mysteries.
White - Associated with divinity, and also shares a likeness with the Wahtcher and Beyond the Void.
Grey - Colorless and dull, grey befits an object, made only to complete its purpose, with little self-regard. This in particular, could have interesting consequences with the ritual in verse 2…

The return of Rainbow light after both chorus 1 and during the second chorus yet again indicate the presence of the divine, and given all the rituals and sacrifice involved, may indicate each Inanis’ ascendant power.

If we believe light to be associated with the friend/wahtcher, it can be read as the previous timeline friend talking to the current one/Temari Ina, warning them of the future, encouraging them to become a priestess in Ina’s place. Hence why she both pushes past Ina away, and appears visually connected with light.
If by chance Past Ina were the Wahtcher, that too might have interesting implications for Abyssal Hymn.
Design

Temari, that is, the actual design for the girl on the cover and during the chorus, is a very different appearance from the other two, displaying its themes with pride. Her colors are overall muted, monochrome all across her surface, save for her eyes. Out of all the Ina’s, Temari hides the most skin, save for her feet, emphasizing her enslaved future and highlighting the awful conditions and circumstances she grew through. From a design standpoint however, Temari is top-heavy, clothes and layers swallowing her frame and dragging with her motions. These all hover over bare legs, and in doing so, emphasize that she is given little care while carrying the hopes and dreams of many others, not even offered protection from the cold stone and wood she walks upon.

The white of her dress hints at her purity, smothered in a charcoal grey haori that cloaks her like a blanket, as if she is being protected from any tainted colors. However, the Haori’s inside is dyed a brilliant crimson red, revealing that despite every effort to crush them, Ina now carries emotions forged by her connections with other humans beneath her cold shell.
Witchcraft and SIX

Stated by Seibin themselves, witchcraft is main theme and aesthetic of Temari, a great deal of both the song and MV focusing on the occult and utilizing numerous elements that invoke it. One of the more peculiar relations however, is the relationship the MV makes between witchcraft and the number 6.
For instance, hex is a word that can be synonymous for spell, as in “I cast a spell and a voice calls my name.”
However, Hex also forms the first part of the word hexagon, a 6 sided shape. Look close enough, and you'll see multiple instances of 6 in Temari.

On the sleeves of the priestesses in chorus 1 and 2, the red interior is full of hexagons, each one with 6 eyes inside. Zoom out during the ritual scenes, and you will see the spinning red holographic is shaped like, you guessed it, a hexagon. To top it all off, there are 6 Temari balls shown at the start.

Now, let's apply this knowledge to the flower sequence. Within it, we see 5 girls. However, the girls vanish in pairs of 2, suggesting the ritual requires 2 parties. So if we round up to get a pair, we end up with 6 girls. But where's  the 6th? Well, remember how Ina mentioned that Violet changed depending on perspective? That's right...
**We are looking from the view of the 6th girl during the flashback sequence.**
Mikurashima island

Discovered thanks to hard-working takodachis, there is a brief flash at 39 seconds into the MV with not just the cipher’s alphabet, but once decoded, coordinates to an island located at 33.87755492239361 139.6206003846799.

“This island has a legend of a Myojin (deity), who on January 20th, a day of misfortune, wearing red clothes and iron geta, descends from the main hall of Inane shrine along the “Path of the Gods” to the village, and on the night of the 24th, roams the village. On this day, called “Taboo-day”, the villagers eat deep fried mochi, and stay inside after midnight to avoid encountering the fearsome Myojin. Early in the morning of the 25th, it is said that a boat sets sail from Daikon-ga-hama, at the foot of the village cliff, bound for Kozushima (Kamishu-jima), the island where the gods gather. On this day, one must not look out at the sea.”

In addition to the very occult-like legend that would be right at home in a lovecraft novel, the connection with the sea and divinity also raises some interesting connections. In fact, the very shrine, the Inane-jinjya shrine, would almost seem to refer to Ina’nis and Ane’nis, sisters, an amusing connection between real sisters and the hardship forged “sisters” of the Inaverse.
EXCEPT…
That is not the shrine the coordinates take us to.
Inane shrine lies near the coast. But the coordinates take us to a far more quaint shrine inland up the hill… One gazing out to the distant sea.
There is no doubt that Ina may have taken some inspiration from the legend of the Myojin and its connection with the sea, and in particular, its journey to Kozushima.
Hmmm, but that isn’t the shrine that appears.
You wanna know that quaint shrines name???
I…

We just got pranked.
Myojin? Sisters? All of it pales to the truth:
**[The God of the Grass Festival.]**

Meta stuff, but for those who missed early Hololive or just may not be familiar with JP in general, Kusa is used to depict laughter, not too dissimilar from LOL, and it isn’t unusual to see chat sometimes say “wwww” to represent blades of grass, since they share a name.  So, in essence, Ina, or at least the first Inanis that is posessed just as the cipher appears, is somehow represented or connected to a "God of laughter."

If we gaze back upon the meta connection of Ina's past before Hololive, and her Past life in lore as being colorless, than this deity, might be her becoming a warped idol she never sought to be. Rather than finding any dreams or color of her own, Ina embraces the ones enforced on her, becoming an empty vessel who brings others joy, while never finding herself, finding only the praise of those who raised her to be somebody else. An empty goddess who never loved herself.
Once upon a time
-there was a girl named Ina'nis. She spent her days singing by the lake. But one day,

Ina’s 3rd birthday live in 1025, Evermore, was a more whimsical and light-hearted affair than her previous ones, and would introduce us to a character who would later become canon to the Inaverse. Set within a magical book, the concert plays heavily into classic fantasy settings, with Ina this time becoming the hero to save a frozen world. So begins a magical tale of song and dance, delighting all who bore witness to the Wandering hero.

Forgotten words / Mirai Kodai Orchestra ft. Kiwako Ashimine
Suzume / RADWIMPS ft. Toaka

Kuroiuta / Eir Aoi
storia / Kalafina (w/ Watame, Botan)
Toaru Ryuu no Koi no Uta / Kanako Ito
Kaine/Salvation / MONACA
Synchronicity～Chapter 3 Meguru Sekai no Requiem～ / Kagamine Rin, Kagamine Len (w/ Bae)
The Brave / YOASOBI
Opening themes

Evermore is the first birthday live to take place AFTER Ina had largely established her story up to this point, and in the interest of time, I’m gonna skim a bit and focus on continuing themes. Reading through the lyrics behind the songs, the first couple are very similar to previous Ina lives, especially Neverland Paradox.

To begin, Innocent Blue highlights an attitude that is drastically different than previously seen in Temari. Caught by the warm wind of a new season, the singer feels at ease, able to be more open and allow her heart to soar. She invokes recalls "their innocent vow", potentially referencing both her own past and future reunion with the Wahtcher in Abyssal Hymn, and led by her own heartbeat, Ina begins to follow.

“At my unsullied wish, the things set in motion,
The irreplaceable future, and the power I believe in this world,
Have all been enveloped by my shine.”
Whether it is naivete, hope, or the confidence that comes with experience, Ina now appears to recognize the light within herself.

With Forgotten Words, the tone begins to change, lyrics in the first verse reflecting elements within the Inaverse, dreams spoken aloud, a fog in a fairytale that leads her astray, and “An extended hand - The slightest hint of a premonition,” imagery very similar to Violet and Temari. The singer drives forward, fate marching on around them, pondering the millions of stories and melodies that will be lost to time, things that “we cannot forget.” A defiance that yet again reflects her drive in projects to come...
Suzume

Arguably the most important of the covers in Evermore, Suzume marks the first ever entrance of Ina the Hero, more commonly known as Yuusha Ina. Given that Yuusha would go on to star in Abyssal Hymn prominently, it is imperitive to take a closer look at her introduction.

The song itself has a somber tone, the singer recalling another’s heart fondly, a repeating theme scene previously in previous concerts, Violet, and just moments ago in Innocent Blue. Seeking the right words to say that will cut through the wind, they describe time as orderly, the breeze as honest, the stars, young and ignorant.
A universe seemingly devoid of chaos and strife, as if someone has been watching over Ina all along. A being that now asks Ina to forget about them, and embrace the happiness she has been given.
If that is their wish... it isn't working.

In the chorus the singer cries, unable to accept that their encounter with a special individual was meant to be forgotten, erased by time. Their heart still beats, but only when it is moved by another’s hand.

If applied to Yuusha and Ina in general, it might be that despite Temari Ina seemingly giving her a better life, she was still the one who moved her heart, and now she can’t help but go back…
Taking place just after post-chorus 1:
“Even if it’s stupid, even if it’s ugly
In the right direction
I want to move forward, hand in hand with you.”

Verse 2 begins with Ina’s transformation into Yuusha, the lyrics carrying on the story from the first chorus, the singer brought to tears and frustrated, unable to recall the memories they shared. No matter how much they forget, the words they were told still reverberate in their heart, and now, the singer, and likely Ina as well, unable to find solace alone, seeks out the answer for the feeling in their heart.
Even if it's stupid. Even if it's ugly.
It's an answer she needs to know.
The Drawn World

The rest of the songs follow Yuusha's story in the drawn world, a quiet place that has fallen to unforeseen disaster, with lying several hololive members, each one frozen by an unseen threat. However, thanks to her swords/pens, she is able to unfreeze them with a simple touch (a drop of ink?). This might also be similar to her bringing the color back to her world. After freeing each member, Ina would sing and dance alongside with various songs, along with her own solo performances. Of these songs, THREE use an original language, further evidence that Yuusha is not from this world, in similar vain to the concept of “a stranger from another world” that Lumina had in Meconopsis.

After confronting a fierce dragon, that is just visualized as a takodachi with a dragon head on top, Ina is finally able to save the last member with Bae freed! Well, last for now, given her merry attitude as she marches off to save more princesses…
"WHAT? IT WASN't JUST ME!?"
"On to the next one!"
Oh Yuusha Ina, you absolute heartbreaker…

Following this, there is one final performance, with The Brave, a song by Yoasobi made for the Frieren: Journey’s End anime adaptation. Like many of her other songs, it comes from one of her favorite series, though with the added irony of Ina often being compared to Frieren. Although ironically, Yuusha Ina resembles Himmel the hero more if anything, and that may have been the inspiration. Lyrics wise, The Brave is another song focused on a singer who carries on the memories of someone dearly departed, and struggling to understand what they are feeling and experiencing.

Within the context of the Inaverse, this may hint at Ina’s arc, having to find themself and their own meanings in life without someone always there to hold their hand, and may indicate that she’s learning to find the colors for herself.
It seems inevitable she will pursue her counterpart down, but, maybe as herself, not the priestess, and armed with the knowledge of past tales, she will succeed in freeing them.

Overall, throughout Evermore, the themes of wonderland, dreams, and yearning carry forth, Ina wandering into yet another world, led forth by her hollow heart, seeking to find the sound and touch that made it beat. This world too, frozen in time, Ina must return the color.
This time however, it is abundantly clear that Yuusha Ina is not from this world, but reborn, potentially by AO or the Wahtcher, to rewrite their fates.
Yuusha Ina

Ina’s new outfit she revealed for Evermore, Yuusha, also known as Ina the Hero, was an outfit produced by Kuroboshi papa as a gift for reaching 1 million subs. Though Ina hit the mark years before, she hadn’t decided on what she wanted until this outfit.
Unlike her preceding outfits, Yuusha was made as a 3D model rather than a 2D one, and the only one to do so that wasn’t already a  group concert outfit.

Unlike other outfits, Yuusha lays over her default dress, but only from the waist up, acting as an underlayer for her torso. But aside from that, her back wings, and her halo, everything else is brand new.
Design

Probably the most striking and noticeable detail about Yuusha Ina at first, is her color set. Rather than being densely purple with mixes of white, gold, black and flesh as her default priestess model, Yuusha Ina is sheathed in white, a gallant and clean form that feels not out of place in a fantasy anime. The white dress cloaks much of her darker colors underneath, making for both nice vertical contrast, but also thematic contrast. The silver crown, white coat, white boots, and white flowers all form strong shapes that hide her form underneath, the stockier silhouette displaying a more serious individual, but with thin fabrics and frills to showcase her innocence and kindness beneath everything.

Yet, beneath the hero lies the unmistakable past of the priestess, and can be seen where the coat doesn’t reach, leaving her identity exposed to the world like a scar. Overall, the white elements strongly give the impression of Ina being a holy knight, blessed by a deity of light to bring good to the world, infusing holy magic with pure, innocent wonder.

Evidence of this is made clear with the creative uses of takodachis in her outfit, the takos acting as battle armor, forming a squishy shield within a cage around her waist, combining whimsy and magic with purpose.

However, despite the overall light-hearted nature of the outfit, Ina looks even less human here, and combined with her exposed torso, gives the impression that she accepts who she is, human or not, so long as she’s a hero.

The purpose is made doubly clear in her right arm. Cloaked in white flowers as if wreathed in magic, dark purple armor sprouts forth from her coat like a monstrous limb. Hard and metallic, the shape provides additional evidence of Yuusha Ina’s growth and transformation, yet remains largely rounded, still retaining some of her friendly shapes. Her right hand is by and far the most armored location of all, hiding away delicate flesh for metal that can withstand the labors and actions she must take.

Up higher, her flaps and squishy hair have grown long, giving her the appearance of a rabbit, while the rounded hair buns strongly resemble Pleides Ina. Finally, colorful takos now lie within her boots, using the palette of colors shared by others to light up every step she takes.

Overall, Yuusha Ina is a character born straight from a fairy-tale book. *Potentially literally*. She is a character who has been reborn through past struggles, and now wears her drive and purpose on her body at every moment.
However, the doll-like appearance also plays back into the theme of puppetry and autonomy, and may suggest she is caught between realities.
Yuusha's Flowers

One thing that remains important but difficult to pin down is the sleeve of flowers along Yuusha’s right arm. Each one is white with 4 petals that bend outward, and are decently sized. After much thought however, the most likely candidate are lilacs.

body.text: One of the most striking features are her large, rabbit-ear-like appendages. Combined with her aggressively silver/white coat, one can draw a connection to the Sea Bunny. Sea Bunnies gastropods, drawing a connection to the overlord and their own gastropod connections, specifically a nudibranch. These cute little critters feed on toxic sponges and store the toxins as a defense mechanism. Given Yuusha’s ability to break curses and appearance as a holy knight, it may be that Yuusha finds strength and meaning in helping others with their own curses.
Additionally, Sea Bunnies also feed on algae, sea grass, sea slugs and sea snails, the latter two in particular suggesting that Yuusha might slay the Overlord.
The Dragon

Coinciding with her 2025 birthday live, Ina would also reveal a new outfit! With dyed pink highlights, Ao as an art book, and a fittingly chuuni eyepatch, Ina the chuunibyo has entered! Though, like most other outfits, it appears to have no lore connection.
*At first*.
"Now it is time to reveal, the dragon in my eye!"
After an, overly dramatic pause, Ina would reveal that her left eye was actually pink, and teased at the idea of a dragon being within her.
*Again, silly chuuni stuff, just Ina being goofy, it’s not like Ina teased at things to come months ahead of time before by saying it as a joke right to our faces.*

Come 2026 and post Abyssal Hymn trailer, and a concerning amount of evidence has mounted that at least one priestess has a “dragon” in their eye. This is only further supported by yuusha Ina, who appeared almost simultaneously with chuuni Ina, becoming canon to the Inaverse. Even further, Yuusha directly parallels and has a story with Abyss in [Drawn 2 Dawn], who also has a pink left eye.

This means one thing:
Abyss Ina likely has a “dragon” of sorts within them.
It also means, we can learn more about who Abyss is, by learning about the dragon’s nature.
And fortunately, Evermore would have one single, small song exactly about a dragon’s love.
Love Song of a Certain Dragon

In addition to being one of Fuwawa's favorite songs, To aru ryuu no koi no uta is potentially one of the most important songs to understanding the Inaverse, *if it reflects any degree of her story.* Sung during her Evermore birthday live, it regales the story of a dragon and a hero, driven to fight by their nature, but ultimately in love with one another, fate always guaranteeing they will meet, again and again. All throughout the song, 1 section is repeated 4 times, explaining the dragon's nature:
Within it dwells time itself.
Within it are entrusted wishes.
Within it floats mistake and error.
Within it sleeps the truth.
Within it illusions take form.
Within it is fate’s reflection.
Within it is sealed reason.
Within it is the dragon’s love…

Each line explains the dragons's love, and each line feels awfully close to thematic elements in Abyssal Hymn (especially the japanese lines). The rest of the lyrics give further insight to the relationship between the  hero and dragon.

“A lonely love awakens here between us,
resurrected from ancient times,”
-can be connected to the pull that draws Ina and her counterpart towards each other, time and time again.

“Seeking our connection, my flames erupted.
Destroyed and reborn 
Is your noble curse”

-displays how one is only capable of connecting through destruction, the only gift they have, given by nature. And through their destruction, the hero is destroyed and reborn, time and time again, suggesting that Ina may be one of many, or at the very least, she's been reborn numerous times.

The dragon's only way to connect being through destruction, also connects with several past themes and ideas. The first is the broken pencil, an immediate contrast between creation and destruction, and may exist as a metaphor for the dragon's self-destructive nature.

Another comparison can be made with both the abyss and the ancient ones. The abyss breaks down memories and people, a destroyer not of object, but mind. Though, if you imagined the abyss as dark matter, antimatter, elements that neutralize the real world, you might also see the Abyss's nature as one of destruction, and it cannot help itself. This too, might explain the Ancient Ones, and the desire for any shadows to become human, wishing to create and make, envious of other's gifts, but cursed in their nature to ruin even that.
The second verse recounts more of the story, offering new insight into their relationship.
“My soul is ever so transparent, so noble and true
But still I embrace the original sin,
seeking an immature love, so foolishly”

Lines that can be tied directly to [Abyssal Hymn], particularly when the japanese singing half states “their sins sleep in the void of time.” The romantic (or agape) angle only becomes more intense when the singer mentions a letter being broken down until it can no longer be read, suggesting the singer feels guilt in their love. 
However, within the context of the lyrics, the noble and true soul seems more connected with the hero in the original song. Connecting that to the Inaverse, describes the hero as choosing a destructive love, one that seems unable to change its nature.
Although the line with To aru ryuu no koi no uta could work for either, it just depends: which love is the more immature and unchanging?
A dragon that cannot help but destroy?
Or the hero who never gives up on them?
And who will break first?

“The moonlight now shines upon the two of us,
and our fleeting moments pile up one by one”
-could genuinely fit in so many RE:vision songs, Abyssal Hymn being the most obvious.
“I embraced the whereabouts of our connection with my hands
The end and the beginning
are my memories of the you I love”
In spite of only being able to meet briefly anymore, their bond remains intense after so many rebirths and deaths.

The final verse mashes together the final sections of the first 2, showcasing how one connects through destruction, the other through their hands, a tool that can create and leave beasts in envy.
Leaving only one certainty:
**Fate will always reunite them.**

Ooh, I almost forgot, but we might actually have a connection to an old outfit. Back in 2022, Hololive EN had a kimono relay, and in it, Ina revealed her kimono outfit, complete with the tako siblings on her head and in her hand. But one small detail that is very easy to forget, was that it added a horn toggle that has still never been seen with any other outfit.
"Do you care? Are you aware you're my dearest creations?"
ONE EIGHT, TAKODACHI! ONE EIGHT TAKODACHI! Ina Ina Inaa! Ina Inaaaa!!!

Opening 2026 with a BANG, Ina would release her 4th original song, TakoTakover, right at the start of the year. An ambitious switch up from her first three tracks, TakoTakover is a party anthem for the end of the world, a celebration of chaos, and utter devotion and glee to Ina’s ascension. Gone are the fears and uncertainties, the silent duties, and the rebellious cries.
For instead, Ina has found nirvana as the Overlord, *the most normal girl there ever was.*

In case it wasn’t clear yet, this song is on drugs. And I mean that literally.
An absolutely chaotic whirlwind brought to life by the writing of Mori Calliope, music of Aiboahn, eye-popping graphics by Tellingbones, with additions by Rumskii (who also did the storyboarding to help bring it to life!), Saku’s logo, Lumina’s editing, and of course, Ninomae Ina’nis herself. TakoTakover is a thrill ride from start to finish, that will have you looping again and again and again!

And again!
And again!
And a- i
Agai-
Ina i-
A- ga- ina!
Ad-

Ina Ina Ina
Ina Inaaa!!!
Meta

This time around, art and animation was largely handled by Tellingbones, the same artist who made the animations for Evermore! The main concept was to be catchy, addicting, and fun to listen to, but still with the darker undertones we know and love in the Inaverse.
“Tako Takover is an ending.”
“The true end is already out… kukuku.” - Laughing and smiling.
Responses to chat would give more hints at how Takover linked with the rest of the Inaverse, describing it as an ending, and *not a good one*.
“So tako takeover is a bad ending- IT IS! You’d have no more world anymore! No more streams, I’d be too famous! It’s TakOVER.”

Though played for laughs, Ina's response also highlights the titular character of the song. Rather than remaining the earnest, down to earth, passionate creator we know her for, Takover is a global celebrity, too busy running the world to enjoy the small things anymore. Thus, Takover depicts first and foremost, a loss of self.
THE OVERLORD

It is IMPOSSIBLE to even begin Tako Takover without first bringing up the aggressive contrast between this ina, and all previous ones. Rather than being shy, anxious, and full of uncertainty, the overlord is bold, aggressive, and hyper-confident. LONG gone is the girl who was afraid of stepping into a colorful world, now exists the girl who colors the world on her own, an absolute diva that craves attention and worship. As Ina herself would tease about it being a bad end cause she’d “be on too many talk shows, I’d be too busy!” One can think of TakoTakover, on a meta level, as an Ina who fully lost herself, seeking attention and fame, attempting to be the center of the universe. Sure, the takodachis worship and kneel before her out of adoration, but it was a forced adoration to a woman Ina never cared to be…
“Divine Omen || And they worshipped her with absolute adoration”

In the end, Ina (likely the first priestess) became exactly what the Ninomae family sought. A god that would allow them to sleep in a blissful dream, and her friend’s worst nightmare, a girl who had a soul all along, becoming the puppet of a [laughing god].
Design

Out of every Ina MV design to come out so far, Takover is BY FAR the most eye-popping immediately, in no small part thanks to her inhuman elements mentioned above. But even beyond the wings, the stalks, and the infection, the very colors and design of Takover scream her alien nature. Her outfit is bombastic, seductive, and playful, split between emphasizing her own body shape, appealing to curiosity, and making her intimidating. Take for instance the sleeves. Beginning at the shoulders, they remain baggy as they rise down the bicep before being pinched together like a trapezoid, giving them an enlarged sense of gravity.

Its role as a flashy weapon and taunt is further emphasized by the fact that the only part where the dress is cut above the hips is her very own armpits, using her own skin to draw attention back to her face. The sleeves roll further down her arms and flare out, this time with a second layer underneath that expands like flower petals before her sleek gloves. The under-layer draws in the eye with its curved shape, drawing takos and other prey alike towards her lithe hands. All the while, contrast emphasizes every small detail, with many light and dark parts placed together in a way to draw in prey.

Meanwhile, the torso itself is slim, sleek, and extremely short, dangerously teasing length that gives additional presence to her long and exposed legs. Said legs are adorned with mirrored black and white boots that appear so tight that they could be mistaken for tights (probably some AO magic), and without any single feature from ankle to dress, their long, smooth length are excellent for emphasizing her movement. The only thing upon them? Her own platforms at the end, each giving her additional height, are rounded into pairs of circles, mirroring a figure eight, and also retaining some playful energy.

Should you take the bait and follow her legs up, you will be greeted by her dress again, and thereafter, asymmetric patterns and nonsensical shapes that first draw in the curious eye. These strange designs, along with the bright waves in the center, accentuate her body shape and drive up the sexiness, giving her hips and waist a stronger impression on the victi- I mean viewer. This strategy carries on up her torso as the bright colors below give way to an abyssal darkness along her spine, spilling out yet again to give her lithe curves additional presence. However, here another detail takes center stage, with the bright purple and red of the eye on her chest proudly displaying her deep connection with the void/AO, unashamed of who she is. A false, glitzy confidence that comes from illusion rather than her own heart, allowing her to only become a desired idol by allowing someone else to play her part.

In this way, the darkness of the dress married with splashes of color, shows how not only AO/the family has their desires wrapped even tighter around Ina, but also how they have turned her very colors into utility and functions meant only to make further gains.

And of course, in spite of all the allure and appeal, a more cautious glance at her very face reveals just how far she is gone. Pale and monochrome, the Overlord's skin lacks the warmth of a normal girl, more fitting of a ghost or the undead. Proof that whatever walks and sings in Ina's body, is no longer her.
Rainbows and Colors
As far as color goes in Ina's work, TakoTakover is maybe her most interesting yet, displaying a dazzling array of different colors throughout, rather than one dominating the entire MV.

First and foremost, rather than Violet, Ina suggests Purple as the color of this song. Whereas Violet is soft and calming, befitting of meditation, Purple is bold and deep, a display of strength. This goes back to color theory, as in the past, purple was a difficult color to produce, so it was often associated with royalty and power, which fits perfectly given the Overlord’s monarch-like status.

Following that, Black is one of the strongest elements in the Overlord’s design, cloaked in the presence of the abyss. Yet she also has splashes of white with her wings and crown, giving her divine grace. Combine this with her white and black boots, and you get the sense that two contrasting identities, one of the abyss and one of the heavens, have been merged. 
And the colors don't stop there.

A sickly yellow is among the most obvious, her normally golden squishies looking pale, and matching her yellow pupils. Each are a sign of her actual deteriorating condition, especially with the eyes as the window to the soul suggesting this takeover is harming Ina inside.
There are also splashes of red on the dress and blue rings  to add variety, and if you stretched it, could be a reference to Temari and Meconopsis.
Pink is another color that appears aggressively, and in fact, *might be the guilty culprit.*

You see, the Wahtcher’s main colors are pink and white, and throughout Takover, much of her body is covered in polka dots, the most prominent of which are pink. Up at the top right stalk, where the tako sits in her head, it is dyed pink, bumps appearing on her like a rash. The neon pink adds an additional flair to gain attention, and gives her some false warmth that isn't her own. Further down, the white boots also feature polka dots, adding further indication that The wahtcher, or whoever they are (if this is timeline 1 and not a definitive ending), is the vector to which the virus spread into Ina.

Finally, all throughout the song, the Overlord is doused in rainbow light, emanating her godly strength. This also ties her in to the poppy sequence in Meconopsis, and the end of chorus 1 in Temari. This might indicate a connection between those moments with the overlord, and given the context of those scenes, reinforces that rainbows represent transformation.
An array of Inas

The color theory doesn't stop with just the Overlord either, as during the second chorus, we get a hint at multiple Ina's within the Overlord as she prays. The scene transitions from Violet and her stars, to Meconopsis and her petals,  to Temari and the red sigil, each one bathed in their own signature color. Playing off of the the earlier color discussion, it adds evidence that the Overlord might be a fusion of all the previous Ina's...

The sequence finally concludes with the Overlord lies in a black void surrounded by points of light, while a rainbow coils around her. Together, it conveys both the overlord's connection with the void, but also that they may have overtaken any other gods, the divine rainbow not just a sign of enlightenment, but of her connection with a higher power. The connection of the other 3 Ina's with her suggests that they are tied to the Overlord in some aspect, and might even be subject to her spell, if not outright pacified by her own call, a mesmerizing fantasy that can even bring other priestesses to heel.
Zombie Snail Virus

Ina’s flaps are no longer little octopus flaps, but THICK, cone-shaped stalks that resemble nudibranches or even Sea angels, both of which are aquatic gastropods. One of these bloated stalks is also covered in pink polka dots, and given the takodachi brain slugs we see later, it becomes pretty apparent the overlord is infected.

This is given a more direct connection later, when Ina attempts to hypnotize takodachis, and the stalks begin to shift between colors. This behavior, as Ina herself would later state was intentional, mimics that of the zombie snail virus: Leucochloridium variae. In real life, this strain of parasitic flatworms gets into snail bodies, and mimic insect larva to attract birds, who pick at the stalks, and then the virus is transmitted into their body. Within the birds bodies, the worms life cycle continues, adults releasing their eggs within the intestines to continue the cycle. While the snail host may not die from the stalk infection, intense infection within birds can lead to emaciation, and death, and they may also freeze to death due to lacking adipose tissue.

In addition to the overlord being infected, this also gives us some hint as to how it travels, likely through digestion and eating something infected. But instead of worms, it of course is the void. This gains additional evidence from later in the song, as Ina describes making and eating takoyaki, suggesting not only how the fate of many perished, but further reinforcing that the tako snail virus eventually becomes self-sustaining.
Sea Angel
Though Ina still overall retains her octopus theming, there is another that is noticeable throughout the MV: The sea angel.

Sea angels are aquatic gastropods, sharing a class with snails in the animal kingdom. Translucent and ethereal, they flap about with floaty wings, not unlike how the overlord floats through a purple abyss near the end of the MV. Even her hair mimics the floaty movement! But beyond all of that, the wings growing from her head are the most literal appearance we’ve had of an angel yet, and adds emphasis to her divine power.
Sea Dragon?

Another possible option, Nudibranches are another form of Gastropod, and include a member named the Blue Sea Dragon. Though the colors and appearance are closer to Meconopsis, if anything, the stalks are quite similar in shape. Even more intriguing, these creatures feed on men’o war, who are rather similar to [Jellyfish], and [Violet snails]. Given Ina's multiple mentions of dragons previously, and the name "Watatsumi" (which sometimes refers to the Dragon God of the sea, Ryujin), it has some degree of possibility.
Takodachis: Living Soul Jars

Among the many scenes throughout the MV, we finally get a section that reveals the takodachis as more than they seem. Following a nun taking Ina’s hand, whether by choice or force, we see her in a new room that mimics a video game character creation screen, with takodachis changing the woman’s appearance. With a takodachi latched onto their head, the girl mutates, her arms and legs transforming into tentacles, and gaining another 8 to resemble an octopus. The process looks painful at first, but after she gains new eyes like the overlord, she stops resisting, displaying the takodachis have mind altering abilities.

Given that many later takos exist without a host, it is heavily implied that takodachis are able to store and become the containers for living souls. This would further imply that takodachis seen in other songs, especially Abyssal Hymn, contain the souls of other characters.
Following their transformation of sight and mind into accepting their takodachi bodies, the takodachis join along with the overlord in spreading wahrld domination, chanting and cheering along.

The chant “I will become a good takodachi to protect my Ina's timeline” suggests that the Takover timeline may be self-aware and defensive, possibly facing an existential threat from outside. However, given The Overlord's own deity like status, this might also make Takover an existential threat to the rest of the Inaverse.
That would also help to explain the second priestesses actions and regret, attempting to subvert fate and creating/becoming the Wahtcher to warn others/stop the Overlord.
"My Dearest Creations"

At one point during the song, we cut to a first person POV, showing a white-silhouette character with blue outlines being approached by The Overlord, trying to convince them to join the party. Instead, we refuse and run down the hall of an ornate mansion soaked in dark colors and red, illuminated only by dim neon pink windows above. Along the way, we pass by 4 art frames, and finally reach the red room at the end of the hall. Within it, we accidentally wake up a colorless Ina awake, her skin a cold blue, eyes red with purple pupils, cradling two takodachis (although we only see one's actual face…).

With the line stated above, the Ina turns and grabs us, and instantly the MV REDSCREENS, filled up with white text stating: [       ] IMMINENT INITIATE [    ] PROTOCOL. We can reasonably assume the words to be some variation of tako takover, and shows just how busted Ina is at this point, able to transform anyone with just a touch.

Additionally, the girl within the dark room might be a reference to Temari, the red screen, room, and eyes all sharing her visual atmosphere. Given the line of takos being her dearest creations and the design of Ina in the [happy birthday] drawing being Temari’s at a younger age, it can be reasonably assumed that the creations Ina speaks of are referring to the [first takodachi].

THEORY:
Assuming that Ina’s friend was taken to the void in Temari, it might be that Ina resurrected her dearest friend as her dearest creation, and in doing so, proved her worth, becoming the celebrated head of the Ninomae family.
Though, it is worth mentioning that Ina referred to “Creations”, as in multiple, and in the shot above, we see 2 takodachis…
Both Inanis'? Ina and her shadow? Multiple timelines? Violet and Meconopsis? Who knows... maybe you have a thought?
Digital Demon

Among the myriad of abilities we see throughout Tako Takover, comes the ability to jump between TV screens and media. Now, at first this may just be a fun gag to emphasize how much larger than life the overlord is. Yet, earlier that year in a teaser for the Fortune Spinner Myth 5th anniversary, Ina was able to travel through the computer screen. Knowing this, the rampant ascent of Tako-Takover makes sense, and fits nicely on a meta level with streaming and being an idol. Ina is no longer the shy, nervous girl afraid of her own voice, she is now on every screen, every device, spreading throughout the digital world like a virus.
Crown of the Goddess

Sitting atop the Overlord’s head is a crown with 5 ridges. Rather than wearing it across her bangs like a hairband, she displays it proudly like a monarch, the deigned ruler of this world. The 5 rulers may also be a hint at the overlord being a fusion of multiple souls. Which, given their colors and hints, it’s likely Violet Ina, Meconopsis Ina, Temari Ina, the Wahtcher, and Past Ina. This would also get us Violet, Blue, Red, White/Pink, and Black/White, all of the colors adorning the Overlord's design.
False Sisters/Nuns

Though really only existing because Tellingbones has a toxic yuri agenda (thank you), there are actually a lot of interesting connections to making Ina’s counterparts a cult of corrupted sisters. The most striking and immediate of course is to Temari, which suggested that the friend Ina has been seeking all this time is a “sister” she had in the Ninomae family. Now, much like religious families like the catholic nuns the corrupted sisters are based on, the name is not literal, but refers more to their status as sharing a special bond with each other and their faith/god, and reinforces again that Ina and her friend had a similar relationship. Both born into a secretive “family” that used them as “twins” in paired ritual sacrifices, despite being raised to only care about her duties, Past Ina clearly felt a strange bond with her sisters, and especially her “twin”.
However, through their duties and fate, their important connection would be fractured, and seeking to fill that hole in their heart, the first tako was born.

Now The Overlord picks up where that Inanis left off, turning the entire world into the sister that she lost with the takodachi, the creature she seemingly rescued her as. In seeking out that irreplaceable bond, she has accidentally become the very deity her family always wanted, while still wishing to be a normal girl deep down.
A future that was stolen from her, and her sister.
