However, whether it is coincidence or intentional, local tako, Sunfish_blue, mentioned a flower that looked remarkably similar to the eyes of Ina and the sisters. Its name: the breadseed poppy.
Also known as the Opium Poppy.

Papaver Somniferum is the full name, somniferum literally meaning “sleep bringing.” The flowers have been used since ancient times as both medicine, food, and drugs, the ancient Sumerians even referring to it as the “Joy plant.” Humans considered the drug to have “healing properties”, thanks in part to the pain relieving qualities of opium. However, the drug is also a sedative, relating back to its name as a sleep-bringer, decreasing the brain’s activity and reducing any irritation and excitement. This gives additional evidence to the overlord being the individual who sends others into a blissful slumber. The drug also has a historical context of being addictive, and given the mind-wiped sisters that adore Ina, yeah, the entire world being on a giant Ina overdose is meant in a very literal way.

Also worth mentioning, is that the poppy seeds themselves are sometimes used in food, and while not having the same quality of effect as the medicine in small amounts, reinforces the idea that the overlord used poisoned food to infect and spread her influence.

Finally, the very name and nature refers back to [Meconopsis] in several ways. First, and most obvious, is that both are poppies, and even helps to explain why the JP singing lyrics are calling out to Ina, calling her to return to her slumber. Meconopsis also stands out further as a result, being the one who was able to break free from a world buried in an abyssal dream. The nature of infection and ingestion also ties in with the warnings to [NOT INGEST] within the MV, and tying back in with [Takodachis as living soul jars] and the [Zombie snail virus], and we start to understand how Ina changed.
Which leaves one question.
How did the tako get inside?
Two sparkles melt into one

Prior to Tako Takover's release, in late November 2025 takodachis and KFP alike were caught by surprise by a shared announcement. First: The release of Kiara's 2nd album, Vogelfrei, and Ina's first EP Re:Vision. The second, and even more exciting, was the announcement of their first ever duo-live, finally performing on stage live on their own before a crowd!
The concert itself wouldn't be until late March 2026, but fans would be treated in the meantime to the releases of both Vogelfrei, and of course, Re:Vision.
The story of Ninomae Ina'nis

Concluding a story years in the making, Ina would discuss in a follow-up stream that RE:vision would conclude and cap off the story started long ago in Violet, and with it, reveal more answers to the Inaverse.
Prior to the release, Ina would discuss the album cover art, drawn by herself, and give fresh hints at her brewing story.

The original sketch was quite a bit different from the final rendition, showing multiple figures walking through picture frames/CD covers, each one arranged like the spokes of a giant gear amid other gears. From the foreground, a massive hand from our point-of-view opens it open like the pages of a book. From the few details, we can make out the figures of multiple inas/sisters, starting from a young girl holding a Temari on the left side, while an older Ina moves through the pages to the right.

Counting each individual Ina, you get 5… + 1, you, the viewer, your very own hand opening the page as if you were one of the characters themselves. Perhaps even the Watcher. That makes for a total of 6.
If each page represents a different universe or location, it may suggest one is moving through worlds, while the others can see between worlds.

However, Ina didn’t feel strongly enough about it, and was hit with inspiration, designing the rough for what would become the final piece.
“And this one is easier to see, it's just a gallery and Ina is walking through with the tentacles coming out.”
“And if you look with a blurred eye, you might be able to see what I was going for with the lighting.”
"Cthullu shaped- YEAH!"

Within the light negative space around Ina, you can see the form of cthullhu within the paint, surrounding Ina. Interestingly, by the final version, the lighting and colors, pink and white, resemble the Wahtchers, but upon further inspection, it might actually refer to the mixture of different individuals: Blue, purple/violet, red, pink, and white.

The shape becomes a bit more clear in the final version of the background without the priestess and tentacles, Cthullu's shape distinctly white surrounded by a mixture of red, violet, and dark blue to black within a picture frame. The silhouette of Cthullu being white hints that the Wahtcher is tied with them in some fashion, while the surrounding colors resemble the strange red realms seen in both Temari, and later in AByssal Hymn.

In conclusion, the cover art teases at picture frames and paintings acting as portals or playing a major role within the Inaverse, and directly refers to Cthullhu. The framing appears to suggest Ina is looking for something, potentially unaware of the danger, followed by a looming shadow that seeks for her in turn. It’s hard to know for sure what she is thinking though, her expression is uncertain, hinting that she is still stuck between her priestess duties, and something in the distance, something that has caught her attention...
Abyss Ina

Along with Drawn 2 Dawn's unveiling came a new design, whom after the design Ina would call "the Abyss outfit." Though it would be months until we got any clues to her place in the story, the key visual alone told a thousand stories.

First and foremost, without a shadow of a doubt, Abyss Ina has an overt connection with Temari. Just like the head priestesses in Temari, Abyss wears a Haori, but this one is a slight bit lighter, more of a gray mauve/lavender with a charcoal dress underneath, as opposed to Temari’s clean charcoal haori. The sleeves are covered in an ornate pattern of temaris, threads, and stars, proudly displaying her past.

This time however, she is outfitted with high boots that almost go up to her knees, proving that she now has the strength and will to walk on her own two feet, and has begun to explore the world on her own terms. Further up the leg, a ring of stars around her thigh mark a departure from every other Ina design, both in and out of the Inaverse, resembling a marking as if from magic (or a tattoo if you so desire).

Around here we also reach the beginning of the haori’s front side, this time with more cuts to show the ornate red, interwoven circles underneath. Again, the increased coloration displays she has grown some amount since Temari, with the red of the coat framing her more revealed body. Whether this is a sign of AO's increasing influence, Ina discovering herself as her monochrome past faces, or some combination of the two (falling to strong, intense emotions as she explores the world?) may depend on your own reading of Abyss within the Inaverse at large.

Looking up her coat, both left and right halves now feature 4 sided stars, 8 in total, twice on the front and twice behind, for a total of 32 stars. These begin black, but turn pink with glowing eyes inside whenever she uses her powers, suggesting she is working with another party (The Dragon, AO, the Wahtcher?). At the top of her chest, her eye emblem is displayed front and center, the eye in a ring of circles and looking forward, suggesting that whatever lies within is now able to be fully awakened. Several white strings tied around both her arms and to her sides add to her experienced appearance, and suggests she has been the head of the cult for some time.

From underneath her dress appears a silver olive branch, tied to both the front and back of her inner outfit by a star within a moon. Historically, olive branches have deep symbolic meaning, relating with peace, eternal life, healing, and protection. Even further, silver is often seen as having divine qualities, seen as more pure than gold and having deep spiritual meaning. It is also connected with the moon. Given that Abyss Ina is heavily tied with the ocean, this might mean the silver branch is a gift. Or, it might be Abyss’s way of enhancing her connection with the moon.

Finally, her coat sleeves feature a takodachi instead of temari at their ends, hinting at not only their parallel roles as soul containers, but also displaying that abyss is a transformed priestess, or one utterly unseen yet.

As for her head, Abyss has several unique qualities, the most striking of which being her pink/red hair on the inside, again hinting at the idea that Abyss is a fusion of two individuals, while matching the creeping transformation appearing from her dress. Abyss's hair length and shape is also about as direct of a connection to Temari’s hairstyle as you can get, cutting aside the painful weight of her past and duties, and returning to a nostalgic place of comfort. That, or she’s outright past Ina/friend, but she looks a good bit older.

She also wears a crown/5 star headpiece, only seen on the heads of Yuusha and priestess Ina (which we would only see in Abyssal Hymn), further connecting her with not just the the sisters of the cult, but the other crowned Ina's. Given we don't see Wahtcher wearing said crown, it might indicate that Abyss herself is an alternate version of our very own priestess, one where she stayed in the cult.
And of course, the glowing pink [dragon] eye makes its grand return, further suggesting that she is connected with the wahtcher or another empowered being in some fashion.

Either way, Kuroboshi papa gave us a wonderful first impression of our new Ina, more sleek, eye-popping, and modern than her predecessors, showing that she has matured from her early cult days. Well, at least literally. After all, she still rules a realm of takodachis, as we finally get a glimpse of her world behind a grey picture frame, potentially acting as a portal as mentioned in the sketches above. She floats among twelve 6-sided stars, beneath a misty night sky and waning crescent moon. 
Behind her, little takodachis march before a pink shrine, and behind it, a massive takodachi stretches into the sky, dwarfing everything below.

All together, Abyss is the new priestess on the block, sleek, modern, and with a bit of sass, almost looking a bit rebellious. Her design combines elements from multiple worlds and forms, and given Ina herself said Abyssal Hymn is a rainbow of colors, suggests that Abyss Ina has an array of emotions and love within her, just waiting to burst out from her.
After all, black paint is simply all the colors of the rainbow mixed into one. And soon, they would be set free.

body.text: The Moon and the Deep Sea

March 2026 would mark an important point in the life of both Ninomae Ina’nis and her many adoring takodachis, finally taking the stage in her very own live concert, alongside fellow Hololive Myth member Takanashi Kiara. After years of trials and growth, Ina found support and courage in the friends around her, and now it was her time to shine.
And shine she did, from a moonlit stage atop a magic book, to the abyssal depths beside a seaside city at night, Two Ina’s would dominate Drawn 2 Dawn:
**Yuusha and Abyss.**

Throughout the concert, Ina would reveal more and more surprises for the audience, and amidst them all, the duality of the Inas stood out in particular. One of the heavens, and one of the deep. Both with two outfits. One bound to the moon, while the other? The very waves pulled by the moon.
Though it is uncertain if the story told between the two here carries any serious consequences for the Inaverse, it is nonetheless invigorating and worth diving into.
*(Author’s note: As of now, Abyssal Hymn MV has released, and may deviate greatly from what is told here. But for now, I will write it as I had previously planned.)*
Now let’s begin our tale, of the girl on the moon, and the one who chased the moon.
Iconography
Prior to the start of each concert’s half, one for Kiara, one for Ina, the singer would have an intro, each one stylized to the performer.

The first displays a waxing crescent moon within a white lotus, teasing at an awakening power. The rings in the center, surrounded by radial lines, mimics the appearance of an eye, and in doing so, connects the waxing, growing moon with her own oncoming transformation and growth.

After a few overlapping animations and 4 spinning lines of light (probably nothing tbh), the scene would then transition into the image of a waning moon imbued with an 8-pointed star, while threads radiate out. The screen flashes once more, and ends by transitioning to the Drawn 2 Dawn cover art by Kurobochi papa, fully outfitted in her Abyss attire. The transition of the moon from a waxing crescent to a waning one both reflects the lyrics:
The waxing moon excites my wanderlust - The waning moon vanishes into the dark
-Bringing everything full circle, and suggesting that Abyss is the opposite side of the same coin, the waning moon Ina has been chasing all along.

The image of the star and moon merged might also be a call back to the symbols scene in chorus 1 of Temari, as there we saw an 8 sided star and crescent moon, both of which were weeping. Here we also see numerous threads encircling the symbol, each half mirroring the other, adding on to the theme of duality present throughout.

And of course, the threads themself call back to Temari, and will later call forward to Abyssal Hymn. Given their role within the Inaverse as weaving memories into new forms, these threads may represent two different souls being bound together. if not the means through which they can connect.

Though the intro sequence is seemingly ignorable in the grand scheme of things, the first appearance of the mixed sun and moon along with the threads makes it more than worth noting before we dive in further.
Yuusha Ina

Making her grand return to singing, along with her first on live audience appearance, Yuusha Ina kicked off Ina's performance during day 1, the stalwart hero arriving in her full outfit. Though as the songs progressed, she would shimmy down to her coatless form, and in doing so, revive the appearance of a ballet dancer.
Along with Yuusha's opening act and varied performances was a unique background, using different elements from Ina's lore, and putting some front and center.
The Moon

With Drawn 2 Dawn, Ina’s moon symbolism takes center stage… literally. Throughout all of her performances, the moon lies behind Ina, a waning crescent both near and far. During the first half of day 1, during Yuusha’s performances, it lies close, suggesting Yuusha has a close connection with the moon in particular.

Now, within culture, the moon often has a deep spiritual meaning as our closest heavenly body, and can be seen as the realm of the gods. This may further reveal that Yuusha has a divine connection or link.
The rabbit
The moon also brings Yuusha’s more rabbit-like qualities into even greater focus, particularly connecting to tales and beliefs of the rabbit on the moon.

One in particular from buddhism, recounts how a god descended to Earth, disguised as a beggar, and came across some animals. Without giving away his identity, the beggar asked the animals for some food. Each animal brought something different for the man, but when it reached the rabbit’s turn, they realized they had nothing to offer. Thus, the rabbit threw itself onto the fire, offering itself for the beggar to eat. The god was so touched by this act, that he pulled the rabbit out of the fire, and brought it with him to the moon.

If this is the inspiration, it suggests that Yuusha may have sacrificed themselves for others, and was saved by a higher being. This further ties in with the idea of Yuusha being gifted by the divine, and ties in with her heroic valor.
Another connection may be that the rabbit on the moon is a sign of rebirth and new beginnings, and this heavily connects with the themes of rebirth and time-travel throughout the inaverse.
The stars

Alongside the moon are many stars, each just as gold and radiant, showering Ina in a heavenly atmosphere. The infusion of stars only furthers the connection Yuusha has with the celestial realm, and ties back to several previous performances.

The first and most obvious being Pleides, in which Ina sang and danced within a music box full of stars, a tiny little universe just for her.  Given Lumina mentioned Ina as a traveller in [Meconopsis] and the use of language and fonts to describe the girls in different ways, the stars surrounding Yuusha continue to suggest is from another world in some aspect.

Following up on the tale of the rabbit and the moon, it may be that Yuusha was reborn through celestial intervention or power, perhaps a gift for actions taken in her past. Which would, after all, befit her being a hero.
Pages and Frames

Much like her debut in [Evermore], Yuusha Ina appears upon the pages of a book throughout her performances. Again, this detail can tie her in with Meconopsis, with both describing their Ina's as being created to some degree. In Meconopsis, the blue flower represented a rare strength, with Ina even describing it as not-natural/synthetic.
On the flip-side, Yuusha almost appears to be a divine creation, a fairy-tale character brought to life, literally walking out of a book. Imagery that was used multiple times in Evermore as well.

Finally, the inclusion of the picture frames ties Yuusha in with the cover of Re:vision, where Ina stood in front of one, as well as Tako Takover, where we saw multiple frames before encountering Temari Ina with her "dearest creations." And of course, how could we overlook the pencil in both Violet and Temari?

Again, multiple implications. First of course, is that Yuusha was somehow created by a past Inanis. Second, is that the individual who would one day become Inanis is present in all of these scenes. Otherwise, each Ina might all be born from their own unique stories.
Third, given the cover of Re:Vision, it is reasonable to imagine that these frames may act as gateways of some sort, possibly connecting with the mirror imagery in other videos.

Finally, and most interesting, is that in the Re:vision cover, it is Cthullu, bathed in white, that seems to call for Ina. Given multiple mentions of "misty dreams" and wonderland in other performances, Yuusha might be chasing illusions. That, or she is the very one trapped in wonderland that the other Inanis has been chasing.
Concluding thoughts on Yuusha's theming
Overall, while the actual direct meaning of Yuusha's themes and their purpose may vary, what those themes are seem rather consistent.
Rebirth: From the rabbit on the moon to various connections to other performances, Yuusha is very likely a reincarnation of another Ina.
Heavenly connection: Along with the moon, she is surrounded by stars, and seems to have been empowered by cosmic magic.

Synthetic creation: From her very introduction through default Ina in Evermore to here with the pages and frames, there is a running theme that Yuusha was brought to life through artificial means rather than born naturally.
Day 1 songs: Meconopsis and Temari

Ina’s section in drawn 2 dawn would begin with Meconopsis, Yuusha taking to the stage before a waxing gold crescent moon, atop a book with two picture frames behind her. The song’s visuals were adorned with the titular flower, and the crowd became a sea of blue.

Yuusha would follow up with Temari, sporting the song's signature red visuals, all the while cult imagery played in the background. In particular, the pre-chorus would display a white screen being filled red, symbolizing the presence of something awakening. The rest of the song carried on in familiar manner to her Pleides and All For One performances, although, I can’t help but mention that takos joined in chanting during the third verse, as if the crowd had become a cult performing a ritual. In the theater, the sound was actually quite loud, and though she didn’t ask for it, it made for a very cool experience (and ironically, tied in with Abyssal Hymn months later).
Tsuki no Waltz

Ina’s 3rd song and first cover of the evening, Tsuki no Waltz stands out deeply from its peers. As she would later go on to explain, Ina chose this song the moment she saw the design, and even had Mikyuki sensei learn how to dance, helping our lovely priestess waltz with elegant ballerina moves. All the while, her cover of choice feels eerily fitting to the Inaverse upon a closer inspection. So let's get lost in the motion of transformation and love alongside her...
*WORD OF CAUTION: A looot of this is me finding connections with an already existing song she chose, and may not be factual. That said, wow I can make a looooot of connections with Tsuki no Waltz.*

Dancing and performing before the moon without the coat, Yuusha Ina resembled a ballet dancer waltzing through the heavens. Whilst colored in bright pink and cyan amidst golden stars and frames, both the song and dance appeared to make a callback to pleiades, beginning from the start with a wind-up music box intro and carrying on into Ina’s dancing.

However, Yuusha Ina’s movements were robotic, limbs and arms moving like a mechanical doll rather than a living being, suggesting Yuusha may be a puppet of something greater beyond. Not helping the matter, Tsuki no Waltzes lyrics feel deeply connected with the idea of a wonderland, with the singer lost deep in a forest, and encountering characters reminiscent of fairy tales.
For example, take the second verse.
A rabbit in a tuxedo comes
He leads me to a table and offers me wine
Underneath the scarlet umbrella of a mushroom
The dance begins

The rabbit of course appears to be Yuusha, still acting just as chivalrous within this wonder-land like setting. Together, the singer and Yuusha take cover under a red mushroom, a very direct connection to Ina's red wagasa, which appears to represent AO's influence. Thus, it may be that the singer and Yuusha are communicating through AO.

Of course, one can also read it a bit darker. After all, mushrooms are symbolic for illusions and psychedelics, which isn't too far off from the theming in TakoTakover. Not helping the matter, mushrooms feed on dead organic matter, and it might be that Yuusha or the very singer herself is a departed soul from the living.
Though, given Yuusha appears to have multiple souls in Abyssal Hymn, it might be that one Ina is actually trapped within AO-chan, perhaps even using the book to fuse themselves together.
As the two waltz together however, a set of lines feels eerily familiar.
Where are you? I'm lost in the land of time
I can't find my way back
Even though I'm waiting, waiting

A voice waiting in a land lost beyond time directly connects to the Wahtcher's entire motif, from the messages in Abyssal Hymn, to vocals in Takodachi no Uta, and even her introduction in the April Fool's stream. She is waiting. "As always."
Which of course, would imply the one seeking her is our Ina.
This sleepless soul
Enters the forest, looking for you
The Prince of Chandra Mahal (the Palace of the Moon)
Kneels and invites me to waltz

The singer's sleepless state suggests Ina is haunted by her memories, yet the forest shows that she no longer knows the way forward. The prince of Chandra Mahal, on the other hand, is implied to be the very person she is searching for.

The singer goes on to describe butterflies dancing in dresses and beetles dancing with swords, mimicking the pageantry and roles of princesses and princes. All the while, their conversation continues.
What do you long for? The labyrinth of temptation
Beyond the milk-colored fog
An overt resemblance to "Beyond the Void", sealed away and hidden from her sight.
I want a reliable love

Finally, the reason behind Ina's entire quest. connecting back again with Yuusha's first appearance in Suzume, where she sought the answer to her beating heart. Now she understands what she felt before, and dives into the fog again and again to bring them back.

This suggestion is only further exacerbated by the singer immediately wrapping their cold fingers in the feathers of a swan right after. The cold fingers exemplify the warmth that has left her life. More enticing however, is her choice of warmth.

For those unaware, swans tend to symbolize both fidelity and lasting monogamous love, forming bonds long before maturing that last for life. Given that throughout all of Re:vision the two constantly seem to be driven by their desire to see each other again, it would appear that their unbreakable bond began when they were both young girls within the cult, and has only grown more intense with time and distance.

To which, the "Prince of Chandra Mahal" laughs, and the singer finds their eyes remind them of the person they are looking for. Within RE:Vision and especially Abyssal Hymn, this directly states the very person they are looking for is right before them the whole time, but no longer recognizable. Thus, leading to Ina getting lost in Wonderland, chasing after foggy memories of someone who is no longer there.
"The mystic ship that travels the cosmos
Waxes then wanes
It tells us that,
Nothing stays the same"
Given the prince is implied to represent the friend/Wahtcher Ina has been looking for all along, she leaves a couple of clues for both Ina and the audience.

The waxing and waning reflects the very moon that is seemingly tied to them both, suggesting both a beginning and an end, further tying Ina's connection with the phases and the moon as different transitions in her life. And of course, "Nothing stays the same" refers to the entire nature of the Inaverse, the cycle of growth, death, and rebirth that encircles them.

To grow and defy their destiny, they had to go throw a transformation that has left them unrecognizable at first, yet is still the same soul Ina seeks deep down. Now they tease the answer before Ina, that they too will not just have to transform, but to except that reality.

The song then concludes with the same verse as the first repeated twice, but with differences to the first and especially the second. The first now describes the "deep forest" as an "unfamiliar forest," possibly implying that Ina has been reborn after this encounter. Otherwise, she may have briefly entered "Beyond the Void", meeting the Wahtcher, but as she hinted at long ago, Ina would be unable to remember this encounter when she returned. As for the second:
On nights when the moon is this blue
Strange things happen
To love is to trust
I dreamed that someday
I could sleep in your arms

Thus, in order to meet the one she loves again, Ina will need to trust in the strangers voice, and accept that change and transformation are natural. Both who for they are now, and for Ina's own self, that way she may grow and escape her fate.
Only once they've both learned to accept change and grow, their hearts will finally be able to reunite.
And then they will finally find rest again.
Gunjou

Gunjou would return again for day 1 of Drawn to Dawn, this time, joined by a choir of takodachis joining in! The general thematic remains the same, Ina finding the strength to show her colors, but this time, the crowd played the backing chorus, the voices of the fans who watched her journey now singing for her to let her colors shine!

Thus, if this is a part of Ina's story, it is the voices and support of all the people around her who help her to not only transform, but to accept her own self, giving her the strength to move forward.
Following Gunjou, the remaining 4 songs would all be sung by Abyss Ina, so let's move onto day 2 for the remainder of Yuusha's songs.
Day 2: Tako Takover

Much to the delight of fans at the concert, Yuusha Ina would kick off day 2 with a bang, arriving with a waxing crescent moon unveiling backwards, the light revealing our hero. Before she could even finish singing the first word, the crowd was already screaming. And thus, day 2 began with a cult rave performed by the hero of all people.

Amidst a sea of purple, the crowd chanted along loud enough to fill the entire theater, and Ina was all the more willing to give them an explosive performance, not letting down until she was snapped away by the static of a tv turning off at the end.
Dead Ma'ams chest

The excitement didn’t stop as Ina swapped to her next song, diving into the crimson red song of her senpai, Houshou Marine: Dead Ma’ams Chest. Behind her, a white octopus insignia with a crown and swords watches over her, combining Ina’s and Marine’s motifs. Dead Ma’ams Chest, in addition to being chosen as one of Ina’s senpais, also has intriguingly similar themes to Ina’s lore, particularly concerning duality.

In the original Music Video, Marine raids a lost vessel, full of ghosts and long forgotten treasures, seeking out one jewel in particular. Upon entering the inside, Marine encounters a ghastly version of herself, and the two fight. After besting the cursed marine, the pirate herself takes to raiding the ship, until the cursed marine wakes up, and begins to resurrect the ships crew to take down her counterpart.

Just as it seems over for our Marine, she kicks open a treasure box, revealing that the other marine was dead all along, a spirit trapped in a treasure chest, cursed to not depart, clinging desperately to a life stolen from her. Cursed Marine then summons a dragon out of pure rage and anguish, and Marine fights her way to the top, emboldened by the truth revealed, slaying the dragon. The music video then ends with Marine embracing her own ghost as they fade away, finally accepting that they’ve passed.

Within the Inaverse, this particular song holds several intriguing possibilities. For one, a red tinted song focused on characters that act as a sort of duality, one in the past, one in the present, feels reminiscent of Temari. The one in the past lives in a dead ship, and the inaverse equivalent might be a priestess of a dead world/bad end. The Treasure Box, hiding the remains of a ghost inside, also might have frightening ramifications. Within the Inaverse, music boxes are a recurring theme, seen in Pleides, Tsuki no Waltz, and Takodachi no Uta. If you consider the treasure box as a loosely connected theme, then it would further reinforce the idea of the music box as a container for memories, and even suggest that whoever’s memories they hold, have since departed from the living.
Or of course, it's just a senpai's song she really likes, but it's fun to ponder...
Palette

The final appearance of Yuusha Ina would arrive at the end of the free section of day 2, in none other than another senpai song, Towa’s Palette. Palette is a song quite similar to Gunjou in terms of themes, Towa singing of exhaustion at living in a monochrome reality, and desperate to paint the world in colors of her own.
“And so the freezing night finally begins to thaw
And reaches out to me with a new dawn.”

Placed into the Inaverse, this connection is one of the most obvious and direct, Ina breaking through her frozen past, breaking through the grey of Past Ina, and embracing the warmth and colors of a messy world.

body.text: The abyss in the heavens shadow
While our rabbit hero, Yuusha, dazzled the very heavens, below, a different story unfolded.

A cry from the depths, born from a soul who could only gaze at the moon from afar, seemingly impossibly out of reach. A girl bound to the very depths of the ocean tugged along by that same moon, caged by her duties to remain the priestess.
Abyss Ina

Following the first four songs of day 1, each performed by Yuusha, Ina's new outfit would finally make its grand reveal. Combined with a massive stage design shift, Abyss Ina feels like an entirely separate being, a stargazer weighed down by the gravity of Earth, starved of comfort in the moon's cold light.
Post Abyssal Hymn CAUTION:

Following Abyssal Hymn's release, we have still yet to see Abyss Ina make a major appearance in Ina's songs or covers. While the girl at the very end of Abyssal Hymn does bare a striking resemblance to Abyss, the attire doesn't exactly match up, and we've yet to see any Ina wielding her "wings of the Abyss".

Yet despite Abyss not making a full appearance in Abyssal Hymn, Ina herself would say after the concert she enjoyed seeing Yuusha and AByss drawn together, hinting at some sort of relationship between the two. Given Yuusha played a HUGE role in Hymn, it is worth taking a deeper look into Abyss Ina, and nowhere else do we get a better glimpse at who she is than Drawn 2 Dawn, where she shares the stage as an equal to Yuusha.
Asphyxia
Now, take all those words of caution, and chuck them out the window! Cause it's time for some fun.

Because out of every single performance at Drawn 2 Dawn, this might just be THE MOST IMPORTANT, connecting back to many, maaaany past performances and hints, while also offering us a very different look at our newest priestess.

Striding onto stage with a takodachi microphone, Ina sings before a dark stage, the black screen behind her filling with a white splash. The moon is no longer gold, but lit by both red and blue, suggesting that we are leaving the cool blue stage that Yuusha has brought before us. Moments later, the music ramps up, computer generated text and information rapidly flooding the screen behind Ina in an overwhelming display. Ina dances along, the crowd chanting and cheering her up, the atmosphere growing even hotter every second as jets of fire light up her transformation.

With each passing second, a dark shadow eclipses the moon, accompanied with the picture frames folding together like pages of a book. As the last light of the moon is snuffed out, the covers of the book snap shut behind Ina,
And Abyss Ina is born.
IMMEDIATELY, EVERYTHING HAS CHANGED.
Rather than dancing before space, Ina now sings from within a city.
Where once the moon was close enough to reach, now it is only left as a wooden frame on a window.
Stars no longer light up her world, instead she is illuminated by manmade lights from windows and lanterns dangling over her head.
That, and of course the blood red moon behind her, lighting up her dark world in its crimson shine.
The hero of the moon is gone.
Now we meet the priestess of the abyss.
A child trapped in the night
Stopped breathing, expressionless

The opening line of Asphyxia that played before Yuusha's transformation immediately strikes a STRONG chord with Temar, a song that is etched into Abyss Ina’s haori. A young Ina, trapped in the dark, dying without a sound, a perfect and quiet husk to the very end.
There's nothing we can do about this!
We're drowning in a world we can't change

Combining the lyrics of Asphyxia with her own design, Abyss's introduction is far darker than that of the other Ina's we've met before, a girl crushed by the weight of the world. The vocal use of drowning ties her closely with her namesake, dark depths of the ocean, more alien than even the heaven's above. Far from the serene calm of the surface, Abyss has capsized beneath the waves of her emotions, her heart sinking to place few could ever reach.
Open your eyes
The shadows sink. But no matter how it seems, this is reality now.
And now, Abyss has accepted her defeat, a destiny impossible to break.
What is freedom?
I selfishly hoped
That the pain you gave to me might be love.
I have no need
For this Schadenfreude that keeps me down.
I've grown tired of its heavy-handed drama
and discord aesthetic.

The first chorus reflects upon how she got here, and inevitably, how she broke. Taking upon the pain given to her, likely through the cult, Abyss had hoped to earn the love of her "family." Schadenfreude, a word that describes the joy of learning through struggle, isn't far off from the metaphor of the Meconopsis as growing through diversity. If not the family, it may very well be the cycles of reincarnation wearing her down, with the pain coming from the one she loved and wished to see again.
And then, another voice begins to fight back in the bridge:
How long can you keep saying
That things are unfair, or "hopeless?"
How much giving up until you're satisfied?
It's laughable.
A voice from within, the same one that drives her ever onwards, laughs at her complaints,  and going into chorus 2, the lyrics swell with resolve.
Even broken, I live on
My ending credit roll betrays all expectation
With a heart that's been broken again and again
I keep on
Each time I breathe, my body continues to rust
I just need to accept the parts of me that fall away as I fight on.

Far less of a hero and more of a beast, Abyss Ina is a far cry from Yuusha. She doesn’t fight on out of desire, but because she has no other choice. She accepts that she is losing, yet she continues to push on, mounting more and more of a fight, building a resistance to the toxic hand of fate dealt to her. Her destiny, her countless struggles, each one builds her stronger and stronger.
Her face unresponsive to her elegy
She starts breathing in the dead of night.
Yet no matter how much spirit Abyss has, her body still betrays her, face unresponsive to her crying heart. Instead, something else begins to breathe in her place in the darkness.

All together, the song’s use and arrival under a blood moon and fire, suggests Abyss Ina is a far cry from our hero, and will do whatever it takes to change fate. The overall emotions also feel oddly reminiscent of Monster without a name. A girl beneath a red moon, unable to escape her reality, accepting a monster into her body. All the while within a city at night…
The Blood Moon

A constant visual referenced in some of her song choices for 3d lives, particularly Monster Without a name and Asphyxia, it appears for the first time with the arrival/birth of Abyss. The blood moon has a great number of symbolic meanings, both in and out of Japan, and among the most prominent across culture and media, is an ominous sign of impending change, often associated with evil. In real life, these lunar eclipses occur when the moon falls into the earth’s shadow, split from the sun, only receiving light diffused through Earth’s atmosphere. Within the context of the Inaverse, this could suggest that a transformation or change occurs when the individual in question has their connection broken from their source of light.

Whereas the moon is often associated with enlightenment and wisdom, a blood moon is the shadow, the emotions that are hidden from view. Rage, anger, bitterness. All of which are reflected in Asphyxia’s lyrics.

Altogether, Abyss Ina feels strikingly similar to the second priestess, a girl driven by grief, attempting to change fate. As the hints from the dragon and Neverland Paradox suggest, she may no longer be content to accept destiny, and will use any means to rewrite them. And if the outfit gives any indication, that includes abusing Ao’s power.
The City

Unlike Yuusha Ina, much of Abyss’s time is spent in a city far away from the moon. Here, the moon only appears in the background as a window design, suggesting Abyss is pondering the moon from far away. Rather than being lit by the stars, she is now lit by the glow of building windows, changing color to fit the theme and mood, along with lanterns. The modern setting around her implies a great deal of time has passed since the cult was around, the world growing up around her while she remains tied to the depths of her past. Finally, the stage is now adorned in red banners/curtains, further emphasizing Abyss Ina as connected to the ancient ones as a priestess.
The stage also shares an overall theme with Monster Without a Name in Neverland Paradox, a song that directly mentions a red moon, implying Ina might’ve had the general idea around a looong time ago.
Ghost of the Deep Sea (Umi no Yuurei)

Abyss's 2nd song, Umi no Yuurei, is yet another one of Ina's favorite songs from an artist she likes, Kenshi Yonezu. Made for the 2019 film, Children of the Sea, it offers a more subdued and introspective look into Abyss's world and mind. In the following MC section, Ina would explain part of her inspiration was the thought of "meeting one summer day," and thought about how she was meeting the takodachis.

The lyrics of the song follow the singer recalling memories of someone whose friend has departed, leaving only the scent of the sea. In spite of their disappearance, the singer continues to do small acts on their behalf like leaving the door open, and waiting to hear a knock. All the while, they ponder what they should say when they meet next.

The yearning and heartfelt wishes on display from the very beginning are very much in line with numerous parts of the Inaverse to this point, and especially seems to call forward to Abyssal Hymn, where Ina is constantly leaving behind heartfelt messages to the Wahtcher, and seeks to meet her again.

The chorus that follows describes a meeting that takes place under shooting stars, which interestingly enough, would actually appear in the next song Ina sang Their meeting, though seemingly brief, forever colored the singers heart, unable to describe everything they felt that summer, seemingly falling in love with this stranger.
And before I knew it, shining there so bright
The ghost of the deep sea
Which of course, of all the characters in the Inaverse, none fit better than the Wahtcher. A pale figure shining in the depths of the abyss.
The verses that follow pour on the yearning more and more, again embodying the desire to meet one another throughout RE:Vision.
I can hear the sound of your laughter from somewhere far away from here.
It's just like a hand upon a warm cheek.
If I travel this winding and twisting road,
Your tightly shut eyes will open wide.
The first verse has a few lines that are remarkably familiar with Takodachi no Uta, especially how the ghost's voice leaves them feeling warm within.
Even if we're separated, beyond space and time.
Scream out loud, "I am happy as I am now."

Again, Ghost of the Deep Sea reflects the distance between Ina and the Wahtcher, encapsulating all the messages sent to one another throughout Abyssal Hymn, showcasing that even across time and space, their love remains unbreakable.
The rest of the song repeats the singer's inability to put their thoughts into words, before repeating the first chorus.
Finally, they cast one more wish, or even a promise, into the air:
On the sandy beach, in the summer wind,
Let's meet together again.
The Abyss

The stage for the second half of day 1 emphasizes Abyss’s connection to the deep sea, particularly during Ghost of the Deep Sea. Rather than staring into the sky, Abyss Ina appears to be within an underwater temple, only able to view the moon through a special window. In between, a whale passes through the looking glass, suggesting a monstress creature blocks her way to reaching the moon, and upon it, Yuusha. However, even if she wanted to run and live her own life, the moon, its central place on her stage even while unreachable, shows where her heart still lies, and now much like the tides, she is at the mercy to follow wherever the moon (be it Yuusha, another Ina, or the Wahtcher) goes.
Beneath the gown

For her final 2 songs, Abyss would discard her outer layers, revealing a more casual fit within, that even despite being all black, felt far more playful and youthful than her full priestess design. Combined with her more exposed legs and smaller body frame, she is far more adorable and friendly looking, and can be read as Abyss displaying more vulnerability and raw emotions.

And indeed, her last songs of the evening, Violet and Takodachi no Uta, would finally give us a glimpse at the girl hidden in the deep, a playful spirit who charmed the stage with her small stature and earnest movement.

Violet itself was a humble and nostalgic trip for all the myth fans in the crowd, a sea of violet penlights waving along before Abyss's dancing. This time, the background transformed into a black screen, as though she were truly singing from the void. Across the screen, white lights would rain down, like drops of rain or even shooting stars splashing into the waves.

Given that Umi no Yuurei, the song just before Violet, mentioned a meeting taking place beneath shooting stars, it's possible the imagery on the background in Violet was chosen deliberately. After all, Violet features Ina's journey to meet someone again as its core theme. Thus, the falling stars from the heavens above into the abyss may just signal the destined reunion between Abyss and her counterpart rapidly approaching.
As for [Takodachi no Uta], Drawn 2 Dawn gives us a large number of hints, and thus, its performance will be discussed in that chapter as a main source.
DAY 2: Among the Stars

True to being among the stars, Abyss’s next song came from one of Ina’s favorite series: Gundam, specifically Gundam Unicorn, with the song also produced by one of her favorites: Aimer.
Bathed in red, the performance began with a slow and somber message,
Please hear me
I want to tell you
Please sing to me
I wanna hear your voice
Please hear me
I want to tell you
Na na na na na, na na na na na
StarRingChild

Abyss’s voice calling out, trying to reach across the stars, recalling all the past moments in both concerts and her own songs where a voice was lost. However, with the power gifted by the halo, she might have finally succeeded in making that connection.

The initial verses are introspective, a voice responding both to the promise of the world around them and their own impossible dreams, recognizing that “the city for which you grew taller to gaze upon is beginning to blur.” Now their goals that set them in motion have begun to fade, and they’re questioning the entire reason to move forward.
“The promise of that day that seems so far away… and can be switched once its color fades,
But your false pride made from a mixture of truth and lies can’t cover up the voice you’ve lost sight of.”
The verse before the first chorus criticizes the desire to run away and hide where it’s safe, saying that though they can always find strength in their ego, they will lose their own voice.
Star * Ring * Child
If you grab hold of this trembling beat, you can make a sound.
Amongst all the pages your once small hands drew,
Is a future sticking out from the folds.

The chorus calls to the singer, telling them that despite how terrifying it may be, if they can grab a hold of what makes their heart shake, they can find their voice again. The second line calls back to their innocent dreams, and within it a spark of their true self that can guide them forward.

In terms of the Inaverse, StarringChild represents a turning point in Abyss’s journey. After previously struggling to accept themselves, caught between the lies of the world around her, be it AO, the “family”, or whatever else you choose, it is a voice from within that reaches out to her, calling from the past. 
Yes, it may be scary, but it is scary because it comes from the heart. The fear of having her dreams crushed, her wishes rejected, of being vulnerable and bearing your soul, it all can feel overwhelming.

Yet in seeking security, she fell further and further from the stars she sought.
The numbness accepted previously in Asphyxia only drew her further and further from her wishes, and while it protected her from being hurt, she also lost herself in doing so.
Starringchild only amplifies this message moving forward, stating that:
“The rhythm of your footsteps has forgotten what weakness is, drowning out even the purest songs of love.”

Given that Abyss is tightly connected with the Ancient Ones, along with Temari’s entire theme around Prayer vs. Meconopsis rejection, Starringchild flat out states Abyss lost herself through seeking out strength and refusing to change. In spite of how she wails and bays for love with her whole heart, her voice could never reach before, warped by the very void she had hidden herself in. By choosing to stay on her path avoid risks, she had lost the most important thing:
Herself.
“Even if you wield the words you adorned out of fear, they won’t graze a thing”

No matter how much strength she may wield, when it only comes from fear, it will never bring about the future she seeks. True strength isn’t found in the most comfortable path, nor in seeking that which is known and safe, but from embracing herself, and releasing it upon the world.

The second chorus repeats the first, though this time rather than “a future” it is “a wish”, calling back to the innocence and honesty of herself as a child. Diving in a bit further, it might be parallel to the very pencil she had broken, a link she had lost. If Abyss is one of the two Inanis after all, then it shows that no matter how dark reality appears, some part of her still remains.

Two final verses follow the chorus, the first one bringing together the songs message, calling them to trust in their unwavering spirit when they were young, not defined by another’s truth, to not give up on themselves even when obstacles tried to change their destination.
The unwavering children didn’t put an end,
To a treasure map that unfolded wherever it pleased.
In that place, there was no need for even a shred of truth;
A world compact into a single second.”
The conclusion brings together major elements of the Inaverse, calling back to the innocent dreams that colored Abyss’s world when she was young, and singing that
Even if the innocent color you let loose comes to blows,
The sound it paints will never be forgotten.
Thus, no matter how others may try to fight or tarnish her dreams, the earnest love wrought forth by it will forever live on, a truth nobody can ever take from her.
The answer you traced to this place no longer has meaning,
So go onward past this world you glimpsed only for a second.

In conclusion, Starringchild, sung from atop the moon so far from where she began, can be seen as a moment of realization for Abyss Ina, ESPECIALLY if we connect her with Past Ina. Past Ina, an innocent child raised to be nothing more than a tool, was one day given an innocent dream for something more. Yet, afraid of straying from the path, she carried on, accepting the lies of her family and AO as the truth, because following those pure dreams came with uncertainties of a life beyond her scope.

Would she be accepted? Where could she go? When would she reach her destination?
A thousand questions stalled her, and she stalled, accepting her fate again and again. But given that she now sports the halo, either she finally reached the truth left in the book, following up on Takodachi no Uta, or another reached for her, and gave her the push to finally move forward.
Now the universe is hers to paint. One that will echo with a voice that she has found once more.
Stellar Stellar

The last song to be set in space during Drawn to Dawn, Stellar Stellar, was met with immediate and raucous applause, the stage and crowd jumping from red to blue within seconds. 
For those who are not aware, Stellar Stellar is the incredible song by Hoshimachi Suisei, comet, singer, and long time hololive member who has long stunned vtuber enjoyers new and old since her debut.

Another fun fact: She is Ina’s kamioshi, or god-oshi, an idol she respects so much that she gets nervous around their presence.
But beyond dropping our spaghetti, Suisei is an incredible vocalist, and with her performance of Stellar Stellar, Ina made a statement: That she too could reach the stars.

Stellar Stellar itself follows in the footsteps of Starringchild to be yet another song revolving around self-actualization, the singer confronting their insecurities and singing out loud their desires, no matter how much they try to downplay their own dreams.

The first several verses follow that theme, describing things they could never say, walls they could never climb, similar to the unfolding map mentioned in just the previous songs. The longer it went on, the more frustrating it became, the promise of a dream that felt impossibly out of reach.

But as the pre-chorus approaches, Suisei, as well as any other singer, in this case: Abyss Ina, sings out to both themselves and the audience, finding strength in making others feel, and realizing how similar everyone is.
Hold your hand out all the way. Reach out and make someone feel
We’re very alike, indeed, both you and me. You’re not special, neither am I, no, not at all
In this instance, it might be that Abyss is finally realizing and connecting with the struggles of others, and in doing so, it is giving her a new strength. The realization she’s not alone.
The first chorus begins with a roar, accepting that they too can become the star they always sought impossibly far away, allowing their voice to reach far and wide.
So I say, what I wanted to be was never
A Cinderella who waits forever
But the prince who goes and gets things done
Just like the shooting star I have become.

And now, Abyss, or whoever she is meant to represent, has stated that she never wanted to be the one waiting forever, a damsel in distress. Imagery and vocals that can be tied to both Takodachi no Uta and the Wahtcher as a whole. No, she wants to be the one to take action and accomplish things. To become the prince, which, as far as Ina goes, whether it is Yuusha, NinoIna the hero, or any given RPG playthrough, is rather in character, always taking action and soldiering forth as a true hero from the heart.
If Abyss is trapped or struggling within an accursed fate, this could hint at her desire to finally take a decisive action, to reach out and try something new, no matter how difficult it may be.

The rest of Stellar Stellar continues in similar vein, the singer facing roadblocks to their path, wanting to still accept defeat to avoid the heartache that comes alongside it, only to find the strength to surge on.

Even after chorus 2 in the bridge, they flat out state it’s a “fairytale, a total fantasy.” Yet with their dedication and effort, they are giving it new life.
The song concludes by stating that not only are they the shooting star they sought to be, but realizing they always were all along.

Stellar Stellar overall finalizes a shift in the mood around Abyss Ina. While Starringchild was a bit more critical, calling out all the ways she sought to hide herself in comfort and security to hide from the very heartache faced in Stellar Stellar, the latter shows that by following her heart was finally able to reach that future she had only dreamt of before, now standing among the stars that were so far out of reach before. Ina further visualizes her self-acceptance by yet again dropping the priestess haori, escaping the security of remaining on a set course as the priestess, but now baring both her vulnerable heart and innocent dreams, accepting her true self and every color within her.
No longer is the priestess layered in the wardrobe of the “family” and AO, the puppet who marched to a fate given to her, instead she now wields the strings of fate for herself.
There’s just… one more loose end.
One Last Kiss

The last cover of Drawn to Dawn would prove to be one of Ina’s most memorable performances, toning down the energy into an experience that was deep and enchanting. One Last kiss by Hikaru Utada, a song used for one of her favorites series, Evangelion, would conclude Abyss’s journey to the moon, opening with an eclipse, returning the stage to a dark world, Abyss left in a lightless city.

Now the only light that returns to her, appearing in the waves of the screen behind, *as if they were ripples echoing from elsewhere.* And yet, even split from the one she seeks by the very universe, Abyss sings nonetheless.
Despite being my first visit to the Louvre
It didn’t surprise me
Because a long time ago
I found my very own Mona Lisa
Since the day I met you, the heart began to turn its gears
I can’t help but have a hunch, that I will lose you.

All together, it suggests that Abyss has been in love for some time, seeing the other (Yuusha? The Wahtcher?) as a work of art. The fact that they were the first individual to move their heart, further ties in with Suzume and Wonderland, the idea that past Ina’s heart was opened by the other, but she never learned how to express that love before it was too late.
Now, alone and in the dark, potentially before accepting a bitter fate, they wish for a memory not even THE VOID could erase.
**Ona last kiss to cherish for eternity.**

The chorus then follows, a back and forth with the audience, along with the backing vocals. Somewhere, beyond the great distance of the void, another soul sings out to Ina, illuminated by the white lights behind her.

Though Abyss’s world is dark and colorless by herself, she dances regardless, performing a sway with both arms and hands, mimicking the tides pulled and pushed by the moon. Her heart, still attached to the moon girl.
Still asking for one last kiss.
Joined in by the thousands of takos before her, chanting along, singing in tandem to help her message reach through the void.
I love you more than you'll ever know.

The verse following chorus 1 gives us more insight into the singer, as well as their relationship with their partner. In this case, be it Ina and the Wahtcher, Yuusha and AByss... or perhaps even some combination.
"I hate when people take my picture" you say
But I don’t need any
For you’re already burned
Into the projector in my heart
I was pretending I wasn't lonely-
-Which sounds an *awful* lot like the Wahtcher pretending she was okay being forgotten in the Abyss, only to dial up the takodachis because she was lonely.
-Well, I guess that makes the two of us-
Though it appears to have been mutual, perhaps her counterpart also trying to act tough. Either way, both miss each other badly.
Yearning for someone
Came hand in hand with heartache

IF Yuusha is her counterpart after all (which could imply Wahtcher IS Abyss), it would appear that their own anxiety and fear, attempting to fix everything alone, only exacerbated their frustration and loneliness. Lack of communication and the desire to solve everything dooming both to timelines of mistakes and broken hearts.
Can you give me one last kiss?
Let’s make it a burning one
One I can never forget
No matter how much I want to
Again, the desire and heartache come hand in hand, and no matter how much it hurts, no matter the pain that comes with it, Ina, Wahtcher, Abyss, Yuusha, whomever. Still wants it.

Playing off the earlier themes of letting your true self out, whomever is singing is letting their full heart bare to the world. Rather fitting that Abyss is still in her coatless version, befitting a song that is raw and vulnerable.
Chorus 2 follows much like the first, before rolling into one more bridge, following a couple of Ina spins, stopping only as the screen behind her goes fully black. And yet, she can't forget.
I know who it is now
Even at the end of the world
Even as I grow older
The one I can can never forget
Throughout each chorus prior, there was a different variation of “never forget”.
In chorus one, it referred to the things “we don’t want to forget”.
In chorus two, it was following up more directly to the kiss as one to not be forgotten.

But by the time of the bridge to the final chorus and within said chorus, it is no longer just the kiss, but the being themselves, “the one they can never forget.” Combined with the ethereal soundscape of One Last Kiss, it speaks to something deeper, a love and bond that can break through timelines and destinies just to meet each other again.
So, how fitting is it, that in Abyssal Hymn’s MV, among the many messages floating about, is one with a little drawing in English, that states My Heart already knows your name.
Whomever the Wahtcher is, no matter the distance.
Ina's heart will never forget.
Thus, Love is the key to overcoming the void’s decay, and in doing so, what saves both Ina and her counterpart. Whatever her name is, Ina will always know in her heart.
On that dazzling afternoon
I chase after the wind that blew across my face.
The outro corresponds richly with Ghost of the deep sea, Takodachi no Uta, and Abyssal Hymn, all looking forward to the summer day they meet again.
Acoustic Violet

The final song of Ina’s EP Re:Vision, we will only be discussing it here for the sake of time.
Following the first release of the original Violet, Ina would share that Seibin had additionally made an acoustic track for the song. This would finally return for RE:Vision, developed even further than before, alongside Ina’s own vocals evolving as well.

Quiet and ambient, Acoustic Violet calls back to the first, and comes across as the end of a journey. The backing vocals and whispers that once followed the track, including Lumina’s original language, have all vanished, suggesting the two travelers have finally met. Or if you want something a bit more bittersweet, that voice has moved on from or merged with the singing Ina. This would align with the idea of the backing vocals in Violet being her own past in the monochrome world.

However, if you believe the vocals belong to the Wahtcher, then perhaps she really did lose her voice, teased as far back as Nai Nai and Neverland Paradox. This would also explain Ina’s difficulty in finding her, as all Violet Ina knew was her “fleeting voice”, while Past Ina only knew her fleeting smile.
An interesting point of evidence comes from the concert itself, where Ina teased previously for takodachis to sing the final Shitteru yo.

Thus, it may be that the other voice in Violet became or came from a takodachi(s), which again, will vary depending on who you believe the takodachi is. If the monochrome section is Past Ina after all, then that would imply Past Ina was in fact the first takodachi, which would help slot a lot of things into place.

On the flip side, the first tako being the Wahtcher also has an amusing meta take to it, with us being the literal watchers of Ina. Thus, the Wahtcher may be the Inanis of a world who gave up her voice, and cheers on the one who became Ina instead.

Much like its appearance on day 1, Abyss sings Violet as the seventh song again in her more casual wear, showing the kind soul who still very much lives under the shell. Add in the warm and breathy vocals, removed of all background noise, and now she comes across far more present and transparent, certain of who she directs her wishes to.

In conclusion, though similar to the original, Acoustic Violet reflects the end of Ina’s journey through re:vision, the culmination of her finding herself, and meeting again the one she longed to see. Though the lyrics are still full of longing and nostalgia, their release is warm and sincere, finding the words she wished to say.
Abyssal Hymn
Following a hearfelt thank you to everyone who supported her over the years, Ina concluded her solo performances of Drawn to Dawn with Abyssal Hymn.

“You know, I love telling stories, so I thought, what better way to end off. Abyssal Hymn is the climax of the story I’ve been working on over the years, and we’re working on a really, really cool MV.”
body.cite: Ninomae Ina'nis: Drawn to Dawn (phrased to the best of my memory)

body.text: Upon the very opening of the performance, the previous stage melted away, the city vanishing, leaving only a pair of picture frames remaining behind Ina. On the background screen behind them, a looping animation of tentacles swirling around Ina played, pinning her as the beating heart of an eldritch god. Additionally, at various moments on screen, several rings of light would appear before vanishing into the distance, as if caught in some form of travel between dimensions. The combination of visuals calls back to the cover art of RE:Vision, with tentacles swirling around Ina from a picture frame, although the existence of two picture frames here again implies a pair of Ina’s trapped within this wicked fate. Otherwise, perhaps Abyss is not one of the two frames, but the sign of a merger between the two. Which, given the eye, might be one possibility.

Colorwise, Ina had told us way back in the RE:Vision release stream that Abyssal Hymn’s colors were a rainbow, and sure enough, the crowd used penlights of every color. Not only fitting for Ina as some sort of ascended being, but also due to the numerous Ina’s seen throughout the trailers (and the MV once it was released). Even her own stage lights would showcase multiple colors, with a band of lights shifting between red, blue, and violet, which easily ties back to her original three songs.

Beyond the visual and audio spectacle, Ina herself would play her part in the story, showing different body motions and hand movements hinting at the events in the song. Like before with Temari, the warping of time was displayed through spinning, and this time, emphasized further with her arms outstretched, ticking like a clock.

There was also at least one if not more moments where Ina appeared to pick up something and wrap it through her hands, as if kneading an object. Given her various lore, the most immediate connection would be that she is weaving together a temari ball.
The End of the Abyss

Alltogether, the journey of Abyss Ina ends with a resolution we have yet to see, finding her resolve to take action in spite of the fate laid against her. A counterpart not just visually but thematically to Yuusha, Abyss is heavily befitting of the second Inanis’ seen in Temari to some capacity, a girl that is self-aware and suffocating under the weight placed upon her, who eventually makes a new choice. What this choice is isn’t completely certain until Ina tells us, but given Yuusha is the one seeking out Past Ina and the Wahtcher at the end, it might have played a part in keeping Ina safe from the clutches of the Ancient Ones, and bearing a sin for both of them.

And throughout it all, love compels them. Love gives them the resolve and desire to keep pushing forward, to bring hell to the heavens if that’s what it takes to reach the distant stars where the other lies. The strength to hold on, even when she’s drowning in the darkness, a light she can never let go of.
A light that will one day save her from oblivion.
"I'll make a rainbow with my spilled tears"
Joy, whimsy, and naivete are married with nostalgia, regret, and loneliness in Ina’s fifth song, Takodachi no Uta.

Originally, this song wasn’t even a thought for Ina, but as she worked on RE:Vision and Abyssal Hymn, she realized there was a part of the story she wanted to explore more, to help flesh it out.
And thus, Takodachi no Uta was born. A song that deliberately invokes a nursery rhyme soundscape, utilizing both a softer tone, light instrumentation, and ambient noises to bring to life memories of a past we have yet to see.

On top of that, Ina was also kind enough to tell us of one thing: An MV for Takodachi would be Black and White color mainly, and would be rather sad… Quoting the priestess herself as she discussed the lyrics and project:
“It really conveyed that innocent, melancholic, nostalgic, emptiness, loneliness kind of feeling, very well.”
Although we currently do not have an MV out yet, Drawn to Dawn and the lyrics themselves give us several visuals to help us explore the story told here.
Black and White

Thanks to Drawn 2 Dawn, we actually do have a couple visuals we can use, and some notes taken while the vod was still up, that will help us immensely in working out Takodachi no Uta’s theme. So let’s start off with the biggest throughout Ina’s MV’s:
Color.

Long before performing the song live, let alone drawing any visuals/animations, Ina gave us the aforementioned hint above, that Takodachi no Uta’s colors are Black AND White. Right from the get go, this gives us several key hints. The first and most obvious is with Past Ina living in a monochrome world, a theme bolstered by her focus on nostalgia, innocence, melancholy, emptiness, and loneliness.

On top of that, Black and White being two colors, may hint at their being two singers within the song. And for those who took their time to rewatch the Drawn 2 Dawn vod while it was up, may have noticed something.

Throughout the song, the stage's lighting would change, shifting between white lights and darkness, the stars and the void, and gradually, it was clear something more was happening.
Indeed, taking the time to highlight when the lighting would shift between black and white gave a telling image on the two singers of Takodachi no Uta.
Rather than a single singer throughout, we have two, clear and distinguished singers. One singing in the dark. One bathed in light and the stars.
Black

The Takodachi, without a doubt. Throughout the song, their many “wahs” would dim the screen behind, but it wasn’t just that. Onomatopoeia and playful sounds all contributed to describing this individual as more innocent and pure, untainted by the sins of the world. Well, seemingly, that is. In actuality, the truth is far murkier. The few moments where the lights vanished/faded, we actually got to listen to their words, far more somber than expected.

The tako, or whoever they represent, appear to have AO-chan/the necronomicon, and call out to the other singer on sleepless nights. Their lyrics are more environmental, describing a starry night where they wait for the other forever, seemingly numb to their situation.
The most intriguing part? The bridge, where the background instruments largely fade into a lullaby-like jingle, with deep, ambient bass adding a layer of tension below. The singer wakes up, again finding themselves lonely, and can’t help but ask to see the other again.
Finally, the outro concludes as it starts, the singer holding a book under a starry night, waiting forever.
White

But of the two, the one in the light appears even lonelier. Sending her feelings into the void, a spell cast into loneliness, she immediately accepts defeat, believing wholeheartedly her prayers will never be answered, and that the other is never coming back. She also appears to have a book of her own, suggesting that there are either two books, or, they may be sending messages across time or another dimension impossibly wide.

Playing games with her counterpart, she is filled with happiness and joy yet again, and perhaps something a little more, stating that their voice calling her name, makes her heart feel warm. However, by the end, the bliss finally finishes, and white fully gives into grief, truly believing they will never meet again, and saying goodbye as she sobs.
Altogether, the white vocals have lost all the naivete of their childhood, and wish they could continue to live within a comfort that was stolen away, one they believe will never return.
Rainbow
A single line, but one worth noting, calling upon the vibrant array we’ve seen in various other songs at this point, stating:
“I’ll make a rainbow with my spilled tears.” Given the status of rainbows as a display of the divine in the Inaverse, it might be that those very tears will bring a miracle to life.
Windup music box

Arguably the single most important element, a windup music box has been featured at multiple points in time throughout Ina’s recent productions. Most noticeable in Pleides, which featured several guests on a music box stage, where a key would unlock new girls over the course of the concert. This is also where Temari was unveiled to the public.
One can also hear the sound of a music box winding down when the music abruptly cuts near the end of Temari, just before the final chorus.
And of course, at the start of Takodachi no Uta, we can hear it being wound up.

And of course, at the start of Takodachi no Uta, we can hear it being wound up.
The music box would also make its return in multiple ways at Drawn 2 Dawn for those with keen eyes, as a golden key appears at the start of Takodachi no Uta, as if unlocking a memory. Another, non-direct example exists in the form of Ina performing Tsuki no Waltz, a jazzy and ethereal performance complete with ballet moves that evoked imagery of a wind-up doll.

Looking at the music box as a symbol, one can see both music as a way of expressing emotion, and retaining it, the memories within it, now being replayed again. The wind-up dolls cannot escape, nor can they deviate, they simply dance as they were designed to do, living out the emotions and performances of the ones who designed them.
Ambient Sounds

Throughout Takodachi no uta, there are numerous sounds that play, adding to an ambient, intimate atmosphere of memories. Splashing water, a swingset swaying, evoking memories of childhood, innocence that was stolen from them. Yet, those memories they hold onto are precious.

They also call back to Lumina’s original language from violet:
“Scars, fireflies, empty, music, sound, childhood. “

Though now their precious memories have had their innocence tainted, they still hold within them comfort and nostalgia. Thus, in spite of the thorns, they cling to them with every last drop of love in their body.
Kodama

Now, the “echoing tree spirits”, or kodama, are referred to at multiple points in the lyrics. These are spirits said to inhabit trees, and are sometimes seen as the source “Yamabiko”, where sound in mountains and valleys echo.

In this way, interpreted a bit more literally, these might refer more to echoes themselves, suggesting that rather than the two singers being able to sing directly to each other, they can only reach each other by distant echo. Thus, they can’t warn one another of danger, nor be with one another when they’re lonely. Split apart by fate, their closest companionship is a passing breeze.
Someday soon (We'll meet)

Following months of teasers and years of hard work, the culmination of Ina's story would be fully unveiled on September 19th, 2026, bringing together all the remaining pieces of the journey that began with Violet.
Animated by an entire studio through Reticles and featuring a backing score by Kirai Modai Orchestra, the full work left Ina extremely excited and proud to show off in her own words, "The climax of her story."
A story of the Ina's

Rather than merely being a story of one Ina, Abyssal Hymn definitively shows a number of different Ina's, concluding with three meeting at the very end. Figuring out who is who can help us decipher the story, and thanks to various visuals and progression of events, we can quickly build a connection between them.
