body.text: "Our Ina"

Most prominent of all is the Ina of the surface world, who seems very much like our own. Look a little deeper though, and you’ll notice a multitude of forms and appearances that almost seem to take place at different points in time, or more interestingly, be different forms of her now rolled into one.

The most immediate and effective element in this is Ina’s very own hints, who explained at numerous moments we can use language to piece the story together. If we focus on only the instances where Ina is singing in english lyrics in Abyssal Hymn, we get 3 outfits, all of which are consistently seen in the overworld/reality. These include Kimono Ina, Priestess Ina, and Yuusha.

Additionally, Ina would also state in the Re:vision release stream that Abyssal Hymn’s colors were a whole array, hinting that rather than a single Ina, Abyssal Hymn would serve as a culmination of previous stories. Alongside this, the ring of lights at Drawn to Dawn during the song’s performance would highlight red, blue, and violet in particular, calling back to her first three songs.

Given these are also the three colors of the pens Yuusha wields, on top of her primary outfit being white, a combination of colored light, it is extremely likely she is a combination of other Inas and their experiences. It isn’t just the pens either, as during chorus 2, when she releases priestess Ina after transforming, we see those three colors forming a trio of orbiting rings around her. Finally, when her light breaks through the barrier after exploding Cthulhu, those 3 colors rain down around the shrine maiden/Wahtcher, dousing her world in color once more.

One alternative explanation could be that rather than belonging to Yuusha, these colors belong to The Overlord, who may now exist within Yuusha. Evidence for this comes not only from Yuusha’s role as a hero and monster slayer in Evermore, but also due to the prayer scene in Tako-Takover displaying the Overlord already possessing 3 other Inas.

Given that a massive, powerful priestess who has access to the internet is unleashed at the very end to cage/kill Cthullu, there are few other individuals who fit the description. Not to mention, the rings of color orbit her, and while the colored rain that follows the tako explosion appears before Yuusha, their source of creation does coincide with the explosion.
Thus, the colors may not belong to one or the other, but be a shared aspect of all of Ina’s forms now, a collection of different lives, experiences, whatever you wish. Now all tied into the same Ina.
Kimono Ina

Appearing in a mirrored pose to the Wahtcher waiting beyond the void, Ina’s first appearance sees her in her New Year’s Kimono outfit, first seen as far back as 2022. Seen leaving prayers at a shrine beneath 5 gohei, she turns around to find Kiara and Calli, ensuring that unmistakably, this Ina is from our own world at the very least.

After we get a few more teases of the myth girls, the scene cuts back to show Ina leaving a kiss on one of the messages, before finally giving us a display of them, half written in english, half in japanese, implying two different speakers. The tender little kiss before also calls back to her numerous concert performances, implying a deeper relationship between mere friendship has allowed the two to remain in contact even when separated by worlds and fates.

Shortly after, she comes into contact with one of the temari balls from the cult, distinguished by the red and black markings. The next and final time we see her is on the train, alone by herself with the sun going down, making the world appear red around her. But as soon as she enters the tunnel, a jellyfish appears to be floating beside her window in the dark. Despite looking sullen and numb only moments earlier, her eyes widen at the beautiful glowing creature, enchanted and moved.

Given this is our last time seeing her, it is very possible that events take place after that lead to Priestess and/or Yuusha Ina. For one, of the three, she is the only one without a halo, and secondly, when Yuusha appears on the train right after, it is night, and now the train is filled with passengers.

It is possible the two are already the same at this point, and that it is merely the passing of time. But, if it isn’t, then either Kimono is an earlier Ina, and other parts of her story follow before she becomes Yuusha/Priestess. Or, she is another Ina altogether. However, due to the MV ending with only 3 Inas alongside the other 2 being deeply connected with Cthullu, I hesitate to believe this is the case.
Priestess/Default Ina

For the first time ever, we finally see Ina’s first outfit in one of her MV’s! Appearing right after Kimono makes contact with the Temari ball, we first glimpse her through various temaris, each colored pink and orange, far different then the ones seen in Temari. Given that the priestess appears to be studying these, having been collecting a number of other jellyfish, it is likely she has been in contact with the Wahtcher for some time.
Given the different appearance, these balls are likely exclusive to the Wahtcher, while the others are connected to the Ina’s of the cult.

As for the priestess herself, she appears to be a bit more experienced than some of the other incarnations. The very fact that both she and the takodachi have a halo suggests they went through some kind of transformation before we met them. With Meconopsis being the only other Ina in an MV to have a halo, there is solid evidence Priestess Ina is derived from her in some aspect, taking place after that MV at some point.

Additionally, it is worth noting the priestesses’ later appearance once unleashed by Yuusha. Following Meconopsis pulling a blue string, her pupils featuring a dot of light only seen before on the Overlord, Priestess Ina is released with a bang, a flash of light and in a swirling bubble, suggesting she has great power. Three colored rings orbit her, each matching her first 3 songs, and following her detonation of Cthullu, those same colors rain down on the Wahtcher.

Priestess Ina not only radiates power, but outright dwarfs the monster that Wahtcher could only cage, appearing first as a black silhouette, absolutely looming over Cthullu before eclipsing them in a red umbrella moments later. With the callback to Myth’s Bad Ending, digital setup, intense eyes, and immense powers, it isn’t unreasonable to imagine she holds some form of connection to, if not outright a continuation of, the Overlord.
After all, who better to clean up your mess than the one with a pocket universe for herself and her takos.

Speaking of which, she also appears to be not only in some kind of spiritual grounds, perhaps even the very home they first came from, but she also has a black void behind her, further hinting at the source of her origin and strength.
Yuusha Ina

The most prominent of the modern Ina’s in Abyssal Hymn, Yuusha Ina appears to be our Ina near the end of her timeline, after a number of previous experiences. Her first appearance in the pre-chorus follows immediately after Kimono Ina in the train, now at night, and with others aboard the train. The differences in the environment suggest a time jump might have happened between the shots, perhaps other events taking place between the jellyfish sighting and Yuusha stepping off the train.

Beyond the already known elements, like Yuusha wearing the base dress of the first Ina design beneath her coat, there are a few other elements that suggest she is a culmination of past Inas, perhaps even past lives now brought together. The first comes when she draws her first pen, a flash of light crossing the screen that looks almost like a fairy, which if intentional, is absolutely a nod to the “heavenly fairy” of Meconopsis. For even more Meconopsis hints, chorus 2 has her holding a blue string, and when the camera pans up close, her eye sports the same red tint at the bottom of Meconopsis eye. This could also indicate another lingering presence to some capacity.

Take a closer look in that same shot, and you will also notice a glowing circle in her pupil. Though it may just be a bit of lighting, it is worth noting that one other character -The Overlord-, actually shares this feature. Which, if she is a culmination of other inas that came before, may explain her transformation in chorus 2, as well as Priestess Ina being unleashed to take down Cthullu.

Finally, her being a culmination of other Inas explains 2 important factors. A: the multiple takos in her dress, despite only having 1 as a primary companion before who seemingly vanished before the last chorus, indicating she must’ve created many before. And of course, since takos can hold souls, who would better fit as an explanation than the Ina who took over the world?
B: The multi-colored pens and array of colors that set her apart. Unlike her previous forms, a swarm of different colors follow Yuusha to the end, primarily the blue, violet, and reddish pink, all associated with other songs and their Ina’s.

If placed in a recurring timeloop or semi-linear narrative, it may be that previous songs represent different parts of Ina’s self discovery. Becoming the priestess, nearly experiencing a bad end, and finally ascending as she accepts herself within Meconopsis, being reborn as Yuusha.
The Other Ina'nis

Alongside Ina exists another form, a reflection of another reality, lost somewhere in her past. This Ina, who thanks to the freshly dropped concept art, we can dub as “Shrine Ina”, is the culmination of the growth of a girl who remained in the cult, or perhaps one who returned to take Our Ina’s place.
The Young Shrine Maiden/Bandaged Ina

Throughout Abyssal Hymn, we see a girl with bandaged fingers, very similar to the appearance of Temari Ina in Temari’s MV. Interestingly, an Ina with long hair in Temari’s MV also seemed to have bruised fingers, implying the scars and bruises never really passed as she aged. However, after waking up in the strange parallel world, the bandages are completely gone and her hands appear fine, suggesting a transformation took place before that cleansed her injuries.
Really, the most likely candidate for that? Is the final transformation at the end of Temari.

Of course, there also exists the possibility the scars don’t just exist for one concurrent Ina. Rather, it may indicate any child's later days within the cult, their bodies and hands bruised until either they broke, or their minds.

In either instance, Ina has been seeking out one of the cult’s “daughters”, a younger girl from a hidden past, now sealed and caged somewhere out of reach. Implied to be connected to the events that allowed Cthulhu to spawn in the first place, she lies drifting in a dark cage in the void. Given descriptions of Past Ina and her monochrome world and dutiful life, there is a strong possibility that this very child is Past Ina, perhaps from the origin timeline.

However, without Cthulhu gone, Ina cannot save her, still trapped to her fate. Only once she accepts the help of Ao-chan and the tako can she remove Cthulhu, saving both the friend she’s been searching for, and her past self.
*Or.*

The one trapped in the cage is actually the younger self of the shrine Inanis, the very mistake the second Ina’nis sought to resolve. If so, then the entire time, Ina has been trying to save someone based off of distant memories that no longer resemble who she became. After all, if you look at the final scene closely enough from that girl's perspective, only Wahtcher’s hand appears at first. Rather than another Ina, the caged Ina might be some part of Wahtcher trapped in the past, and by reaching out and connecting with Ina, she saves herself.
Cultist Ina/Temari Ina

Almost certainly The Second Inanis spoken of in Temari, she returns here briefly, her origin finally revealed. Bandaged Ina/cultist Ina, upon touching the book while trapped in the cage, is immediately transformed. Her haori gains new metal balls on each sleeve, her eyes immediately become a vivid red, and her hair becomes sheet white.

Yet her life in this new form is cut short abruptly, the shattered temple sending her plunging into the abyss immediately after transforming. When we finally see a girl with the same appearance in verse 1, her body is as still as a floating flower, eyes wide open, and stiff. A pale corpse beneath a red eclipse, laying adrift on a dark void. Lifeless.

But life in the Inaverse doesn’t end so simply. Especially not for those who touch upon the magic of the Ancients. As implied within Temari, it would appear that their soul was able to persist in some form, and if the Second Inanis is the one who shoved away ours all along, it is likely the one who fell into the void helped warn her. Whether through direct intervention, or being reborn through the void, especially as the tako, the result is the same.

In Temari, we see multiple girls with bruised hands, but the ones in the rituals appear to be older than the ones seen in Abyssal Hymn, their dark hair grown all the way down to their waist. Assuming this is the Second Inanis after all, she likely spent some time as the head of the priestess after taking over, arming herself with experience and knowledge, speaking both to the child of the past, and whoever lays within the abyss, quite possibly the tako. Slowly but surely, they work in tandem to set a trap using their connections, preparing to weave a new fate into reality.
The Wahtcher/Shrine Maiden Ina'nis

After four years, we finally get our first clear view of the Wahtcher. Beginning as the previously discussed cultist Ina, she would be reborn as the water rushed over her while sealing away Cthullu, her entire image shifting along with her. Take the time to pause, and along with her hair getting longer, you’ll notice that the transformation is entirely after the wave crosses over.

Designwise, the Wahtcher is almost a direct parallel not only to Ina, but temari Ina as well. Beyond everything else, she is pale and white from dress to hair, suggesting an almost ghostly, spiritual presence, as well as having been washed of her past sins. The white hair also expresses a great deal of stress and mutation upon her body, generally only seen within older populations, tying back in with the idea of time being manipulated, her body forced to endure a great deal of stress and hardship through the powers she wields.

Along with the white, deep, vibrant pink suggests a purer, kinder soul, removed from her blood soaked past, now atoning for whatever crimes she feels guilty of. Combined with the white and later symbols, it may also be meant to evoke Sakura blossoms and Lotus flowers, both symbols of change and transformation, displaying her own growth in turn.

The last color is seen through a splash of Violet around her waist, invoking the idea that she still cherishes their past memories, and hopes to meet one day again. Thus, no matter how much she has seemingly accepted her fate to remain in the dark, forgotten forever, a spark of hope still lays buried within.
Glasses Ina

Seen only briefly during the bridge, we get a quick look at an Ina meeting the first tako in a snowy forest, seemingly the same place or environment of the island from long ago. Now all that remains of its legacy is a single rock.

This Ina stands out from her peers, wielding white/pink umbrella and red glasses, along with a book bag. Combined with her school-girl attire, it is immediately clear that a great deal of time has passed, suggesting that Ina may have been reborn, or that the past was changed when her friend left. That, or the two are from entirely separate realities altogether, but given the takodachi managed to find Ina again, it's more likely a case of time manipulation and/or parallel realities.

The choice of color for the umbrella is also incredibly telling. Previously, we’ve seen Kimono Ina in Temari and the younger cult girl carrying the red wagasa, a color associated heavily with the cult and implied to be the Ancient Ones to some capacity. Wagasas, like umbrellas, are used to keep the rain off the wielder, perhaps playing some role in containing the voids' power.

Yet now she holds an umbrella that carries the patterns seen with the Kimono pattern, but pastel and white, colors associated with purity and divinity. All the while walking through a winter landscape, perfectly befitting the wishes frozen in time thanks to the Wahtcher, lying dormant with Cthulhu in Beyond the Void. Given the Wahtcher’s goal in “Making a world where Ina can be happy,” it seems this may be the Ina she left behind, protected when she locked away Cthulhu.
A perfect world where the rain can never claim her again. A perfect world where life is still and silent, awaiting the dreams of a coming spring.
Takodachis
After almost 5 years, we finally get our first rendezvous with the very first takodachi, drawn all the way back in her “Happy Birthday” artwork on 10/31/2021.
The First Takodachi

Unlike its later brethren, the first tako is very distinguishable thanks to its dark, voidlike surface, and silver eyes. Silver eyes that are… unsettlingly similar to Past Ina’s own. Acting as the companion of the young shrine maiden, given their relative closeness and fondness spoken of in Ina’s many projects up to this point, there is still a very strong possibility that the tako isn’t just anyone, but another girl... Of which, 2 options are most likely.
First, our Ina.

Remember everything before. Past Ina lived a monochrome life, a dull world, one where she lived only to experience her cultly duties. Yet the young shrine maiden is actually a bit colorful, and wields the same center ball from Temari. On the other hand, we never truly discovered who the owner of the black and white, monochrome ball belonged to.
Well, isn't it obvious?
Whoever the takodachi is, a monochrome creature made from the void. Thus, it is equally likely that rather than the girl she is looking for, our very own Past Ina was the first to fall into the void.
And the first to become a takodachi.

After all, red-eyed girl in Abyssal Hymn does hold a tako… But red eyes may not be exclusive to the shrine Ina, as we see our very own’s shift hues multiple times. Instead, it may simply be the sign of her communicating with another world, or under another influence.

Therefore, a strong counter-argument should be made that rather than being our Past Ina, the first tako was actually the first shrine Ina. Evidence includes the fact that while Ina’s animal familiars are takodachis, the shrine Inanis appears intertwined with jellyfish. Not to mention, it was she who we actually see fall into the void, body appearing to go lifeless the moment she hit the surface, whisked away to another world.

And from there, the only way the shrine girl could return was in the blobby, inky form crafted with love by the First Inanis. Should the first tako be her past friend after all, it'd add a nice twist to the chorus. Both transformed through time, Ina looking to find her own past, and the tako telling their future self they will no longer be alone.
Transformed Takodachi

Alongside the first tako, fans would also be greeted by the familiar violet shade of our own tako, complete with the halo over its head. This tako, we’ll call the Transformed Takodachi, appears to have transformed alongside our very own Ina, likely some time after returning to the surface. Rather than being a separate takodachi, they are likely the very same companion as the First tako, and grew alongside Ina, experiencing their own growth and self-discovery alongside our Ina.

One point worth mentioning is that after Ina receives her flashback in the bridge, Yuusha is seen on the beach with the tako next to them. Prior to this, the only time we had seen the tako was with the priestess design and at the shrine, not once alongside Yuusha. Thus, either Yuusha remembered a past life or memory, and returned to bring back the tako, or, the tako had, somewhere, become trapped in the void, and Yuusha rescued them.

The fact that the tako transformed alongside Ina transformed as well, does reinforce the idea they aren’t past Ina, but her friend and faithful companion all along, and plays along greatly with the lyrics. Rather than just being Ina’s own journey, it is both of theirs, along with their counterparts from the past (Past Ina) and future (Wahtcher), growing and transforming to save not just each other, but themselves.
Jellyfish

Alongside the takodachis, a new critter would join the ranks of the Inaverse, promptly featured throughout Abyssal Hymn. Unlike our Ina, Jellyfish are the close companion of the Wahtcher, acting as her messengers from Beyond the Void.

Symbolically, jellyfish are often associated with the moon, their translucent bodies in the water looking eerily similar to the stellar observer above. In fact, the exact species of jellyfish created for the MV look very similar to Moon Jellyfish, sharing the same markings on the bulb. Though, the exact shape of the bulb can also be said to be quite similar to Stellar Medusa, a name that obviously associates the creature with more heavenly properties.

Physically, jellyfish are strange creatures, lacking bones or a central nervous system, they float through the water, using tentacles to ensnare prey. Though they can propel themselves through the water, they are often at the mercy of the current. Yet, their ability to survive in just about any environment, including the dark depths of the ocean, presents them as a creature that is both adaptable and transformative, befitting the growth the Wahtcher has gone through.

In that sense, the jellyfish represents an adaptation in the Wahtcher’s strategy and ability to communicate. Within them, she can store a temari ball, allowing her to send messages through the void to reach Ina. Amusingly, the jellyfish of the Inaverse feature a unique hybrid design. Each one appears to come from the lotus flowers in Beyond the Void, which the Wahtcher is able to open and shut to store things within, similar to a message in a bottle, thrown to the sea. Rather than merely sting, the tentacles resemble string, and likely function just like the woven temari balls. And of course, those very temari balls appear to be the gifts Ina receives on the other end, collecting a number of the jelly’s and keeping them safe over time.

The jellys, though not nearly as emotive as takodachis, appear to be able to travel alongside Ina. However, their inability to communicate altogether may be further proof that the Wahtcher had her ability to communicate with Ina stolen, or her voice is lost due to being within Beyond the Void. Instead, they are like her, a silent, ghostly companion and light for Ina in the dark.

A light we can trace back to The Ghost of the Deep Sea sung at Drawn to Dawn. 
It isn’t a coincidence that the corpse of the Ina who fell into the void looks just like a jellyfish in the abyss, translucent white hair drifting aimlessly, only able to float upon the water. With its own translucent appearance and drifting presence, the jellyfish is often seen as spiritually significant, including as a ghost, its white, floating image just like an apparition.
Thus, Abyss Ina, or whoever she represents, may have been singing about the Wahtcher, after finally getting a glimpse of her.
Servants of Ryujin

Within Japanese mythology, the jellyfish is said to be a servant of Ryujin, the dragon god of the sea. Said dragon god of the sea, who in some traditions is seen as the equivalent to Watatsumi, a singular god of the sea.

One particular myth explains how the jellyfish lost their bones. One day, Ryujin asked for the Jellyfish to bring him a monkey’s liver to eat, only for said monkey to trick the jellyfish, returning empty handed. Upon hearing the story, Ryujin was enraged, and beat every bone in their body.

Though this likely doesn’t completely align to the Inaverse, it does suggest that the Wahtcher may have become a servant to a more powerful being, and through her past mistakes during her service, lost her ability to return to the real world of our Ina.
Ryujin and Ryugu-jo

As mentioned previously, Ryujin is the dragon god of the sea, and is sometimes associated with Watatsumi, offering one possible explanation behind the lyrics used in Abyssal Hymn. Now, with Cthulhu also having godly associations, connected to the sea, and seen as a cross between a dragon and octopus, this could very well explain him altogether.

However, there is one counter idea.
With duality such a present theme throughout the Inaverse, perhaps there isn’t one god, but two. The Ryujin, the dragon sea god, and Cthulhu. After all, while one Ina gets her strength from the abyss, another gets hers from light, and appears far more divine.

In fact, if you slow down the scene where Ina looms over Cthulhu in chorus 2, you can faintly see a translucent figure in the background, looking like the serpentine body and head of an eastern dragon, just like Ryujin.

The background too, also resembles a palace ground, vibrant and heavenly. Though it could just be a chunk from the beginning of the MV, when the island was split in half, perhaps it might be something else altogether…

The Dragon Palace Castle, or Ryuju-go, is the undersea palace of Ryujin. A palace also associated with the fish-scale-palace that is home to Watatsumi in the kojiki.
Unlike the dark imagery associated with Cthulhu, Ryugu-jo is far more vibrant, with walls made of choral, and trees with emeralds for leaves and rubies for berries. Fish scales illuminate the interior halls, and overhead, the palace is sheltered by a crystal dome, all while lying deep beneath the water. In some versions, the palace is even seen to have multiple seasons, one on each side.

Perhaps then, what happened isn’t merely that the girls revived Cthulhu. Rather, to bring about his return, they first needed to capture or prevent Ryujin from interfering. Given their whole life being raised in the cult, it is possible they weren’t fully aware of the consequences to come, or were just more afraid of failing.
This also explains why they appear to be trapped within the realm of the priestess in chorus 2, while Wahtcher is trapped within Cthulhu.

Although, given Yuusha’s appearance, it may be that they actually saved or helped Ryujin in some way, and gained a divine blessing in turn. Although that reasoning could just as well fit the Wahtcher, thanks to her appearance and transformation implying she has been reborn and purified.

In any case, the evidence that Ryujin even exists and is a separate entity is thin, but it's more than enough to craft some interesting ideas and theories, and may be a sneaky surprise for many if the dragon truly was lurking behind Ina in the end.
Cthulhu

After years of teases and hints, we finally get a glimpse of not just any Ancient One, but the very Cthulhu, or a monster deliberately designed to look like them. Appearing the moment the shrine maiden made contact with Ao-chan, likely after a ritual, his presence immediately transforms her, lengthening her hair and turning it white, along with her eyes becoming red.

Its head is split into 8 subdivisions, and upon transforming the shrine girl, unfurls into what appears to be some sort of twisted flower, where the center has been replaced by the void itself. Given that we see the young shrine maiden later in the abyss, along with Priestess Ina’s own void bubble at the end of the song, this may be some form of imprisonment beyond the universe. Which also explains why Ina cannot save the child until she banishes/kills Cthulhu themselves.

The transformation is paired with an ornate flower design behind them, while multiple rings of eyes, three, become more detailed as they expand outward, as if coming into focus as they approach. Surrounding them is one last banner, where eyes are placed between criss-crossing lines, like threads intertwining them. All of which implies just as the temari and threads would later help save the Inas, it may have very well been part of their doom to begin with.

Across the various scenes of Abyssal Hymn, Cthulhu remains a present threat, the elder shrine Inanis unable to stop them outright, only able to freeze them in time. And if her warning in the pre-chorus is any indication, that grasp is slipping. In spite of her bravery and desire to protect the world, loneliness is breaking her down, and her resistance is in jeopardy.

By the end, Ina finally succeeds and following her transformation, releases Cthulhu, who flies up into the heavens, only to find themselves now eclipsed by the power of priestess Ina. Whether she is amped up on the prayers of takos, whether she is the evolution of the Overlord, or even the takodachi all along, the result is the same.
"That is not dead which can eternal lie, / And with strange aeons even death may die."
Playing on the ironic quote from Lovecraft, Cthulhu appears to vanish into a tako singularity before exploding, putting them to rest once and for all. “Though death may die, love is now and forever.”
"Papa" and the Ninomae "family"

At long last, we finally get our face to face with the “Ninomae family”, a cult who live upon their island, hidden away from the world. Donning white coverings from head to toe, wearing masks that hide their faces, only featuring a single drawing of an eye just like the one from Wahtcher’s debut.

But beyond all of the other members, one stands at the top, leading the path forward, facing the eclipse at the front. Due to Temari briefly mentioning a “Papa” and their position at the head of the family, we will be dubbing them “Papa”. Though, it is worth mentioning that title could easily be referring to AO or “God” (Whoever the girls were taught to worship). With long white hair and outstretched hands, he welcomes the coming apocalypse, smile seen where the wind blows back the mask. However, during two brief scenes, one at the beginning, and one during the bridge, we see multiple images flash rapidly. Within one, the mask has been taken fully off, and we see the true monster who lies beneath.

Much like the Inas we’ve seen so far, this “Papa” actually has markings beneath his cheeks as well, only this time, they are less moles, and actually shaped like the very eye within a diamond worn on their masks. Yet unlike the Inas, Papa has two markings, one on the left of their face, one on the right.

Their eyes are completely blank white, suggesting they are utterly possessed, giving away their own vision to live in a misty dream. The third eye upon their forehead appears to be a result of their awakening achieved through the ritual, proof of their contact with a higher power. Now, throughout Ina’s MVs, they never gain a third eye on their forehead. However, we do have something that could act similarly. The eye insigna/medallion, seen throughout each Ina iteration. In Temari, for example, it sat on their dress, and both split open, and had a spirit enter it.
This may inform how the ritual occurs, but, that is not all…
Parallel Worlds
Throughout both Temari and now Abyssal Hymn, there is overwhelming evidence that supports parallel worlds.
So, remember Papa, who has both markings on his face? The inas only have it on their right (left when we face them), so, how do you make a match?
You send them to a mirrored world.
Further proving that all the instances where “Ina” was flipped was not an accident, but intentional. Proof of two worlds that lie parallel to one another.
Unreality and the Abyss

Potentially two entirely separate realms. I hesitate to call the eclipsed world the abyss, as within Temari, we directly saw the abyss as exactly that. A void devoid of any shape, featureless, and dark. On the other hand, the eclipsed world resembles the [Third Realm] discussed previously in Temari's MV, a world drowned in red.

While in Abyssal Hymn, we see the white haired girl both laying on a dark void surface in two different looking settings. One is a more white lit world, clearly the same snowy world Past Ina/Temari came from thanks to the Camellias. Yet when she wakes up later, the flowers are not present, and the world looks redder. On top of that, both the takodachi and Ao-chan are present here.
Not to mention, the very image of the island being split shows the left half in blue, the right half red, and in the middle, black.

Thus, the void is not the opposite of reality, but a realm that allows people to traverse between realities, and perhaps even to an unreality of sorts. Such as a realm where time moves backwards, to the beginning.
Watatsumi

Watatsumi is a word with multiple definitions. The first to often come up, is that of a god, usually Ryujin, the dragon god of the sea. However, Watatsumi can also refer to the gods of the upper, middle, and lower seas. Within Abyssal Hymn, we see an instance of 3 girls in a cavern, looking like the abyss, each one being set over a pool of water with masked cult worshippers. Very in character for any lovecraftian/eldritch universe.
Of particular note, each cage is raised to different heights. One is above the water, one lies upon its surface, and one lies underwater.
Upper, middle, and lower seas.

Additionally, each cage is designed like the unopened bud of a poppy flower, yet to bloom into the world. At the top, lies a staff with a dark void at the center, and surrounding it, a series of 8 tentacles.
And then from all places, came a major tease from an Arknight: Endfield stream of all places.
“But if you flip two 3’s it makes an 8”
Let us rewind.

8, as in Tako Takover, can be flipped to make an infinity symbol. 8 is formed not by 4 plus 4, but 3 mirrored with another 3, implying that in addition to requiring 3 vessels on one side, you need another 3 to parallel them in a mirrored dimension.
Between the concept art, island being split in twain, and papa having two markings under each eye when the girls only had it under their right, it all becomes clear.

Three girls are raised to different heights in mirrored worlds, one is likely our reality, the other, a mirrored reality. The heights of the cages altogether bringing together this definition of Watatsumi. In this instance, gods of the upper, middle, and lower seas, as displayed with the cages at various points in the water.

Since we know there are at least five girls, it is likely six was required for the full ritual, 3 girls in each realm used as vessels in paired rituals. In fact, if you pay close enough attention to catch the eye shown in the rapid image cuts, you’ll notice there are actually 6 eyes altogether. Four at each corner around a central pupil, which is itself an eye, and of course, that girl’s real eye the others lie within.

Thus, the Wahtcher is very likely the very first one to have been paired with Ina in the past, and in the wake of the destruction they wrought, possibly desperate to save themselves or Ina, made a terrible mistake. This would lead to the Second Inanis discovering the truth, shoving aside our Ina, and vanishing to fix this mess, even if it meant being forgotten by the universe.
Temari balls

All throughout Abyssal Hymn, the colorful balls make their grand return, this time in a number of new ways and settings. From the classic designs to new ones and even balls that are seemingly stitched together, the balls help to organize and explain the events of the song, while also tying back to previous lore, bridging them together.

Within the first verse, viewers are greeted with a number of callbacks to Temari, including the balls themselves, the initial set clearly the same designs as the ones introduced in the first MV, although this time, we only see 4 girls at the start.

Their status as memory holders is reinforced when one is dropped down a set of steps, with every bounce Past Ina receiving a vision born from another girl's temari, each collision drawing Ina’s attention away. Following this trail of memories, she eventually reaches the shore, where not one, not two, nor four or five or even six temari balls wait.
Across the rocks 12 temari balls sit, twice the number seen previously in Temari.

Given we don’t get anywhere close to seeing twelve girls together, it implies half of these temaris are from another version of themselves, each representing another reality and life, another set of memories. Which ultimately, would tie all the way back to the notes on Temari of the balls representing memories being woven together. Which brings us to-
The Woven Balls

Prior to the white haired priestess’ transformation into the Wahtcher, the bandaged girl releases a number of temari balls into the water. Most intriguingly is the same 5 pointed star made of white and red triangles seen falling down the steps. Only now, the shape of the pattern has changed entirely, and if you look closely enough, you’ll see it has a seam running down the side, with each half mirroring the other.
Following this, the scene cuts out to show the other balls that were released in the water, of which there are only six now, rather than the 12 shown before.
With both the balls now only being half the amount seen before, and a seam running between two parallel sides that break the previous shape, it means without a doubt, the balls were woven together.
IMMEDIATELY, we get multiple sufficient support for multiple theories and clues that help tie it all together.

FIRST, rather than taking place in a single world, there exists some kind of mirrored reality, which is further stated through other upcoming visuals. This explains why these balls have another half they can sow together, as well as the sudden change in appearance.

SECOND, the temari balls are able to carry some aspect of the individual between worlds, displayed clearly when Ina received messages from the bouncing temari, and later in her communications with the jellyfish.

THIRD, they are able to travel through bodies of water, and is how Ina becomes aware of this other reality in the first place. Beyond just appearing on the rocks, they later appear in the same woods of Temari as if thrown through a puddle, and traveling within the jellyfish sent by the Wahtcher.

Knowing both the existence, purpose, and traversal of the temaris, it becomes a bit more apparent what Temari Ina is doing with them. With the balls for each reality being stitched together, Temari appears to be literally weaving together the memories of “her past” to her own, bridging the gap between the two. Thus, the threads wrapping around both the pillars and zipping through the void, once used to express communication, were likely reshaped throughout that very song to tie these worlds together.

This is made even more evident when you recall the imagery of the red balls appearing from the ring in verse 3 and chorus 2, each tied to another, as if paired with another reality. And with the ring itself seeming to be a device that allows travel between worlds, a sign of a being tied to a higher plain, we can finally weave together Abyssal Hymn and Temari.

Rather than 1 reality or timeline, the Inaverse takes place in at least 2, utilizing temari balls and threads to speak between them. Choosing to tie the balls together, the second Inanis is able to reach the other side, and by traveling between the realms, perhaps even having her own self stitched with the other side, she ascends, leading to the transformation in Temari. Upon finally reaching her destination, she wakes up in the parallel world/unreality.

If this very unreality functions as a mirror dimension, then time here flows backwards.
Which means: by tying together reality and unreality, along with the different timelines (or the past reality became “unreality” with Cthulhu’s ascension, sending the Earth back to the beginning.), temari Ina is able to flip the two, freezing a region of space around the very temari balls that the bandaged Ina had set out, In the process of fusing together these worlds, the Wahtcher is reborn in a wave of water, successfully returning to her original timeline, but unable to leave Cthulhu, watching over the caged girl to atone for her past sins.
But not before sending off her beloved tako and Ao-chan, before closing her eyes and dreaming.
Painted temaris

Completely subverting the visuals seen within the cult, Abyssal Hymn introduces a number of new temari balls, this time painted in vibrant patterns of pink, orange, and red. Given Ina has one beside her growing jellyfish aquarium, these are no doubt being sent by the Wahtcher herself. Far from the dreary, blood-stained world she worked to stop, the painted temaris, like the halo tako and jellyfish, represent her own evolution and transformation, purified of pain with art and creation. Art that is now made with her full heart and love, carrying messages to our Ina.
Interestingly, it appears only our own priestess and Yuusha see these balls, while Kimono makes contact with the old temari ball from their younger past.
Ball Beyond the Void

When the Wahtcher freezes Cthulhu, we get a brief glimpse of Beyond the Void’s full structure. Just as hinted with the VRchat version of Beyond the Void, the location is actually set within a massive temari ball, seemingly using the temaris woven together from two timelines/realities to freeze Cthulhu in between.

While one half of the ball remains an icy white, the other is covered in dark tentacles that snake along the surface, showcasing the delicate balance of power keeping the beings trapped within. The background of Beyond the Void also features a massive eyeball shaped temari, segmented into 8 parts, likely the true form of Cthulhu the young shrine maiden appears trapped within. Rounding the 8 segments back into our previous discussion with Watatsumi, it appears one form of the ritual involving 6 souls is what ensnared her in the first place, since 3 and a mirrored 3 can overlap to make 8.

When Yuusha finally pulls the thread, time finally is unfrozen, seemingly releasing Cthulhu to wreak havoc on the world. Only for Ina to also release her godly priestess form (again, maybe the overlord cause she is pack heat.) and engulf Cthulhu herself, more than capable of handling them.
With the frozen ball of time unwoven, the two can finally reunite at long last.
Water

Finally, it’s time we discuss in full context one of the greatest elements throughout the Inaverse. From beginning to end, water is what brings about their doomed fate, but in time, their salvation.
In addition to the various elements of hidden feelings and fading secrets discussed in past songs, water is proven to have two practical effects through Abyssal Hymn.

First and foremost, just like many myths, legends, and religions state water has magical properties, and in particular, acts as a conduit between realities. Abyssal Hymn puts this on full display by the first verse, where a younger girl sees twice the number of temari balls upon the rocks, and following the previous sequence of the balls floating underwater, they seem to have risen to the surface. Yet, this surface is another world entirely, revealing not only the fates of other girls, but intertwining with another reality, warning the future to come. These balls eventually reach Kimono Ina as well, seen from a shot below the water’s surface, proof of their sender from the deep.

With their abilities to act as transports and allow for the passage of temaris, objects woven of memories, they also seem to act as transportation for souls, proven not only with the second Inanis being able to reach the other realm, but later with Yuusha vanishing into the water’s surface.

Of course, transportation works two ways, and just as the girls in the abyss have their memories reach the surface, these temaris later assist the one in the red world to bind Cthulhu, allowing her to trap their doomed future in the bubble of a more hopeful one to pass.

Equally important, as illuminated many times, reflections play a massive role within the Inaverse, and no source of reflection is more plentiful than the very source of all life. After all, the girls in the cages were specifically bound with the water, allowing them to reach the abyss, the necronomicon, and raise Cthulhu to the surface in the first place.

Yet, as much as it brought the girls destruction, it would in time save them, their own wishes falling through their own water to reach their future hero, diving back in to rewind the clock. With Yuusha literally vanishing within the moon’s reflection on the surface, as well as the later invisible wall that stops her rippling between Yuusha and the Wahtcher, its presence carries on to the very end. Calling back to theming present in most previous stories, water proves that not only is some form of a mirrored reality canon to the Inaverse, but everpresent, lurking in practically every moment, maybe even in your own cup…
Not only a source of life, waters shared properties of being enterable while being a reflective surface, allowing the two to both fall victim to it, and save one another from that fate.
Reborn in water

While both girls have a strong connection with light and water, it is Temari Inanis who appears to have a stronger connection with the element. From waiting down in the depths, her connection with jellyfish, and even being a source of her powers. Beyond just being a highway for her to communicate with the other world and travel through the void, water is also the thing that brings about her transformation, the Wahtcher born as a wave washes over her.

Literally trapped within the abyss, it becomes difficult not to consider that Abyss Ina has some amount of connection to the Wahtcher, perhaps even a younger version of herself. After all, her very own story in Drawn to Dawn suggested she was waiting for Ina at the bottom of the sea. Though, the lack of white hair and red eyes might point the evidence back to our very own Past Ina, the first priestess, the pink dragon eye suggesting she is tied to the shrine maiden that was lost to the void, but didn’t transform immediately. Rather, she remained a priestess for some time, explaining how the first tako was reborn with the soul of their friend, since Ina is associated with takodachis and the void.

If not a version of either girl before Abyssal Hymn, then likely she is some form of fusion after the fact, much like how Yuusha is a combination of the hero and the priestess, Abyss could be a combination of the shrine maiden and cultist.
Ripples

Complimenting the usage of water as a path between the realms, ripples make constant appearances not just in Abyssal Hymn, but even as far back as Violet’s MV. Just like in real life, ripples signify the presence of something making contact with the surface of water, disrupting the smooth appearing in a wave of rings. Yet, with water acting as a corridor for communication, ripples gain a new meaning.

Pay close attention during the scene where Kimono Ina looks back, and you’ll notice she turns as soon as the wave reaches her. Compare this with Violet’s MV, where the fading memories of Ina’s past reappeared with ripples, fading only as the waves smoothed. And of course, it is through a ripple that the Wahtcher is finally able to reach through to Ina, her own tears piercing the water-like barrier between them, and giving back some of her memories.

Tie this together with the sound of water being breached in Temari and mentions of echoes in Takodachi no Uta, and ripples are no longer just physical remains of contact, but a result of memories and sound breaching the barrier between them. In similar vein to echolocation, neither girl can reach other directly, and instead must rely on sending messages through the abyss separating them, yet also connecting them. The only problem, as echoes would imply, is that these echoes are split by the physical limitations of their universes, and while the Wahtcher appears capable of watching Ina, she struggles to reach her anymore, her voice lost within the void. Echoes splashing across the gulf in space and time is all that reaches the other side, Ina seeking out a mirage made of her memories rather than the true source.
All that remains for the Wahtcher to do is cry, and while her voice could not reach the other side, something else did…
Teardrops

During the bridge sequence, Ina finally has her first close encounter with the Wahtcher/shrine Ina. Falling through the void, she reaches a place where water droplets around her appear to freeze, evidence of her arriving at the shell of frozen time. 
More diligent eyes will also notice that each tear resembles an octopus eye, with a horizontal eye in the center of each.

Given that in numerous scenes the Wahtcher is crying, on top of concept art also showing she’s a bit emotional, it is very possible these are her own tears. Now, look back at the scene of her in a puddle of water, filled with lotus after lotus after lotus, evidence of many conversations and attempts lost in time. Rather than just water, the very pond she waits in might be her own tears, and by grazing against it, got a glimpse of her memories.
Cthulhu's tears

Abyssal Hymn finally confirms, once and for all, that among all things, the mole on Ina’s cheek is actually very important, thanks to the imagery of Papa with a third eye, having 2 marks beneath each cheek surrounded by diamonds, resembling a miniature eye. 
Thus, the “sisters” are not chosen by mere blood or connection, but by a shared mark on their right cheek below their eye. One that Ina took care to cover with hair or obscure for the other sisters, cause she wanted to keep us guessing. This also reinforces the need and purpose for a mirror dimension, as papa would need a realm where the mole seems to appear on the opposite cheek. For the sake of this instance, we will be calling these moles *Cthulu tears*.

This comes into play when Ina finally reaches the barrier separating her from the Wahtcher during the bridge. 
As she finally finds the place she has been searching for, a tear splashes Ina’s face on her left cheek below her eye, mirroring the mole on her right cheek. That tear, appearing just after Yuusha mimicked Wahtcher’s pinky finger, came not from thin air, but beyond the void, a tear that came through frozen time. This final little touch may have been just the magic Ina needed, not only reminding her of her past, but also causing her to remember previous lessons and knowledge, arming her with knowledge. Above all else, reaffirming that they would never be alone.
The moon

Once again the moon returns, this time in spectacular fashion, connecting to projects throughout the Inaverse and their climax in Abyssal Hymn. As teased previously in Drawn to Dawn and Temari, the moon appears to function as a portal of sorts, similar to Ina’s own halo, allowing for early forms of travel and connection between the worlds even without the ascension that comes with the angelic ring.

Instead, we directly see that eclipses are able to send messages through the abyss, proven by the Temari appearing afterwards, and also act as a gate for Yuusha to reach the abyss, vanishing as she touches the very water’s surface. The moon would also appear near the end of the song, coinciding with Ina’s transformation, a waxing moon overlaid with the sun, just like in the Drawn to Dawn opening video. Thus, while the abyss and water are a source of the Wahtcher’s power, the moon and stars are once again empowering our Ina/Yuusha, the heavens themselves gifting her their strength.
The Eclipse

Of course, the moon is far from the only entity to light up our sky, and beyond any other, it is the sun, first and foremost, that acts as Earth’s benefactor. The light that allows us to see, the warmth that gives life to the planet and its many seasons. The sun is a cosmic entity who, within our own solar system, is unmatched in prominence, and often seen as akin to the gods and creators. After all, to some extent, it is.

Thus, unlike the lunar eclipse seen in Drawn to Dawn, the solar eclipse is seen throughout Abyssal Hymn. Still, similarly to blood moons and lunar eclipses, the solar eclipse is often seen as a bad omen, the sun, its holy role as a bringer of life, silenced by the moon's passage. In the Inaverse, this definition remains apt, and may even describe what occurs,

The celestial realm and their order are overthrown, allowing a dark god to ascend to the surface, and given how Cthulhu leaps to the heavens in chorus 2, it may have been his goal all along. That, or given the lovecraft mythos, maybe just to return to the stars. Either way, ensuring the light would never return had he succeeded.

Yet, the eclipse also seems to have a positive side to it, as during the second verse, we see the moon gradually cover the sun, and then pass when we view the tako shrine, the light returning. Right after, a temari ball falls from the sky, and appears to be the one that first reached Kimono Ina.

Thus, rather than a force of evil, eclipses seem to act as a bridge between the two worlds, helping messages reach one another, even if it is brief. Though, once the first connection is made, it seems the two are able to communicate with each other more often.
Light

A constant presence throughout many of Ina’s songs and Music videos, light appears to be the defining element that transforms Our Ina into the priestess, in direct contrast to the Shrine girl transforming with water. Following along with the rabbit on the moon being connected with the divine realm, light being a source of Yuusha’s power presents her as a hero that received divine support, granted for past actions in saving the world.

However, it would be presumptuous to assume it is Yuusha’s element alone. After all, it is the Wahtcher’s white glow that reaches her first, and despite Ina’s own heavenly aesthetic, the young shrine maiden holds a temari intertwined with the full moon hanafuda, not to mention past connections to the heavens in Temari and other places.

Thus, rather than one person, it may be a source of power, which given Ina’s own enjoyment of Cosmic Princess Kaguya and references to the rabbit on the moon, might just be a celestial realm. Therefore, much like the rainbow, light signifies power, and in the context of white light, likely entails purity, grace, and some level of divinity, granted to either girl in exchange for their own work and sacrifice.
Shrine
Relatively unknown prior to Abyssal Hymn, the advent of not just a shrine, but a shrine maiden, provokes several questions about the Inaverse.

Seen briefly at the beginning of the second verse, the shrine appears rather distant in both time and appearance from the temple seen at the beginning, a far more humble and quiet location overlooking the Ocean and city from atop a hill.

The shrine itself features the familiar Inanis eye emblem at the top, while two boxes to left and right appear reminiscent of the lamps seen at Drawn to Dawn, also associated with a nearby city. Clearly, this isn’t the same mikurashima mentioned in Temari, far too small and nowhere near as densely populated, but instead Tokyo, distinguished by the rising red/white tower and bay in the background.

Above Ina’s head, five gohei sit strewn beneath a rope, each matching the stars seen on her crown, a nod towards the other girls of the cult. With gohei being used to sanctify a person or place, it appears these have been placed to honor and bring rest to the other girls. Otherwise, it may be their own blessing upon Ina.

Atop the shrine sit a number of personal objects, seemingly offerings of Ina’s own life to the Wahtcher. A camera and some coins offer insight into past times together, while a few takos, including a charm, appear to be a recurring gift for the Wahtcher, little trinkets of Ina’s life. In fact, in the following scene, we see one tako with a halo sitting beside 5 other trinkets, one per sister, suggesting the takodachi is helping to send the messages back and forth. If so, then Kimono Ina is already intertwined with Priestess and Yuusha by now, as the figurine already features her halo too. Finally, a single box lies to the top left, and while it could be a game console, there is a decent chance it’s actually a music box, much like the recurring theme of past productions.

To round it all off, a number of pens have been used to write messages to and fro, each one remarkably similar to the very ones wielded by Yuusha. Though not nearly as powerful at first, these very pens would help to thaw the frozen time keeping the two apart.
Ema
"I really, really miss you!"
"How can I find you?"

Strewn along the shrine are a number of Ema, plaques that are used to send prayers and wishes to the Gods. Each one invokes the patterns and imagery of Ina’s clothes, the temari balls, and flowers, though most are pink, orange, and white, closer in tone with the painted temaris. Given Ina and the shrine maiden/Wahtcher have been communicating through these Ema, it would seem that the latter has taken up a role as a minor spiritual deity, reading her messages Beyond the Void.

As Ina has noted multiple times as well, language plays a vital role in piecing her story together, and given that all of the shrine maiden’s vocals are in Japanese while Ina’s are in English, it’s immediately obvious who is talking to who. Gauging each one, we get a better understanding of both girls' inner thoughts.

At the shrine, Ina’s messages express not only her yearning, but ask for help in reaching the other, unsure where to look. Given Takodachi no Uta implying one of the singers is only hearing echoes, either the Wahtcher’s messages are unable to reach Ina in a helpful fashion, or she has decided to remain hidden out of the desire to protect Ina.
"I want to see you! Really..."
"See you later"

Her messages, however, match the tone and mood of both the Second Inanis and others across past concerts and covers, a girl who wishes to meet again, but has seemingly accepted her own fate. Regret is strewn all across the messages, but again, seems unable to reach Ina easily.
Well, given she is holding Cthulhu back and did say Ina’s world might end if she left, she has a justifiable reason for remaining put, until it becomes clear she can no longer do it alone.
All the while little doodles upon the ema show that they each have been in contact for some time, Ina clearly having already met the jellyfish, and also having her squishies and flaps in doodles.

At the end of the song, the emas come back into full focus, all their heartfelt messages between dimensions, like the temaris themselves, succeeding in breaking the barrier keeping them apart. As the words “Matane”, as in, “Until we meet again” cross the center, Yuusha appears from behind, a play on Wahtcher’s constant goodbyes, arriving at the later Wahtcher always sang of.
“I’ll be missing you until the end of time!”
“I’ll be waiting no matter how it takes!”
“Until we meet”
“My heart already knows your name”

Across all of the EN messages, we get a larger glimpse of just how bad the two have missed each other, with Ina confessing purely from the heart. Constantly searching no matter how long, our Ina makes it clear she will never, ever forget the other, an “unforgettable person”, as teased in One Last Kiss previously. “My heart already knows your name” proving that, even if there is a barrier that has split them across space and time, Ina will never give up, and even if her memory has been taken from her, her heart will tell her instead. A belief affirmed with “Until we meet” being the last to leave the screen as their promise comes to fruition.
“Praying for a reunion. It’s a bargain, even just for once.”
“Today, too, I’ll be waiting”
“I/We will definitely find it”
"See you later”

In spite of her earlier pessimism, even the Wahtcher’s own messages begin to come across more hopeful, determination rising before they finally meet, perhaps after they finally connected during the bridge. Connected at long last, the daily messages of her waiting are able to finally reach Ina’s side, answering our hero’s determination with her unbreakable perseverance, bolstered after finally making brief contact. From bargaining and praying for a reunion, she finally becomes convinced that together the two of them can meet again. Finally, with one final Matane, Yuusha flips the script, ensuring the Wahtcher’s eternal wait has been lifted, the two finally meeting again at the distant future they always dreamed of.

In the end, after countless failures and untold destinies, the two finally reunite once again, not only destroying the force that held them apart, but shattering the barrier, allowing the Wahtcher to finally escape her destiny of remaining imprisoned by her lonesome until the end of time.
“Mitsuketa! // I found you!”
Adonis

Tied to the Greek tragic character of the same name, who fell in love with both Aphrodite and Persephone: Goddesses of love and the underworld. When he died after being gored by a wild boar, he did so in Aphrodite’s arms, her tears mixing with his blood to create the anemone: A poppy that symbolizes brevity and withered hopes, fitting for a love that died too soon.
Though the interior of the Anemone shares some similarities with the Cthulhu head, the Adonis flower actually has 8 petals, and therefore, feels like the more intertwined plant.

As for Adonis flowers themselves, they represent painful memories and sorrowful remembrances, which could be taken any number of ways within Abyssal Hymn’s context. Most likely, it might be that the once pure wishes of the child who touched the book had since been stained by the pain and hardship of the world around them. With her spirit and mind broken, the perfect vessel to bring about a monster.
Which honestly, given Ina’s love for Evangelion, I’m just making a mental *Mr_fresh.Gif* note right here.
Camellias

Returning from [Temari], again heavily symbolizing death and misfortune, along with modesty, befitting the children who walk into their own demise. Not to forget either, old yokai are said to sometimes grow from old Camellia trees, perfectly fitting the first girls summoning of the eldritch beast.

Their fallen flower-heads yet again symbolize the unfortunate fates befalling the girls, and appear to be absolutely bountiful in the cold world of the past cult. With a number of ripples washing all over the fallen girl's form, it seems the shrine girl we started with was not the only one to fall to the void. The main difference? A single book, and the love to bring her back.
Rose

Atop Kimono Ina's head she wears a rose, bright and pink. Obviously, roses
are associated with love, and pink are no exception, in particular connecting
with first love. Similarly, they symbolize admiration and innocence, suggesting
a relationship that hasn't fully blossomed, but if Ina's kiss on the message is any
indication, it is strong and everpresent beneath the surface.
Lotus flowers

Seen throughout Beyond the Void across what appears to be a frozen lake (perhaps even of tears) is a large number of white pristine flowers, each icy and without color. These flowers later come to hold colored temari balls sent to the surface, turning into jellyfish to act as the Wahtcher’s messenger.

Although colorwise they don’t look quite like the lotus, the very nature of their symbolism and the way they open and close heavily resembles the Lotus. Otherwise, maaaaybe some other form of water flower, like the water lily, though the symbolism there is more scarce.

Lotus flowers grow from the bottom of bodies of water and rise to the surface. Symbolically, this is associated, especially within Buddhism, as rising from the world's impurities and attaining enlightenment. Likewise, they are also seen as a form of rebirth.

Together, these perfectly describe exactly who the Wahtcher is. The same girl from the start who fell into the void, who would be revived and reborn into the Wahtcher under a wave of water that wiped away her past sins.

This also, is another point that implies the girl in the cage Ina seeks was the younger version of the Wahtcher all along, one that she would grow from and cleanse. One Ina sought because she could no longer recognize the person she was looking for.
Wisteria OR Deadly Nightshade

As Ina finally seeks to banish Cthulhu for good, she appears with a large plant behind her. This plant, seen with long thin branches, numerous leaves, and possibly some form of fruit in dark, round berries, is debatable.

The latter, wisteria, is certainly more popular among anime and within japan. In particular, wisteria is a symbol for welcoming someone to a new town or home, and would certainly fit Cthulhu being taken within an even bigger, badder, girl of the void.

On the flipside, Deadly Nightshade certainly resembles both the leaves as well as the fruit within the branches, and as the name implies, is heavily connected with death. This would imply that rather than merely welcoming in Cthulhu, this priestess is outright killing them. In fact, Meconopsis itself even plays with the line “though death may die, love is now and forever,” implying she may be purging the worst so that love may shine.
This also funnily ties back into a Lovecraft quote, bringing everything full circle:

"That is not dead which can eternal lie, 
And with strange aeons even death may die."

Implying that, through all their efforts and attempts, Ina and the Wahtcher have been able to defy destiny, and even overwrite the very logic of the Ancient Ones with their own illogical monstrosity: Love.
Cherry Blossoms/Sakura

Cherry Blossoms, also known as sakura, are long celebrated flowers within Japan, tied to spring and the changing of seasons. Likewise, they are heavily associated with the concepts of Wabi-sabi and Mono no Aware.

Wabi sabi is the acceptance of transience and imperfection, appreciating the beauty in the imperfect, impermanent, and incomplete. Under wabi-sabi, the petals imply acceptance of their imperfections and flaws, loving one another as a whole, even the parts they are insecure about.

Mono no Aware is a similar idea, but focuses more on appreciating the fleeting nature of life, befitting the seasons of change. The concept is seen with a gentle, deep sadness, an understanding that all things come to pass. In the context of Abyssal Hymn, this could be seen in a more grave light, as if their souls have finally moved on. Or, it might be more focused on the idea of change, that even their darkest nights will come to pass.

Looking back in time at previous performances all before now, a mixture of the two meanings is most likely. Wabi-sabi resolves their longstanding desire to be more complete and whole, hinted at in the yearning in both her own songs and especially her past concerts and covers. Mono no Aware suggests a new dawn and a breaking of the spell that trapped them, preventing them from moving forward.

And finally, the Cherry Blossoms themselves, beyond just the concepts of Wabi-sabi and Mono-no-Aware, center around the transient nature of life as a whole. Throughout Abyssal Hymn, we get glimpses of changing seasons, which can connect all the way back to the hanafuda cards that inspired Temari, and Ina’s stated desire to “meet on a summer day” at Abyssal Hymn.
Combine these elements, and we get both the change and transient nature of the cherry blossom with the two finally breaking free from their cycle, attained by accepting their own flaws and growing.

Thus: Only by learning to love themselves and accepting the assistance/kindness of others are the two able to finally meet, their immature love finally blooming into something radiant, deep, and understanding, where they can fully support each other. No longer a fleeting smile and voice the other seeks out, but two fully realized halves who make a greater whole.

Transformed through love into a binary system that can outlast the end of the universe and reality itself, two blazing hearts beating even in the darkest abyss and vast silence, with the strength and will to bend the multiverse just to be by each others side. 
No cosmic horror or existential threat ever able to destroy an honest love that can both persevere and fight.
Past the end and beyond...
Always.

body.text: My past submission was "she became lonely", sorry, I haven't slept tonight. Here's my take on the timeline of the story, sorry that's it's not all that organized.

Past Ina happens (island, sacrifices, Temari, successful ritual, watatsumi summoned, island's population destroyed, Ina seals watatsumi with herself in a timeless void, thus becoming Wahtcher), small tako gets book to the surface and waits for a long time (it possibly sings takodachi no uta while waiting). After many years in the future Our Ina meets tako with the book, takes the book and thus makes contact with Wahtcher they probably spend time together and become friends, then contact is disrupted and the two become separated. Years pass, Wahtcher sings Violet and sends prayers in the form of jellyfish (like a message in a bottle),  Our Ina becomes older and continuously searches for Wahtcher, makes those tanabata wishes. One day Our Ina finally finds jellyfish "message" and it leads her to now drowned island, where she tries to rescue Wahtcher using jellyfish to conjure pen-weapon that can almost reach what appears to be Past Ina. Wahtcher continues to make jellyfish, and Our Ina continues trying to rescue her. Unfortunately every attempt fails. Notably, Our Ina haven't used the book in her attempts (maybe some kind of power unbalance between her and AO-chan), at some point she says INAFF, sings Meconopsis together with Wahtcher, manages to take control of the book, casts a spell to undo the seal, to summon/turn into Big Ina and overpower the released Watatsumi. Wahtcher and Our Ina are reunited. The end.

TakoTakover is what happens if Our Ina doesn't find jellyfish, and turns to darker AO-chan powers to do something about the missing Wahtcher situation. In the process she goes cuckoo and destroys the world.

I don't know what to do about Past Ina that isn't the Wahtcher. Why Wahtcher and Our Ina saved Past Ina at the end of Abyssal Hymn MV? Why Violet, Temari and Abyssal Hymn all have imagery of hands trying to reach each other? I'd assume that throughout Abyssal Hymn Wahtcher and Our Ina are working together to help Past Ina, so that ritual doesn't happen. In this scenario helping Wahtcher wasn't initially in the plans, maybe AO-chan guided them saying you can save Past Ina and withholding information about how to undo the seal. And so they were trying to brute force the issue, but then they say INAFF, Meconopsis happens, girls realize that Wahtcher needs to be saved first, and then when Wahtcher is saved they do time shenanigans to save Past Ina before the ritual happens. With that in mind, all the imagery of hand reaching out could be  premonitions of different attempts of Our Ina trying to save Past Ina.
I also don't understand those tanabata wish tablets. They have both english and japanese text. Did Wahtcher and Our Ina communicate using those at some point?

I also like the idea if takodachi no uta is sung by Wahtcher when she becomes lonely after her initial contact with Our Ina is disrupted. I like to imagine that when Our Ina makes contact with Wahtcher, Watcher is still a kid, and they just play around together a lot.
(TEMARI + Abyssal Hymn)
There are multiple candidates of the cult who must become sacrifices to the Ancient One, Watatsumi. Temari and her Imouto (most likely an “alternate version” of herself) are among them.
The Ancient One took hold of Imouto and trapped her within its grasp, because it knew Imouto had some special power/quality to her.
In order to save her Imouto, Temari brazenly takes hold of the Ancient One's power with the book, ascending into the Watcher.
She seals herself and Watatsumi beneath the sea, in R’lyeh, a place beyond time, at the edge of eternity.
While Imouto is also still trapped, frozen in time until someone can save her.
(Takodachi no Uta + Abyssal Hymn + Ina introduction lore)
A Takodachi, who has witnessed multiple time loops at the side of Ninomae Ina'nis sings to itself, yearning to see Ina again.
It holds the special book.

Sent by the Watcher to a distant timeline in the future, it meets the fated reincarnation of Imouto – Present Ina. Receiving the book from the Takodachi, Present Ina awakens from a normal girl to becoming a Priestess, in touch with her power of time, memories, and eternity.
(VIOLET)

After receiving the power of the Ancient Ones, Present Ina receives memories of her fragmented past lives. She sees the image of Imouto and Temari, and something in her heart feels wistful, yearning for something she doesn't know but feels deeply.
She senses the Watcher, even if it's faint.
(Takover)

In one timeline, Present Ina becomes corrupted by the book of the Ancient Ones, declaring herself the overlord and seeking world domination and mind control. She rewrites history with her authority. She becomes Takover.
She becomes one in the same with Watatsumi. She goes back in time to expand her cult, and start the cult that will be the beginning of Temari and Imouto’s story.
She is sealed away after the Watcher intervenes, but her power persists throughout the timelines as other Inas draw upon her, Watatsumi.

(Note: The plot point about “Takover becomes the same entity as Watatsumi” is not fully supported by evidence, mainly just the fact I think it'd be interesting if Takover/Watatsumi was also part of a timeloop situation and that all the entities in the re:VISION story are versions of Ina)
(Meconopsis)
In another timeline, Present Ina becomes Meconopsis. She loses most of her power as the world becomes destroyed, as well as all her friends. She becomes a “fallen angel.”
Holding on to one glimmer of hope, she uses a ritual to send her memories of love and conviction throughout the timelines.
(Abyssal Hymn)

In the main timeline, The Watcher calls out to Present Ina with a “temari” of memory, and she answers the call. She becomes Yuusha, and travels back in time to save Imouto – who is her past reincarnation.
Yuusha tries multiple times to save Imouto, resetting and failing, but she keeps trying.

The Watcher imparts upon Yuusha a spell/ritual to help her. Joined by her Takodachi, Yuusha prays to all the other timelines of Ina, invoking the greatest power of the Ancient Ones, and the power of Ina herself.
She becomes True Ina, the coalescence of all Ina timelines. In confronting Watatsumi, she defeats it and frees The Watcher from R'lyeh, breaking the barrier between time.
The Watcher and Yuusha (reincarnation of Imouto + now carries all memories of all Inas) reunite at long last.
Imouto is also freed from her prison, and reaches out to reunite with her “elder sister” (the Watcher) and to reach out to her “future” (Yuusha).
By being freed from the grasp of Watatsumi, she can now finally reincarnate…
As Present Ina.
Symbolically, Ina has:
- reconciled with her past
- healed her inner child
- conquered her darkness
- freed herself from her burdens
- accepted all versions of herself

body.text: The Tale of the Three Ninomae Children: The Watcher full of Love, The Faithful Child of the Angry God, and the Excommunicated Hero of Hope (in reference to the line in a snapshot in “Violet” – “And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is love).  In my analysis, Watcher and the Hero are twins forcefully separated by the Ninomae Cult. I am making that stance due to not only the two of them having the closest physical attributes, but also due to the fact that out of all the children, only two of them can see the Tako on the Necronomicon (with Temari “Ina” being truly friendly with one). I am assuming their separation due to the following: 1. Cults are oddly obsessed with “purity” and perfection in aesthetic and “desired attribute,”  2. twins were considered bad luck in multiple traditional superstitions and religions, and 3. the lines saying “It is time to tell myself…” and the way plenty of it being followed by allusions to “reincarnation” and connection leads me to believe that Hero Ina is referring to an “other self” or “my other half.  Following those lines of thought, it would make sense that one child is allowed to stay within the confines of the cult’s estate and the other can be seen wearing a school uniform, which is a clue that she is studying things that would be considered taboo in a cult setting.  As for the so called “Faithful Child of the Angry God,” she is younger sibling that Temari “Ina” talks about. She is also the one we see locked up with bandages in her hand desperately reaching for the Grimoire that appeared in front of her. Based off of the few frames going into the Abyssal Hymn MV, the shot where it shows her reaching hand and the face of Angry C’thulu behind it tells us that she has been praying for salvation from being the chosen sacrifice alongside the many other children in the estate. Her prayers, alongside the other vengeful children who perished with despair, were answered – or at least a version of it: the destruction of what brought them pain. At the end of the MV, she is also the youngest looking “Ina” look alike.

Watcher Ina, wracked with guilt as to how she contributed to all of this, sealed her possessed younger sibling that is carrying an innumerable angry souls alongside herself in a dimension underneath the sea and made it so that the world does not remember them – even our Ina.

Our Ina was far away from the tragedy that occurred. She may have tried to live a “normal life” due to not being involved with her clan, but all that changed when she came across the grimoire that washed ashore upon the sealing of the rest of her surviving family. She most likely tried to reject the call as well as per Tako Take Over where we see her attempting to pray the voices away. Of course she could no longer ignore it – there was both joy and sadness in her heart that she needed to reconcile. Even without fully remembering, she accepted the call but not succumbed to it.  As she put it, “Faith and dreams belong in the arms of love… Enough, I won’t pray endlessly. A world without love is not a world I want to see.”

The Temari – They embody the prayers and souls of the children. As they seem to not have been allowed much (not even footwear), the only thing that brought them joy is possibly the Temari lovingly given to them by our Watcher “Ina.” In relation to that, it is possibly why you can see them float about and released in the sea – as an offering to whomever can hear them. They are also the Temari spirits that summoned our Hero Ina to go to the sea and also helped her a great deal in finally setting her siblings free from their prison.
(I apologize for rambling – I also posted about it in length here. https://x.com/jayteamations/status/2101974725073457333?s=20
Thank you all and I hope you all have a WAHnderful morning afternoon evening)
