body.text: In the beginning there was 1 Ina (Temari) who was raised in a cult of the watasumi amongst other children. The children are used up one by one as the sacrifice to watatsumi. Interestingly enough, the girl in kimono at the beginning of Temari is probably not Ina but the previous vessel. Young Ina and her pet Takodachi watched all the other children dies and she sends out their temari as an SOS over the water but no help came. Eventually it was young Ina's turn to be sacrificed. While she was locked in the room, she communicated with the presence in the next room (maybe the watatsumi in the form of the previous vessel?) and her desperate plea was answered in the form of the necronomicon. In a bid for survival, she opened the book, fracturing her soul into 2 parts, one became the white haired girl seen in temari and eventually became the Wahtcher in Abyssal Hymn, the other lost to the cycle of reincarnation. Opening the book let loose the watatsumi upon this world. Upon realising what she has done, the white haired girl took the power of the book, performed ayatori magic and sealed herself and the watatsumi manifestation away in the depth of the lake content to watch her "sister" (literally other half) reincarnate and live a happy life while suffering alone for eternity to pay for their shared sin. The takodachi held on to the book and was swept away, spending its time waiting to meet Ina again (Takodachi no Uta). The second part of Ina eventually reincarnated into the world and found the takodachi and the necronomicon again. By opening the book, she slowly regains her memories of the past life and falls under the watatsumi's influence again. If this went unchecked she became Takover Ina and became the vessel for world domination. However by encountering Myth (Meconopsis), she is able to resist the watatsumi's influence and embarked on the journey as Yuusha Ina to save her desperate younger self and pay for the sin of letting the watatsumi into the world. However, while expecting to find herself trapped in the watatsumi's grasps in the depth of the lake, Yuusha Ina finds nothing (as Young Ina has split and Wahtcher has sealed herself and watatsumi away in her pocket dimension). After many desperate attempts, Yuusha Ina mastered Ayatori magic and is able to trace the watatsumi to the Wahtcher, who was responding to the strong feelings from Yuusha Ina (the temari-s blooming into lotuses). Drawing out the Wahtcher, Yuusha Ina who is strengthened by bonds of friendship (and presumably, support of modern takodachis worldwide) ascend into Ascendant Ina and sealed the weakened watatsumi into her kasa and finally reumited with Wahtcher (the longing is real). Together at last, they can now rescue that young little girl who was alone and desperate in the dark. I leaned into this theory because I felt from it a strong parallel with growing up, where you had to seal off part of yourself to survive, and eventually, once you've matured emotiinally and healed, you can find that sraled off part of yourself again and finally reassure that little you in the past that you are no longer alone and scared in the dark.

body.text: All the info revealed about the lore revealed in Abyssal Hymn's MV recontextualized every other MV that came before. The info in question:

1. The WAHcher is able to communicate with all the other Inas in every version of the timeline, whether through jellyfish or temaris (in fact, the walls from Beyond The Void shown in an April Fool's stream looked like the inside of a temari when brightened up, but we wouldn't know this until temari). In all likelihood, she transcended time itself.
2. The WAHcher was separated from her takodachi after throwing herself and the monster into the void, and it should be noted that said takodachi and the book were raised to above water.
3. Said tako later met an Ina that seemed untouched by the Ancient Ones up until that meeting.
4. There's a takodachi on Kid Ina's shoulder, but notably none of the other little girls have one. The implication was that a takofication had happened before the events of Temari.

5. The several Temari balls on the shore suggest there was a previous attempt to do the resurrection ritual established in Temari, which requires human sacrifices. It was also shown that they've been systematically putting little girls in cages and drowning them, and I suspect the idea was that one of them would be able to use the book, or if they failed they would be used as fodder for the resurrection ritual.

6. Time is frozen in the void. It's not outright stated, but Yuusha Ina did spend the second half of the MV trying to reach Kid Ina from Temari by going deep enough into the sea. Given that they are the same person, this should not have been possible, unless time was frozen there.

7. A bit of an inference; if time is frozen within the void, combined with it being accessible from every point in time in every timeline, thus meaning that being in the void, and by extension being a takodachi, is to experience eternity (well, more like experiencing every moment of your life and every possible variation of it in one singular moment all at once), and to do that is effectively to become ancient - an Ancient One.
8. And another inference, that there’s three levels. One’s the surface of the sea. Deeper is the void. Yet deeper is Beyond The Void.

9. Yuusha Ina defeated the big monster seen at the beginning after releasing it from their prison, the very same one the WAHcher sacrificed herself to seal, by treating it like any other takodachi (see the Ina with glasses extending a parasol to shield a much smaller one from the snow, the same thing she did to calm the monster down). And that's just it, that monster *is* a takodachi, and I think that was the result of a mass takofication of several people all at once ("A cage of vessels, creaking as they stack" spoken in japanese), twisting and bending them together specifically, the little girls they've been systematically drowning for the resurrection ritual, and there either might've been a previous attempt, as suggested by the takodachi on Kid Ina's shoulder and the 12 temaris at the beginning (dunno if it was a big sacrifice of 12 or two attempts with 6 sacrifices each, but I don't think that changes anything).

10. This is more of an aside, monsters don't normally have any reason to listen to humans, but this one did. My own guess would be that void itself is a living entity, and because to the Ancient Ones the whole thing with the umbrella was recent from their POV, all they remember is the girl who shielded them from the snow and prayed to them every day (Also from Temari's lyrics: "This path covered in the blood of many, bays out for love", thus suggesting that love is something The Ancient Ones desperately crave).
11. Another aside, I think that to become a takodachi is to become one with the void, I'll get on this later.
12. It was confirmed that Yuusha Ina went deep enough into the sea to reach Beyond The Void, which would've put her outside of time.

13. The WAHcher and Yuusha did eventually succeed in pulling Kid Ina out of the void, but their ultimate fates remained unknown. As it stands, all of them could've been flung out into any version of the timeline, but my own guess would be that this enabled Kid Ina to lead a mostly normal life until she meets the First Takodachi who happened to be around the purple book, and then grows up to become Yuusha Ina (and thus the timeline is stabilized).

14. Bit of trivia, but I don’t think it changes anything: Watatsumi - a sea dragon god, who was mentioned in the lyrics - had a legend (though I’m skipping a lot of details for the sake of brevity) where a visitor came to his palace, and when said visitor returned to the surface, several centuries had passed. In the MV itself, there was a dragon blending with the background during the scene where Ina extended a parasol to the monster that appeared at the beginning and the legend does look rather similar to how the void is implied to work.
Now I will be going over every piece of lore I had prior and how it changed, because of all of this:
Temari's MV:

1. AO-chan is the Necronomicon, a book known to bring the souls of the dead back to live as their undead slaves. (“the necronomicon --forbidden knowledge” Time stamp: 1:03 Visitor’s Script) And that's why it enables takofication - it takes the soul, casts it into the void, where it can forever be preserved in time, and then gives the void shape and form to interact with the world.

2. Several girls were told they would become the head of the house, but seemingly only one survived (and something "bloomed" in their heads and each of them lost their head when that happened, and I believe it was from trying to use the book, and therefore access knowledge humans were not meant to know at the time), and all of them were called Ninomae Ina'nis when they were informed of this (“Ninomae Inanis From Today Onwards You Shall Become The Head of This Family.” Timestamp: 0:01). And if this interpretation of the imagery holds, rather than getting killed by a ritual, it's likely that trying to utilize the book killed/drove insane each of them, except the only one who successfully brought someone back from the dead.

3. The cult was trying to resurrect someone (“the sealed island -- and a resurrection” Time stamp: 1:57). I used to think it was an original priestess that didn't exist, now I think they were trying to resurrect their god. But the spell doesn't resurrect anything, it just traps souls into the void (though it does enable them to live forever), and they did this to a bunch of little girls they made suffer, thus giving them the power to destroy the world, the one they've come to despise because all they have known is misery ("This whole world feels – Nothing but cursed").

4. There was a second Ina (“the second inanis ” time stamp: 0:40) who had a different destiny (“the second destiny -- another destiny ” time stamp: 0:43). After Abyssal Hymn's MV, I'm pretty sure the two Inas are The WAHcher, the second one is the one in the kimono we see at the beginning who would presumably become a different one - either TakoTakover or Meconopsis.

5. Ina was hearing voices from "Beyond the beginning and the end" and going “towards the beginning and the end” (A reference to Beyond The Void, which would be outside of time, though she said in the April Fool’s stream, and I quote “I told you there's just me and this frozen time. It's pretty empty here.”), and in particular an "unsaved voice" belonging to a sister she wants to see again was mentioned in the lyrics. She did say "if you're there", taking in that in Abyssal Hymn's MV Kid Ina did have a takodachi and that the cult thinks this is a resurrection ritual, she probably believed that too and brought her back as a takodachi.

6. It was said in the Visitor's Script (Time stamp: 2:15) that "across the divide stood another fated child" and "she was wracked with guilt and at last she made a new choice". After Abyssal Hymn's MV, it's pretty obvious it was the WAHcher, who feels guilty about the creation of the kaiju-takodachi, because before then, she proved it was possible by takofying her dead friend.

7. Another way to interpret it, would be that The First Takodachi was this other girl, who brought Kid Ina her book so that she could break out of her cage (or rather pull her out of her out of the void), and she did that because she realized Ina would become part of the monster, and the reason that was almost her fate, and the monster’s very appearance, happened because she came back from the dead as a takodachi (should be noted this idea is contingent on the cult not placing the book near Ina on purpose to goad her into using it to kickstart the ritual).

8. In Temari's MV the WAHcher came into the picture albeit in a very disjointed manner (Furthermore, “I shall descend now into the world of humankind to watch over you” circling Ina at time stamp: 1:53). Abyssal Hymn's MV made it clear that the older one and the younger one are the same one.

9. In hindsight, the parts of Temari's MV where the cage breaks apart and the black eye with the caption "The oldest and strongest emotion of mankind is fear. And the oldest and strongest kind of fear is fear of the unknown." opened, was when The WAHcher woke up both literally and figuratively ("Cracked dreams of white, turned to crimson. A tinted lullaby now gone")

10. There were two summoning circles, one with blood and another with threads. After Abyssal Hymn MV, I believe the first one created the Giant Kaiju Takodachi (blood), the second one was from when the WAHcher sealed it away. This gets referenced in Meconopsis.
11. Ninomae Ina'nis is less a name and more a title granted to the one not killed/driven insane by the book.

12. There were six temari balls, but we only saw five girls. And the one the girl who would become Ninomae Ina'nis happened to be holding was also the only one that got a duplicate, the implication being that there was an unseen sixth girl. We see this duplicate in the shots with the older "Ina" (actually the WAHcher). Abyssal Hymn's MV later confirmed not just her existence, but also previous attempts to use the resurrection ritual.

13. Without Abyssal Hymn’s context, I thought the MV was Ina reflecting on the past (and later I found myself questioning why she turned into the Wahcher despite that evidently having not happened yet), with its context I now think it was a vision sent to Ina from the Wahcher, letting her see how she became the Wahcher (also as an explanation as to why the mole was mirrored in some shots; because Ina was watching it happen, from the outside, rather than remembering it happening to her). Further supported by this part of the Visitor’s Script at time stamp (0:11): “Can you hear my voice?--Witchcraft ”
Violet's MV:

1. Ina reminisced about a friend she missed enough that it felt like time stopped for her. Abyssal Hymn's MV showed this was not a metaphor: In Violet's MV, Ina was submerged (but not drowning), praying and glowing/powering up (the glow being like that of the moon). In Abyssal Hymn's MV, Yuusha Ina spent the second half of the MV trying to reach out to Kid Ina (from Temari's MV), who seemingly had been imprisoned in what I think is the void. Which just so happens to be underwater. And Violet Ina had been praying endlessly and every time she did it she was submerged. There is one difference however, Violet Ina reached the void by praying, Yuusha did it by going deep under the sea. The main point of evidence for both these instances being on the same location was that Violet's lyrics were talking about time being frozen, and Kid Ina was reached out to by Yuusha Ina and The WAHcher at the end, something that shouldn't be possible unless time froze there.

2. There is one other implication, if all it took to reach the void and harness its power is praying, and if time is frozen there, then it means that the power she gets from the void is cumulative - that is to say even if Ina stopped praying, the moment became frozen into the void, the power she obtained is now with every version of her.

3. If takofication is ultimately a way to preserve a person's soul (killing their mortal body in the process) by way of throwing it into the void with all the others, then her prayers in Violet MV were all an attempt to reach them again. And likely she did, and that became the tako on her shoulder when she was a kid.
4. Speaking of which, this also means praying lets her telepathically speak to every tako, everywhere in every timeline, by virtue of directly casting her voice into the void.

5. Given that the WAHcher did get separated from her takodachi, and given Violet Ina's motives, it seemingly looks like Violet Ina (who glows like the moon when she prays) is the WAHcher (from Temari: “Heading towards the beginning and the end. Beyond which I only hear your unsaved voice. Oh, my dear little sister, tell me if you're there. I wonder if I can hold your hand again someday “). Furthermore, around the time Temari released Ina pointed in a tweet that Tako Lane was suspiciously round, which was explored in VR in a stream, and it was shown to have an entrance to Beyond The Void, which is where we first met the WAHcher in an April Fools stream. However, I also have reason to think Violet Ina is not actually Ina, but rather the first takodachi as they are within the void, and speaking of which.

Takodachi No Uta: I think this song was from when Kid Ina (before becoming the WAHcher) successfully did the first takofication just to prevent her friend from dying to the cult's activities, but lamented that her friend is gone, and she can only ever see them in the void. Alternatively, and in light of the fact that the First Takodachi was separated from the WAHcher with the book in tow, the singer might be the First Tako, who is lamenting they can only see their beloved friend by using the book.

But this presents a problem: Which one of them is the singer? Which of them is/became Violet Ina? And is there any reason it can’t be both of them? In order to resolve this we must look into certain lyrics across all the songs in Re:Vision, the wooden plaques in the wish wall in Abyssal Hymn, and the April Fool's stream.

Something that kept being repeated in Takodachi No Uta was “またね”, which means “see you later” or “hope we see again later”. This was also one of the wooden plaques in the wish wall seen in Abyssal Hymn, alongside with “How can I find you?”, “I really, really miss you!” And in japanese “I want to see you! Really…”. The only two people who could’ve written any of those would be Kimono Ina and The First Takodachi. Later, in the MV when Yuusha/Kimono Ina broken into Beyond The Void and reached the Wahcher, the “またね” plaque flew off, (along with “My heart already knows your name”, “Until we meet” and a few several others) thus implication becomes that those plaques, and by extension Takodachi No Uta, was directed at the Wahcher. Further supporting this, the singer of Takodachi No Uta has access to the book, which narrows it down to Kimono Ina (who doesn’t know who the Wahcher is) and The First Takodachi (who does know who she is).

This clears up who sings Takodachi No Uta - the First Takodachi, instead of the Wahcher. But that brings us back to the other two questions: Which of them is Violet Ina? And why can’t it be both of them singing?
Next is the April Fool’s stream. Here are some transcripts of the April Fool’s stream I took the liberty of making:
“The Ancient Ones… Hm, they have no place here. Don’t worry, I’m much better than AO-chan, I think. Probably.”
"I just make sure that the one you call Ina can happily live where she is, so the world doesn't end."
"Nah, I just watch over stuff, basically. Yes, I witness. But without me here, her world might end."
"So, you know, I get bored. But I stay here, as always."
"It does get a little lonely around here, just me after all. I thought, I just, uh, invite you guys."
"It doesn't happen every day where I can invite you guys. I did have to borrow the Ancient Ones' powers a little bit."
"I told you there's just me and this frozen time. It's pretty empty here."
"I may not look like it, but I got powers too, uh, should I say, keep the world in check. I don't know how else to put this."
"What magic, I wouldn't really say magic, but Ina's world as is... you could say I basically created that. I think"
"Oh don't worry, you won't remember anything once you get out of here"
"I can't really be there, physically. But I can, um... influence things. That's the closest way to put it."

Throughout the entire segment; The WAHcher kept calling Ina "the one you call Ina", almost as if confused about that being her name, and given revelation from Abyssal Hymn's MV (specifically, The WAHcher is the earliest Ina’nis), this would suggest that she's forgotten who she is/used to be, and implies that being in the void or Beyond The Void for an extended period of time slowly erases the memory of those who are in there (further supporting this: Violet's illustrations showed the friend to be rather nondescript, and in Temari despite said friend being part of the backstory, was completely absent from the group of little girls, and the First Takodachi from Abyssal Hymn’s MV is not present either, and at the end of the stream itself she did say us the viewers - the takodachis - wouldn’t remember anything).

We also learned that The Ancient Ones are not present in Beyond The Void. If the implications I inferred from how time in Void is frozen affects things holds, specifically that being in the void means experiencing every single thing that was thrown in there all at once, effectively becoming an ancient one, then the First Takodachi cannot follow her or rather cannot stay there, and notably the monster takodachi from the beginning of Abyssal Hymn, is not present. Thus Takodachi No Uta cannot be sung by the same person.

It presents a major difference between the Void and Beyond The Void - Still having access to all of that was frozen in there, but being able to influence what you see by way of messages and visions. It also places a layer of tragedy: Neither the Wahcher or The First Tako can recognize one another.

That brings us to the last question: Which of them is Violet Ina? Across the songs of Re:Vision there's lines referencing sleeping and waking up, Violet being the only notable exception. Here’s all of them:
"Misty whispers that calls, drown in endless dreams." (Meconopsis, in english)
"The Ancient Ones dream as they wait in R'lyeh." (Meconopsis, in japanese)
"Faith and dreams, belong in the arms of love." (Meconopsis, in english )
"Ah, as I fall and fade out. My name and a spell rings out. It resonates with my hollow body. And dreaming eyes open again" (Temari. Song is fully in japanese)

"I open a book here. On a night when I can't sleep, I call you. The surface of the water is swaying (yurari). Stars are spilling (parala)Forever. I will pray for you. I will pray here" (Takodachi No Uta unofficial translation. The song is also fully in japanese)
"If it's a dream, stay awake..." (Takodachi No Uta unofficial translation)
"Before I knew it, I was asleep. I'm lonely. Hey again, I want to see you " (Takodachi No Uta unofficial translation)
"Watatsumi sleeping in a misty dream. A Cage of Vessels, creaking as they stack. Cracked dreams of white, turned to crimson. A tinted lullaby now gone" (Abyssal Hymn, in japanese)
"My sin asleep in the hollow of time. A lonely lullaby's melody. Hold me" (Abyssal Hymn, in japanese)
"Watatsumi sleeping in a misty dream. Misty dreams hold a prophecy of truth" (Abyssal Hymn, in english)
"Sleepy eyes to fight your fears. (Like... a world without Ina!!!)" (TakoTakover, another song fully in japanese)

Collectively, they all point that being inside the void is to be in a dream, and to go there is to reunite with a loved one or dream about being with them. If time in the void is frozen, this would mean that those moments are frozen too, and so are the words that are cast upon it, and the end result would be like hearing a billion voices talking to you at the same time (Fittingly, Violet Ina has been praying endlessly, “My silent voice calls out your name longingly. To return luster to my faded paints. With my voice hoarse and long ran dry. Your fleeting words. Are all I know.”). Thus an overwhelming feeling of yearning would exist within the void, and all who are in it will feel as if it was their own, becoming one with it, or so to speak; “the path covered in blood that bays out for love”.

And that explains why Violet is the exception: Violet Ina was submerged in a dream otherwise known as the void for the entire MV (which puts her outside of Beyond The Void), and once in it her prayers *cannot* cease. And that would eliminate the Wahcher as a possible identity of Violet Ina, leaving The First Takodachi as the only possibility left.
If Violet Ina and The First Takodachi are one and the same:

1. If Ninomae Ina’nis is a title, there was a second Ina’nis, and their memories are getting erased, and eventually the wish/desire will erode from “I wish to see my friend again” to “I wish to see Ninomae Ina’nis again” and both Violet Ina and Wahcher will think this.

2. The void doesn’t just contain the soul of the first takodachi, but that of several little girls, however Violet Ina prayed so hard and so much that her yearning affected every other soul trapped in it, hence why the monster takodachi listened to her at all.

3. Also the implication that the first tako doesn’t just have the soul of those little girls, it also has the soul of the unsaved voice - Violet Ina. And because the smaller tako she was inhabiting predated the monster, it let her interact with Wahcher without attacking her.

4. If this second Ina’nis is the one referenced in “across the divide stood another fated child -- she was wracked with guilt and at last she made a new choice”, then “My sin asleep in the hollow of time. A lonely lullaby's melody. Hold me” would read that the other fated child who was wracked with guilt is Wahcher, and she feels guilty for the sacrifices made, among them her friend, and for failing to save her from being turned into a monster.

5. A hypothesis: Wahcher tasked Yuusha Ina with the mission to free the souls used to create the takodachi monster, including Kid Ina, who is at the center of said monster, and is Yuusha Ina, or rather could’ve become her if not for the cults machinations.

6. If this is true, then it would explain what happened after the three of them got reunited - they let Kid Ina lead a normal life, then she met the first tako who was spat into her timeline and found the book, thus stabilizing the timeline.

7. Another hypothesis, in Temari and Violet there was a shot of a kid pushing another, and one of them is Kid Ina from the Temari, but we never see the face of the other. The hypothesis is that that shot was Violet Ina pushing Wahcher out of the void, and just in time for Wahcher to seal the monster takodachi away.

This brings us to the two possible endings of the story (well, there's actually a third, and we see it in Abyssal Hymn's MV, though the song itself was indicated by Ina to be the climax but not the ending itself), Meconopsis and Takotakover:
The Meconopsis ending:
1. Initially, I interpreted the songs to be that Ina turned against the Ancient Ones. There was a particular pose in the illustrations showing Ina with a Cat's Cradle and a melting halo.

2. The Cat's Cradle was said to represent her to be in a bind in the after party. I took that to mean that her hands are tied by her own choice. In Abyssal Hymn MV, whenever we saw strings attached to Ina's/WAHcher's fingers, they were either sealing/unsealing the Kaiju-sized Takodachi, or they were communicating with each other (see the shot of both of their pinkies while seeing a reflection of each other). The implication was that the WAHcher was overseeing this, and likely speaking through Ina.

3. Speaking of which, "An oath of blood. An oath of love." was spoken in japanese, which I've come to associate with Kid Ina, Takodachis and the WAHcher. On the face of it, it sounds like the WAHcher made an oath, less obviously it references her responsibility both for creating the kaiju takodachi and for sealing them away (and partially their eventual unsealing by Yuusha Ina but facilitated by her).

4. Symbolically speaking, blood would be the sacrifices made to empower the priestess, love is more about the connections, or the threads, like the ones used to make the temaris or the jellyfishes used to communicate with the other Inas across time and space.

5. The melting halo, I believed to represent that AO's powers are trying to leave her but failing to do so. Further supporting this, was that she said she will not pray endlessly, and because of Abyssal Hymn's MV I read that now as a rejection of void, and if it's true that every time she prays, the moment in question gets frozen inside the void, that would explain why her power wouldn't leave her - the void and by extension the takodachis do not want to separate from her.

6. Meconopsis Ina's reason for turning against the Ancient Ones was because she saw them as liars who were creating "a world without love". After Abyssal Hymn's MV, I feel that description fits the cult better than the Ancient Ones (cults never tell those they try to recruit the whole deal). On top of that while Ina did (or tried to) reject the Ancient Ones, she (and the WAHcher) was more angry at the cult than the Ancient Ones.

7. About lines spoken in japanese: "The Ancient Ones dream as they wait in R'lyeh" and "And their hearts, they see through all the lies you tell", and if this is The WAHcher speaking, and if being in the void/being takofied is to experience eternity, it would indicate the souls who've been thrown into the void, and by extension the void itself, are just as angry as she is. She was also insisting this was the last chance to save everyone ("Now is the time to save everyone, it's the final chance").

8. As for the lines spoken in English like "Is my sanity clinging from my mem'ry", "Is humanity a long forgotten friend?" and "How do I reconcile the joy in my memory?", made it all but seem that Meconopsis Ina has gaps in her memory, especially about the friend who disappeared, has largely been disconnected from humanity and wants to rectify that. I think the only way this would've happened is if Meconopsis Ina had spent an eternity time-frozen inside the void.

9. Here’s my hypothesis about what I think made Meconopsis happen: Yuusha Ina died trying to save Kid Ina (also caused Takotakover, more on that in a moment), thus leaving Kid Ina inside the void for a very long time, during which her memory of her friend - The Wahcher - eroded until she forgot her name at one point wasn’t Ninomae Ina’nis and later eroded further, until she stopped thinking of her friend and instead started to think humanity as a whole. Then in each attempt Yuusha tried to save her, Kid Ina mistook her potential future self for her friend and believed she managed to reach her through prayer, so after becoming Violet Ina/First Takodachi, she stopped seeing Yuusha despite her prayers when she died and with it, her reason to pray endlessly. The void couldn’t stand the idea of any Ina’nis dying, so it got angry at the cult, and let Violet Ina overtake the void, reverse her takofication (Meconopsis Ina was at least able to control it, as indicated by the Cat’s Cradle, which we also saw both Wahcher and Yuusha Ina have string attached to their finger, and notably was also symbolic of their ability to communicate), and then use its powers to attack the cult, completely unaware her friend didn’t die and in fact was with her the entire time, but couldn’t recognize her either.
10. This is contingent on there being multiple Inas inside the void as a result from repeated access to the void through prayer and its property of having time frozen.

11. An aside, "Though death may die, Love is now and for forever", I think is a reference to what takofication does, that is preserving someone for eternity, but it also puts in the nuance that the love Ina has been showing the void (and by extension her takodachis) is also going to last for eternity. Also, "When death, rebirth, time and oceans align, Eternity's hope will power through." I suspect it to be related to takofication too.
The Takotakover ending (as stated in its afterparty to be "an ending, but not the true ending"):

1. Ina was trying to erase something that upset her from history, enforcing a fake happiness on the pain of death if necessary, and to do this she takofied people under the pretense of helping them reach their full potential. There was a lot of imagery invoking "infection", not unlike the paradoxum infection you see in snails. This however presented the Ancient Ones influence as an infection.

2. Meconopsis Ina turned against the cult over their lies (that one was more The WAHcher's grievance though), and because she didn't want to see "a world without love", but here she was enforcing a fake happiness - said world without love - and lying constantly about being normal girl, or that her motives is to "help humanity reach their full potential". This implies she was being possessed or had otherwise been brainwashed, and unlike Meconopsis; I don't think the WAHcher was co-fronting with her.

3. Strangely enough, the takodachis spoke solely in japanese and it was usually about takofication, and protecting the timeline ("To protect my Ina timeline, I'll become an octopus"). And notably, it was mentioned "A world without Ina" when talking about their sleepy eyes to protect from fears (The First Takodachi does not have sleepy eyes though).
